This is a hard one.  I like trains, I like train simulators (OpenBVE being by far the best and is free) but Train Simulator 2014 (2012 when I bought it) is so...lacklustre.
Don't get me wrong, the visual detail ranges from adequate (ground textures, houses, cars) to impressively realised (stations, viaducts, overall scenery) however it is in how you drive the train which is very uninteractive.  I draw comparisons to OpenBVE because everything has a button and each diesel/electric train has throttle *positions* rather than a throttle that cannot be set to go at a certain percentage (and goes through the power level percentages extremely smoothly), the sounds recorded by amateurs for OpenBVE have the realism that Train Simuator lacks (trains sound like they are idling, even when the throttle is at 100% and going up a gradient) and if you care about the little details (such as replying to the guard's buzzer) then you're going to notice their conspicuous absence.
For the most part you will be sat there doing nothing, whereas in OpenBVE you would be constantly adjusting throttle and braking to ensure best possible speed, time and passenger comfort (should you be doing a passenger run) or taking into account how the freight changes the handling.  This is the kind of pressure that's present in Euro Truck Simulator (which is disappointing on a different level, but not in terms of the actual driving of the trucks) but not here in Train Simulator 2014.
I even bought the Settle-Carlisle pack during the sale, just to see if the experience would be any different to those included as standard.  The answer, rather resoundingly, is no as the trains still sound awful (the horns may as well be weak synth or foleyed car horns, the steam engine noises are equally weak), the amount of interactivity is negligible and when there is pressure on the more difficult routes? Be prepared for awful controls and trains that need to go to their virtual depot for either scrapping or rebuilding from scratch as they are that poor in terms of performance.
I would have loved to have said that Train Simulator was - at least - good.  But it isn't.  Until Train Simulator receives a thorough reworking, it is best that you avoid this and either go buy a train set; play OpenBVE/Transport Tycoon or volunteer at your local heritage railway.  You'll save a lot of money (especially where all the DLC combined costs over £1000 prior to a Steam sale) and you'll have a far more enriching experience.
I will definitely recommend this game to SMRT, family and friends.

Really solid doujin shmup that's a great purchase for anyone who's a fan of the genre.
RefRain does a great job of distinguishing itself in a genre of very similar titles by mechanically focusing on offense heavy gameplay and scoring rather than pure dodging. There is still much dodging to be done as is standard in the genre, however you have a very large, bullet destroying attack that charges very quickly when you deal damage. As well, your bombs charge based on point pickups encouraging players to explore scoring even when playing for survival. The game features three characters which all provide very different play styles to stay interesting. There are also a large number of difficulty modes to keep the game challenging to both newcomers and STG veterans.
The scoring system present in Refrain is incredibly deep. In simple terms, the distance you are from an enemy determines the value of point items dropped, the closer the better. Further, your bombs turn all bullets on screen into shootable objects which give points and charge your special attack. Using your special attack on bosses makes them drop point items upon being damaged for a short time. What this means is that the special attack effectively charges your bomb, and your bombs effectively charge your special attack. Effective use of this mechanic allows players to chain the two attacks to rapidly defeat bosses. Doing so will earn a skip bonus upon defeating the boss. There is far more to the system however the general idea of scoring is captured with these two mechanics. An extensive manual is provided with the game for players who want to go deep into scoring.
Presentation wise the game is top notch. Visuals are crisp and clear, and the soundtrack is truly amazing. There are a lot of nice little touches as well, from the swooping designs of the bullet patterns, to how each character has a different start menu to fit their personality. RefRain is one of the strongest in the genre with how it presents itself.
I really hope that Degica brings out more like this. While I love the Cave titles they're bringing to Steam, there's something really special about seeing strange doujin titles get a chance to shine. I highly recommend this game to anyone interested in the genre.

I like hard bosses as much as the next shmupper, but this game's special attack and bullet cancelling system intrigued me.

Easy mode is truly easy, and with advanced and expert still waiting for me I am expecting great challenge ahead.

In most games that would be an issue but due to how quickly this game feeds you your special weapon you can actually due this on command with good play.
The soundtrack is really good and there is kind of a story that happens through emails and the menus outside of the gameplay. This game is one of the cooler obscure shmups on steam and one of the most fun ones I've played in a while.

What started off as a simple demo in 2006, evolved into the full game you see today in 2011, RefRain -prism memories- is a STG/Shump that's both classic formula, but also a bit wild, giving it a nice little niche in an already niche grouping.
The storyline itself isn't too grand in it's aprotch, as you 'Dive' with one of three girls all stuck within the M.R.S. network, trying to recovery their memorys, pasts, and just escape outright. Told via E-mails and endings, it presents itself in a way only the .Hack games ever really played around with, and because of how each player has their own 'Desktop' and the like, it really does give the game this really cool aesthetic.
The gameplay itself is the real core though, and it does this extrmely well with 3 core fuctions. The first is the 'Reactor Unit', where by killing foes, they drop chips that when collected both give you score, and fills up your 'bomb' for this game, and able to hold three of them that when used, turns all of the bullets into descrutable chips giving you more score in turn. Chips also end up larger, and worth a lot more points, the closer towards something you are when you KO them, making the game reward a very 'gutsy' gameplay style. The next comes by with the M.E.F.A2, a 'super attack' of sorts that you can charge up to 6 levels, and expend up towards 4 at once to delever highly powerful screen clearing attacks. The M.E.F.A2 does more then screen clear though, as on any Boss, it will 'lock' them, allowing you to build up a 'chain' with your shots, and if they die in this 'lock', your 'chain' then gives you an even BIGGER bonus towards their death! The last one is a simple but nice touch towards how lifes work. Your ship, for once, isn't a 'one point wonder', and can take 2 hits before destruction, but in turn, taking the first hit will put you into a 'fractured' status. While your damage and options haven't been hampered in any way, your score on the other hand is reduced by a large amount while under this mode for any life, giving the game an easy way to 'play for 1CC', but still requires a lot of skill for high scores!
Overall, this game as an STG fan is goingg to scratch that itch in a lot of good ways, as you can jump in and learn it easy enough, but it's got enough mecanics and subtule details that will require repeated playing to develop the best route and stratergys to get onto the leaderboards. If you enjoy STGs/Shmups of any kind, I HIGHLY recommend this, even more so now that it's in English, and is in a far easier to support format!

I've played this game's demo for 7 years. I went back to Japan for several times, looked around Akihabara to see if this game is still out there. No luck.
Jump to 2016, now it's on Steam. A dream com true.
Am I over reacting? no. This game is possibly my #1 favorite  shmup out there. I wouldn't wait for 7 years trying to get the game.
While the game seems like bullet hell,
The devs also mention this too, (in japanese) that the game was never meant to focus on dodging, rather, breaking the enemy's bullet. You see, other than the boss fight, the bullet is not patterned. In fact, some curtain of bullets are purposely unavoidable. That's when you use "M.E.F.A.2", which is a special weapon that breaks enemy's bullet, and this recharges very fast. The bomb in this game, or called "concept reactor", is more of traditional bomb, but used in different way. It converts the enemy's bullet into a breakable item that recharges the M.E.F.A2. So, the game WANTS you to break enemy's bullet, not dodging them all of the time. Of course, you can do so, but I would assume that you won't raise your score that way.
The game also offers 2 unlockable characters, total of 3.
Miria, traditional straight shot+laser with chaser options
Tee, narrow shot+close range focus shot with lock type option,
Mews, wide shot with angle type option.
The game also offers several difficulties. The easy mode offers 4 stages, and the rest offers full 5 stages. The game also has NG+ stages.
I won't spoil anything here, but the story progresses as you play the game by unlocking the email's archive. Since they unlocks depends on how well you play, there is a good replayability here, not just as a scoring.
Each character has its own ending, and has 1 common bad ending.
Yes, it's bit outdated. A little blurry too, since it is only optimized for 3:4 size. You can put it to full screen though.
However, as this game developed back in 2006, you really can't blame this factor. It is only a localized version anyway, not a HD remake or anything.
Overall, the background is simple 3d and not overly complicated, resembling the cyber theme just like the storyline. The bullet is very bright and easy to see. The light sparkle everywhere and great as an eye candy.
The menu UI is also different from many shmups. Instead you "toss coin" and "select your battleship", you choose your character, and it jumps to what it seems like a desktop screen. Each character has its own theme and soundtrack. You can access the email archives and soundtrack from here.
OST is fantastic, especially if you like trancy dance music. It also has nice variety in genre too, like drum'n bass. I wish, however, the sound effect of the main shots were little bit quiter. It is quite high pitched and botheres  me. The explosion sounds are great though.
The soundtrack can be listened from the menu.
Now, this is something that you need to bite on. It is a doujin game, and setting is somewhat limited. Unless you play with game pad, the keyboard control cannot be changed. Beautiful game with amazing focus on details
: 4/5
Very fun gameplay with some neat features. For the most part, the story and the gameplay are separated, allowing for a more seamless shoot 'em up experience.
Each character has their own playstyle and bomb patterns, which allows players to experience very different methods of beating the game.
In addition to killing a boss, bosses can be waited out, allowing players to play very defensively and still win.
This game has many differences from most shoot 'em ups. Your bomb specials are not limited and you have many escape options. You have a defensive special ability to negate bullets that charges up by collecting items, which drop such as by killing enemies or by using your bomb type special.  Your bomb type special charges by doing damage, including to negated bullets, which can also be used to charge up your defensive special. This allows for chaining the two abilities in order to make a powerful series of attacks that not only act as defense, but double as offense.
Bosses can and should be stunned. This uses up at least three points of your bomb special, but with careful comboing, can allow players to effectively one shot a boss. The game even rewards you for fast kills and skipping boss phases, which somewhat mitigates the need to milk a boss for points.
Some minor differences include that attacks that are coming have rather precise visual warnings, allowing players to avoid attacks that would otherwise be sneaky. This is different from other games that may only show the direction the attack would come from.
: 3.5/5
The story is told through log files, which are unlocked by playing through the game as each character. Each character has their own personality and their own reasons for trying to fight and the logs reveal these only after you are done playing through. Yet, these log files also provide hints as to how to fight various bosses.
In the end, the story is bittersweet, and while much of it needs to be pieced together, the player can see a tale where everyone has their own reasons for their actions, even the enemies.
: 4/5
The graphics are generally rather simple when in combat, but this leads for a more enjoyable gameplay rather than detracting from it. While some of the bosses may look similar as far as combat goes, each has a few different characteristics. The images of the characters are each designed to have their own distinct appearances.
The ships, the UI, and the bomb patterns are each designed for the character. Switching from one character to another, will result in a completely different main menu, and in-combat, the UI is colored to match the character. This matches with the theme of the game being part of a computer based system, with each character having their own log in desktop.
An interesting part of the combat UI is that if one looks careful, they can see a log of every action of the characters. The boss fights all have a health bar in a location by one of the logs, making it very simple for the player to understand what is occurring.
As far as audio goes, the soundtrack is very carefully designed for the game and a neat feature is that certain characters have the ability to see the artist notes about how each song was designed and what thoughts each song was meant to convey. The game of course has a sound room for each character which is more or less customized for each character, giving the player more than one music player option.
: 2.5/5
One full loop of the game should take around half an hour to over an hour. However, there are three characters and each has their own good ending, so while a single loop might get you through the game, it will likely take four loops to truly experience the game, giving the player easily four hours of playtime if the player never has to retry.
The replayability after beating the game completely will differ from person to person, but for players aiming for high scores and achievements, this game can easily take several weeks to perfect for an average player.
: 4/5
This game is definitely enjoyable and worth getting. With a much different approach at telling a story than most shoot 'em ups and many mechanics that are rarely seen together, if at all, this game provides a fun experience.

Grind simulator...
My god the grinding. If you want any half decent weapons prepare to spend hours upon hours trying to get it, and then even longer just to get the attachments you want. I got so sick of it I just forked up £20 and bought the stuff I wanted, once I did that I had a pretty fun time with this. Despite the horrendously abusable spawning system, even though you get a few seconds of invisibilty as infantry, you end up being spawned out in the open, where you will be blasted by a tank or sniped from god knows where. Vehicles however, have no spawn protection whatsoever, and their spawn point varies to about 2 places if you're lucky, allowing for a single enemy player to drive to your spawn with an ammo crate on his jeep, and camp you out till the cows come home, lack of voice chat means that warning any tankers of impending infantry attacks takes forever, by which time they've been killed, respawned and been killed again. If you can get past the grind fest and the heavy spawncamping the game is quite fun, however you probably won't notice it because you'll be either so tired from grinding you forget what fun is, or you'll be bleeding out of every orifice with fury at being spawn camped for the 900th time.
POST RELEASE EDIT
Christ alone knows what the devs were thinking when they decided it was a good time to release, I get that the game had been in beta for a long time but it seems there was zero preperation on their part for the influx of players releasing the game would cause. Since release it's rare to find a match that isn't lagging and desynced to all hell, with the familiar message of "Network is trying to catch up" appearing a minimum of 40 times a game. The new spawn system solved the spawn issues for all of 2 matches, then everyone figured out where the spawn points were and just camps the exits of these areas. Even worse it's fostered a tactic of getting a rifle and just hiding within your own spawn zone near an objective, since enemy players can't use weapons within your spawn area, you can give yourself a nice safe area in which you are basically untouchable. The good things to come out of the last update was the increased size of capture zones and fleshing out the maps with some much needed cover, you can now move across the airfield without being visible to everyone and his dog, and the fleshed out capture points make fighting around them much more interesting, instead of the previous camping 2 doorways until the point is taken or a lucky grenade toss kills you. All in all though, grind reduction taken in to account, still horrendously grindy and not even close to ready for a release.

I understand the concept of “free to play” games.
Naturally the companies want to obtain profit and will implement secondary features that will tempt you into paying (character customization, cuter weapons and gear even with better stats, etc.).
This game, however, is in a whole different level.
No secondary features here, you have to pay for literally everything that is decent:
-Inventory size (something that doesn’t fill up in 1 minute of playing)
-Gear that doesn’t make you look like every other free player
-Extra character slots, beyond the whopping 2 you get free
-Access to main features, without which you’ll just be a clown flying around pointlessly
-Even loot you constantly get everywhere that only opens if you pay up
-In summary, every attractive aspect of the game, pay up or no-can-do
And you might think “I might pay up if I’m interested”.
Not when you see the price…OMG…
What in the world possesses these people to ask such amounts of money for 12 months of premium access, amounts you can easily use to buy 2 other good recent games (no I’m not joking).
If you still want to try sure, it its “free”, enjoy the 3-5 days you will be able to endure it.

I got this game for $1.99 on a sale so I can't complain too much. I have played this on console a bit and was quite excited to see the PC version at such a heavy discount. Regardless, I can't reccomend this to anyone, whether it's on sale or not.
Cons:
1. Windows Live - It makes you create a Windows Live account before playing. You do have the option to play offline, but multiplayer is impossible this way.
2. Lag - This may not effect everyone, but people with mid to low end PCs should be wary. Even after setting the graphics and resolution as low as it can be, I would still never get over 15 fps, much less when destroying something.
3. Graphical Issues - Immediately upon starting the game, my character's coat began flying around like crazy and eventually just gave up and dissappear. After getting a kick out of that, I walked around the first level and everything began blinking in and out of existence. "See that tower? No you don-- Oh, there it is! Wait nevermind..." This would happen with everything from structures to weapons, to my body (oddly enough however, not my clothes)
4. Other Glitches - I had a controller plugged in and initially could not move my body, only my camera, with either my keyboard or controller. I researched this problem online and apparently it is quite common, although no one had a fix. I ended up exiting and unplugging my controller and surprise, surprise, I began to move.
Pros:
1. Destructible Environment - Breaking everything was quite satisfying, even though I sensed my GPU was ready to burst into flames when ever something would fall down.
2. Good Physics - Self explanatory.
Final Conclusion:
If you have a PC gifted to you from the gods, and want to break some virtual buildings with a sledgehammer, buy this game. If either one of those things does not apply to you, stay away from this game.

While I do run a below bottom end computer, the game initially lived up all my hopes and dreams despite the horrific framerate (which after disabling TSX and dropping many other graphical settings usually hovers between 14-15, occasionally going higher to 24 or more, which is good enough for me). Though I quickly lost interest in route building after realizing how time consuming it was.
Well my opinion of the game has been changing since then and I feel like I also need to share what I think of the game noow and add to the growing list of negative reviews despite this being my first review ever and my sloppy writing style.
While I don't hate the game, I've become disappointed to the point I no longer recommend it to anyone or scramble for the DLC.
One of my biggest issues isn't the pricing (not saying I don't have issues about it), it's the quality. The routes tend to be very good in my opinion despite the lack of TSX and reduced density in my case, but the same isn't as true with the locomotives and that was the first thing that made me start thinking "Is this really the game I wanted for over two years?"
While driving around on Sherman Hill I noticed the sounds, specifically the horns, weren't consistent enough. One locomotive would have a loud horn, but another may have a horn that was dramatically lower in volume. Vastly different bell sounds and quality also disappointing, like the Challenger having such a bell that sounds much too high pitched.
Lights are another common disappointment. The variation in all the different styles quickly becomes an eyesore when you start mixing and matching units. Especially with the new headlight glare from the upgraded locomotives (though it does look awesome). The Cab Forward takes the lighting issue to another level with not even having the textures for one of the marker lamps in the correct locations.
The best example of lack of quality in my mind is the A4 pack. While the driving programming is decent, the unrealistically quiet whistles kills much of the fun of driving them. Then there's Dominion of Canada. I was highly disappointed that not only did the sound not match the whistle's appearance, but also the bell didn't function (though I recognize that bells aren't usually needed in the UK).
Graphics and sound aside, you then come to functionality. While all the basic functions are simulated, how well they are simulated varies. The brakes aren't realistic across all locomotives (though the Marias units are well simulated with their dynamic braking). I'm told that independent brakes are the best for stopping locomotives running light, but I have yet to see independent braking make a difference at all, in fact I wrecked on my first scenario because of it. Then there's throttle operation on some diesel locomotives where the amps instantly jump to one point and the rpms slowly catch up, I would only find this realistic when reducing power not increasing power. I've discovered that the operation of certain features aren't consistent inside and outside of the locomotive, such as the case of the road locomotive included with Marias Pass where all wipers are moving outside the locomotive, but one of the wipers isn't moving on the inside.
My latest disappointment is also my biggest, how Railsimulator treats its community, trying to keep the bugs in the dark to the point where reviews are targeted. If a company is taking extreme measures to try keeping bugs and glitches in the dark instead of fixing them, then their products aren't worth buying regardless of price.
Until they stop trying to censor and start fixing bugs and issuing the patches free of charge (for everything and I don't mean introducing another version you have to pay for just to get one problem fixed), I don't recommend you invest in this game. No company should ever treat their community like this and expect to get away with it. If they straighten up their act and start fixing this game like the community wants, then I will start recommending this game again and with much more effort than I ever did.

Train Simulator is definitely not for everyone. Real-time simulation means you can travel for a couple of minutes through tunnels under London, or for an hour or so through desert landscape of Cajun Pass. If you're true to the spirit of the simulation and you use the cabin view exclusively, it can even get worse, as some trains have really tiny windows with limited view.
But it is as mesmerising, as only trains can be. I can spend hours just rocking myself in the chair as my train is passing ill-kept tracks. Scenery, sounds, and first of all driving "real" trains is like a childhood dream come true. And it can be challenging - even some "easy" scenarios.
I am not much into developing scenarios, routes or rolling stock, so I cannot review edition tools. I am not a hardcore sim fan, but I like the fact that TS does not feel like an arcade game - even though I am aware of concessions made.
And finally, the price of the game and its DLC. It is way too expensive. To get the Steam edition plus some additional essential packs, you have to cough up like 100 Euro. But if you can wait for a sale - I definitely recomend it. During the latest Autumn Sale I got the game plus enough routes and rolling stock to keep me busy for a couple of months.
So, if you're into trains - don't hesitate, buy and play - now or, better, when the next sale hits Steam.

Oh Arma 2. Where do I begin? First off, let it be known that this game is NOT a 1st/3rd person shooter game, it's tagged a "Military Simulator" or "MilSim", for short, for obvious reasons. This game is designed to deliver a realistic warfare feel to it, complete with accurate ballistics, realistic gear loadouts, and over 40 weapons and vehicles. I paid for this game and all the expansions, forking out a pretty 40$, mainly for the DayZ mod, as Arma 2 and Operation Arrowhead are required, the other expansions supposed to "improve graphics/animations", so after it sitting in my library for a couple years I felt inclined to try it. With that out of the way, time for the nitty gritty of this review.
The game spans over many miles (yes, literally MILES) of open country to explore throughout missions, including many cities, villages, farms, industrial complexes, hidden camps and castles, and the general rolling fields and foothills. Although, alot of this is just more "eyecandy/backdrop" than actual relevant terrain, as some of the missions only have you operating within specific areas. No worries, as when the missions open up for you, you are allowed to decide exactly how, when, and where you go about meeting and accomplishing your objectives. So, putting you in the boots of an experienced First Recon Marine Combat Vet, and allowing you to control his squad, drive Humvee's, or call in Helo-Extract at your leisure sounds tempting, correct? This is where the game is wrong. Firstly, if you've docked many hours in Call Of Duty, or Battlefield even, and for some reason think this game is gonna be along those same lines, then you're wrong. It's nothing like them. In more bad ways than good, I'm afraid. A vast majority of the voice acting is horrendous, im saying Marine's that havent hit puberty horrendous. Or how important character's voice over sounds like it was done over a phonecall, perhaps google translate even, and any character that is not in your squad has terrible or non-existant animations, standing like statues only moving their mouths to the occasional garble the spit up. Top it off with even worse AI and you got yourself a nice♥♥♥♥♥♥garbage cake. Try this, order your squad to pile into a Humvee, then order them to drive to a specific location, for me it was literally up the road 1/4 mile, in a straight line. Now proceed to witness them drive into anything and everything that was not in that straight line. Im talking hitting walls, buildings and other vehicles, while tring to backup continuously into the brick wall behind us, despite a simple order to move "forward". Ok then, them driving is a no go, let us try the Helo. Some missions allow support vehicles, such as Helo transport. Call it in, it flies to your position, you pick a drop off point, it flies there. No problem. Right? Wrong, again. In the middle of clearings, I've had the chopper refuse to land to get me and my squad, I've had it crash trying to take off, or drop us off, I've even had one of my squadmates run into the rear propellar and die instantly, when all I told him to do was get in. So far, so good I suppose. However, if you find yourself more perserverant than I, and want to continue to play this game, some advice should help;
-Get used to not firing your gun throughout an entire mission. Only having 5 mags may seem daunting at first, but once you realize your squad is going to most likely see the enemy before you do, they're gonna shoot them (or try to at least) first.
-Battlefield veterans can recall experiences when getting sniped from across the map was frustrating, but you'd just wait for a buddy in a chopper to rain down hot 5mm hell on them. For this game, imagine every damn enemy is a sniper. Most engagements for me and my squad involve us firing at enemy "positions", meaning "where we think they are", at an average of 150-300 meters away, or just shy of 1000 feet away. Thats about 10 football fields in distance.
- game deletes your saves upon completion of a mission, meaning if it didnt quite go according to plan, which is alot of this game is planning, have fun restarting the mission.
--PROS--
-Good graphics
-4 expansions
-plenty of weapons/vehicles
-weapon ballistics is fun to play with
--CONS--
-Terrible AI
-Game saves deleted when mission ends
-Horrendous voice acting (literally can't stress this enough, although kind of remedied from expansions)
-Character animations are stiff, and poor overall.
-perhaps too many controlls, not for everyone.

Thoughts after first playthrough:
Story
The story centers around a young man training to become a mech pilot. It's a fun premise that doesn't really go anywhere - It doesn't really build up to anything. There's no climax against a villain, or achieving a goal. The story ends abruptly without much payoff. This story is more about the journey than the destination. It's about individual moments, and the people in your character's life, which it does do well.
Characters
The MC is shaped by the dialogue and action choices you make through the game, so he can be anywhere from charming to pervy, cowardly to courageous based on how you want to play him. While many of the NPCs are tropes, they are familiar and well characterized. There are some genuinely funny and touching moments. I wanted to see them succeed and be happy.
Gameplay
You'd expect a game about giant robot battles to have more giant robot battles in it. I think in the whole game there is maybe three battles, which boil down to quicktime events. It would have been nice to have some impact on strategy or mech upgrades etc. The game has the dating-sim tag, but it's not really about buying them gifts, silly mini-games or anything tedious like that. Basically, when you have free time you hang out with your Waifu of choice and pick the dialogue choice you think they'd most like to hear.
Conclusion
ACE academy has some good ideas in it, and the characters are interesting. I like the artwork, the full english voice acting and the music is enjoyable. The problem is that there isn't a whole lot for the player to do. It's much more a novel than it is a game. I would be fine with that if the story was a little more intereting with a stronger climax and ending. I fully recommend it on sale ~$5-10, I would not pay $21.99 for it as it is currently listed.

This is a visual novel that wasn't developed for perverts. Well, kinda... Anyway, maybe all the reviews of VN's that are a point outside of the curve should begin like that, but that's what happens after having to carry a stigma related to the genre for so many years.
Well then, the story is about this guy and his sister who have recently moved to Japan to live with their uncle after their parents' death. The guy you control is good with mechas and stuff, and the girl fulfills her role perfectly (like a real sister). Through this premise, you get to meet some people throughout the way (mostly girls, of course), and... Yeah, you know it. You get to choose who's the most interesting character and then you go chase after them.
Now let's take a look on the game's aspects: The story is pretty basic (in my opinion). The soundtrack and effects are kinda decent, can't complain about them. The art is really neat, but I didn't really like the voice acting. As for the length, you can get to kill quite a good amount of time and try some different choices until you've done everything that's available. Even though this game has cloud saving, I'm still trying to understand why in the world it doesn't have achievements nor trading cards. Please try to implement these in the future, devs.
Overall, if you're a fan of the visual novel genre and is the kind of person who'd rather play the games because of the story rather than the naughty stuff (which usually comes included in the package), then this is a good alternative for you.

We have a shy girl, a tomboy girl, an overly flirty girl, and a girl whose characterization is fully expressed in words "nice with big boobs". Oh and the little sister who is adorable and likes to cook. What an exciting line-up.
Steam says I played this game for over 10 hours, but it felt like twice that. I kept waiting for the plot to actually pick up, but it just... didn't. It felt like it was just there as a vehicle for girl delivery. And okay, that's the case with most romantic-focused visual novels, but in this game it just felt. so. long. and. so. laborious. The writing itself is gramatically sound but bland across the board. Things that were supposed to be funny were not actually funny, and things that were supposed to be endearing were not endearing.
Overall I could have spent those hours reading fanfiction for more entertaining results.

Grind simulator...
My god the grinding. If you want any half decent weapons prepare to spend hours upon hours trying to get it, and then even longer just to get the attachments you want. I got so sick of it I just forked up £20 and bought the stuff I wanted, once I did that I had a pretty fun time with this. Despite the horrendously abusable spawning system, even though you get a few seconds of invisibilty as infantry, you end up being spawned out in the open, where you will be blasted by a tank or sniped from god knows where. Vehicles however, have no spawn protection whatsoever, and their spawn point varies to about 2 places if you're lucky, allowing for a single enemy player to drive to your spawn with an ammo crate on his jeep, and camp you out till the cows come home, lack of voice chat means that warning any tankers of impending infantry attacks takes forever, by which time they've been killed, respawned and been killed again. If you can get past the grind fest and the heavy spawncamping the game is quite fun, however you probably won't notice it because you'll be either so tired from grinding you forget what fun is, or you'll be bleeding out of every orifice with fury at being spawn camped for the 900th time.
POST RELEASE EDIT
Christ alone knows what the devs were thinking when they decided it was a good time to release, I get that the game had been in beta for a long time but it seems there was zero preperation on their part for the influx of players releasing the game would cause. Since release it's rare to find a match that isn't lagging and desynced to all hell, with the familiar message of "Network is trying to catch up" appearing a minimum of 40 times a game. The new spawn system solved the spawn issues for all of 2 matches, then everyone figured out where the spawn points were and just camps the exits of these areas. Even worse it's fostered a tactic of getting a rifle and just hiding within your own spawn zone near an objective, since enemy players can't use weapons within your spawn area, you can give yourself a nice safe area in which you are basically untouchable. The good things to come out of the last update was the increased size of capture zones and fleshing out the maps with some much needed cover, you can now move across the airfield without being visible to everyone and his dog, and the fleshed out capture points make fighting around them much more interesting, instead of the previous camping 2 doorways until the point is taken or a lucky grenade toss kills you. All in all though, grind reduction taken in to account, still horrendously grindy and not even close to ready for a release.

One of my favorite games to come out in recent years. Moon Hunters is an incredibly enrapturing experience, though one to be played in small doses. It's the kind of game to play sparingly, as trying to grind every achievement at once takes a lot of fun out of the game. Definitely recommend it for people who like RPGs or D&D and enjoy getting into the mindset of their character, and develop them through choices that they think that their character would make. Both singleplayer and multiplayer are fun experiences, though certain multiplayer features are slightly bugged, in the sense that all unlocks will go only to whoever is hosting the game, and that if people make different choices than one another the game doesn't really know how to handle it and just randomly chooses one.
My few complaints are that despite how narratively and artistically rich this game is, it's still relatively shallow, and I can't see there being much replayability value after all endings, characters, etc have been unlocked. Also, the "legends" feature that writes a tale about your character is pretty buggy, and will often list things that your character definitely never did, but that's a relatively small complaint.
Overall, however, Moon Hunters is a great game, though unless you're rolling in cash I recommend waiting until it's on sale to buy, as it's understandably pricey due to it being an indie game. I've had a lot of fun with it so far, and definitely recommend it.

HOLIDAY EXPRESS STANDALONE GAME REVIEW -- NOT A REVIEW OF TRAIN SIM 2014
If you are an old-timer like me, this game will stir nostalgic memories and flights of fantasy involving that much anticipated electric train arriving in Santa's bag with shiney tracks glistening under the twinkling lights of a Christmas tree, the faint smell of ozone as the engine crackled to life, and the artificial smoke beginning to magically flow as the mighty engine began its journey of delight.  The game is wonderful at any age where the heart is stirred by a love of trains and a desire to get on the floor and switch on the transformer to start an imaginary adventure.  Nope, it isn't the usual serious rail sim fare.  While it does use the Train Simulator 2014 UI and does have tools to edit your layout, the game is a more casual and relaxed experience.
You can earn some achievements, gain some experience points, and collect the trading cards in much the same way as the primary game.  It may also spark an interest in more serious virtual railroading for those who find the game enjoyable.
At the steeply discounted price of $2.99 for Holiday Express through the rest of the month, it is hard to go wrong with a game that delivers such a fun experience.  (Note: You do not need to own Train Simulator 2014 to play this standalone game.)  And who knows, it might just be a good fit as a virtual stocking stuffer for your gaming friends.
My last experience with Train Simulator was with a much earlier version.  I have to say this sure is improved and a lot more fun.  I have a feeling that every once in awhile in the days before Christmas I'll be punching that left controller stick to hear the train horn/whistle and with childish glee guiding an engine around curves and up inclines just for the fun of it.
That said, it does have some rough edges that might make it a little tough for the youngest players.  The on-screen directions will tell you to stop at a marker, which you can see in the 2D map, but which isn't visible in the 3D view.  In the 2D view, you can't see your speed to know what you should be doing.  The controls while easy to use with a controller could do with more granularity in managing speed and braking - the jumps with the slightest touch are fairly big.  So mom or dad probably will need to be nearby to give a little bit of coaching on using the controls for young players just starting out.

On first glance appearing as a badly thrown together physics game that simply doesn't work the game will for most people suddenly reveal its genius after significant trial and error.
All of a sudden you start noticing the absurd british humour, the subtle (Or not so subtle) political commentary on a view of the British national health service and you start to understand just how the game works and start becoming good at it. To the point where your not just trying to accomplish a heart surgery in the back of a moving ambulance, your seeing how quickly you can do it, if you can do it using only a fire extinguisher and a pair of scissors. Your seeing exactly how much crap you can place in the chest cavity of a patient mid operation and trying desperately to pry a kidney out from some ribs using a plastic spoon.
There are plenty of frustrations, due to a niave expectation of how the game 'should' play to the occasional physics bug that can cause your hands or a scapel to get stuck in awkward situations (between ribs, in a fridge [Yes, there is a firdge] etc). Rising above these frustrations and learning from is key to getting the best from this game.
This is no game of the year. But it is suprisingly intelligent and funny. Frankly if you don't have it, your missing out on something most people don't encounter very often. A new experience.

is short, but it's short and sweet. The visuals are always gorgeous, and at times, breathtaking.
Gameplay is simple without feeling simplistic: move the brothers around and manipulate objects to solve the puzzles. The control scheme, though confusing at times (you simultaneously control each brother with one stick and one trigger), is pleasantly novel; sometimes I felt like I was getting the hang of it, but the next minute, I was laughing at my confusion. The star of this game, though, is the story of the travails of these two brothers, and the people (and creatures) they encounter. Sometimes you'll laugh, and sometimes you may get kind of misty-eyed.
Being a value gamer, I generally prefer games that give me the maximum gameplay hours for the dollar, but even though this game only took about 3 1/2 hours for me to finish, I don't at all regret buying this title.

Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons is the most perfect 3 hours I've spent gaming this year. A absolute masterpiece and a total joy from beginning to end - just make sure you have a controller to play it.

Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons is, obviously, a tale about two brothers on a quest. A dying father requires healing, and his two sons set out to find a way to save him. The developers are able to tell you a story without any direct use of dialogue, text, tutorials, or narration. The control scheme requires a controller (xbox 360, third party, etc.), and while it can at times feel unintuitive, one quickly realizes how important the control style is to the narrative of the story. Despite the fact that the game is short (about 3-4 hours), it provides a fullfilling experience that most AAA-games fail to deliver. I highly suggest picking it up, as it is an excellent example of game design and storytelling through novel means.

There's something burningly satisfying about building up an army from a bunch of rag-tag recruits. You play other games and become attached to characters through learning their story but in this game, you become attached to them by being part of their story. Charging into battle with troops you've poured hours into training often induces a true concern but can also bring to surface a sense of strong confidence that your soldiers will utterly obliterate the opposition. This game's ability to poke at your different range of emotions makes it a very addictive and unique one.
For $20, this replayable, frustrating, pleasurable, ragdoll-heavy and rivetting game should make it into your "Top 10 Games" list, as it has for me.
{It most definitely should be noted that this game was made before the beloved Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim and is just as memorable and enjoyable as or more so than any newer games that are pumping out.}

A clever twist on tower defense that mixes traditional tower defense with a bit of Gratuitous Space Battles.
You are the rakish captain of a delivery ship that is built out of blank platforms that, upon launching into space, can have various traditional tower defense modules (canons, shields) built upon them along with engines to increase thrust. The game consists of starting at a port, accepting a delivery assignment, buying upgrades, launching your ship, then racing from the starting point to the destination with your deliveries intact, while defending your ship against asteroids and other ships and drones that you'll pass along your way. You'll acquire currency for upgrades and repairs by mousing-over floating golden nuts which appear in space after things are destroyed.
Once you reach your destination, you'll have rather long dialog scenes with your ship's droid, CEOs of the companies you are delivering cargo for, and others. These have a basic level of humor, but can drag on for a bit too long. Fortunately, they are fully voiced, which makes a big difference. If you were forced to click through these long bits of text, otherwise, it would detract a lot from the overall game.
If you're a big fan of tower defense games, this is worth checking out.

Sometimes a game comes along and reminds us that even a tired old genre can still be interesting if it's done exceptionally right.  Space Run is one of those games, as it turns tower defense on its head by casting you as running cargo through hostile sectors while controlling a ship that can convert resources ("hexnuts") into additional generators, shields, weaponry, engines, and the like.  The end result barely looks like tower defense at all, but manages to capture the best parts of the genre while possibly creating something even better.
In the most basic sense, it's a game about placing things on hexagons to survive various attacking threats.  However, this game goes far beyond the basics, and delivers a rock-solid good balance and great presentation.  It's great to see a PC game that was not rushed to market - THIS is an example of how indies are revitalizing the platform.

Creative spaceship-sandbox strategy & hilarious B-movie banter makes "Space Run" standout as a new microgenre: STD, a.k.a. Space Tower Defense.  Design experiments alone are mind-bogglingly complex with too many possibilities to comfortably calculate.   ...more to come.

It's an interesting enough spin on tower defense type games since you have to more actively manage your towers (repair them, change their firing radius) as well as your defensive tools (shields, ion cannon, et cetera).
If you don't like games that require a lot of trial and error (and subsequent experimentation) or just don't like tower defense in general, then don't bother. If you do like either of those two type of game design aspects, then it is passable. Not great, just passable.

This is basically the first VN of this type I've played (after the nightmare that is Doki Doki Literature Club made me aware of the genre), so if you're new like me you may relate to my perspective: I never thought much about VNs as they weren't "real" games in my eyes and -tbh- I still feel the same way. However, I always liked those Chose-Your-Own-Adventure books as a child, as they gave you some agency instead of just passively consuming.
Well, this is that but with way more focus on the characters, which I found to be actually quite believable, despite each of them obviously adhering to a common stereotype, though they each have their own bagckstory to discover, gaining some depth as the game progresses.
The story is basically a concatenation of mostly unrelated scenarios with the other characters in either your free time or during the mecha-fights, which lend the game its futuristic theme. There is somewhat of an underlying conspiracy plot going on, which however is resolved a little unspectacularly. It still kept my intereset the whole way, though.
The game has a lot of choices to make and most have three options to choose from. I do not think most make a big difference, but each one makes a scenario play out in a different way, making it your own expirence despite arriving at the same end situation. Mostly, your choice is to either relate to the character you're speaking to, make a reasonable argument or some quip/perverted remark. Although I found, that even the "BOOBIES!"-kind of dialouge choices were something I could see at least other actually saying. It was also a bit longer than expected at 14h played which was a nice surprise, although I might add I'd consider myslef a slow reader.
If I have one gripe with this game it is, that what is has in substance it lacks in resources and polish. Frequently reused backrounds often don't reflect what the story is telling (e.g. a crowded room is empty in the background) and charcters basically appear in a single standing pose except for some special occasions during the game. The faces of the girls seem to alll have the same shape with a pointed chin and the biggest difference seems to be in stature and attire. I'm glad to say though, that the faces nicely change expression in every situation you're in, so the focus of the budget was on the spot from my perspective. I would say that the voice acting felt very off at times, but english is my second language so take that with a grain of salt. I just turned it off in the settings and I was happier for it.
If you'd excuse me now, I need to revisit some choices I've made and see if I can romance the girl that always seems to hate on me for some reason. :-)

I've been considering Train Simulator for a while now. Up until now, the main reason I didn't get it, was the price. However, during Steam's recent autumn sale, the christmas DLC was 80% off, and since it didn't need the (expensive) core game to play, I decided this was my chance to try it out and see for myself how I like it.
Well, the game itself could be fun for a while, but my overall experience wasn't all on the positive side. While the game doesn't seem too complicated, the interface isn't very comfortable, to say the least. It took me a while just to figure out where exactly I'm supposed to stop to complete a scenario. You'd think it should be really simple, right? Well, so would I. At first I thought that maybe I was just being stupid and impatient, so I gave it some time and soon enough I figured it out. Regardless, I was feeling a little cheated, sort of like "Okay, I got it, I completed the scenario, but what now? Is that supposed to be it? Where's the fun!?".
Still not being sure whether I should give this little game more time or not, I figured I'd go read reviews on Steam, see what other people think, and then I encountered the reason for my decision not to get the game. It seems like the moderators the developers assigned to moderate the reviews to their game are quite the dictators. Watch how they mark this review as "off-topic", just like they did with the other negative reviews this game received. While those reviews described flaws and drawbacks regarding the game, they were fair, to the point and as on-topic as you can get.
It seems like the developers of this game would go quite far to hide any negative criticism, justified as it may be. If this is how it works, it makes me wonder - what are they so worried about? What are they working so hard to hide from everyone? I don't know about you, but if I ever find out, I promise you - it won't be by playing the game itself. Those guys are not getting any of my money. Not only because I have doubts about the game (and I do still have doubts), but mainly because I feel I'm being manipulated and left in the dark.
In conclusion, while I'm still not completely sure about the game itself, the attitude of the developers made me decide to stay away from this game, and I suggest to you to stay away as well.

Holy f***, I'm impressed. I haven't played a co-op RPG this good in a very long time. It combines DnD story elements with fantastic atmosphere and streamlined multiplayer interactions. You all experience dialogue together at the same pace (everyone has to confirm they've read it), experience the different random events together (if something happens to a specific person, you get to see their choices in real time!), and defeat bosses together. You adventure in 5 days of in-game time, so it presents something you can actually complete with your friends instead of just going "oh, it's an RPG... we'll play for a few hours and never touch it again, too bad."
My only criticism is the combat is super easy, but I think that was done on purpose to (once again) cater to the co-op aspect - and I get it, they want all players to be able to enjoy and have fun without getting stressed about performance. I really do recommend it to anyone looking for a fun game to play with friends. Totally an undiscovered gem.

I think this might be my Diablo III.  It's different: even more cartoony (I already complained about the general cartooniness of D3) but it doesn't feel like it takes itself seriously.  The world is a little shallow and the plot basic, but it doesn't pretend that the plot is important either.  This is pure action.  Playing a 5-player co-op right now with friends on Elite and it was a total blast, a nice mix of challenge and pace.  It keeps very true to the Diablo isometric combat mechanics, although different weapons now have slightly different mechanical functions (such as claws striking single opponents while a greatsword attacks in a large sweeping motion).  There are only 4 classes but the skill tree builds have enough diversity even within a class to feel fairly unique even in a large multiplayer.  It's a lot of fun and if you're looking for the multiplayer experience of Diablo for significantly cheaper, I think I actually enjoyed this a little more than co-op Diablo III!

ACE Academy is a story-rich visual novel developed and published by PixelFade Inc.. Following your little sister as she begins her studies in a new country, you find yourself transferring to ACE Academy which is a premier school for Cenorobotic studies in Japan. "Cenorobotics" is a new academic field dealing with the study and use of GEARs which are giant mechanized robots originally developed for military applications. The popularity of arena GEAR combat has enveloped a number of different areas with engineering, sponsorship, entertainment and weapons development just to name a few. How will you and your sister adjust to life in a different nation, will you be able to make friends or possibly find love and most importantly will your piloting skills position you and your GEAR at the top of the Cenorobotics program? Welcome to Japan.
Usually I skip the gameplay portion of a visual novel review because it's a visual novel and there is no gameplay...until now that is...sort of? Strangely enough, there actually is some gameplay involved in ACE Academy whenever there is combat with the mechs or GEARs as they are properly refered to. On the battlefield, as advances are made by you and your opponents you are quickly given a list of actions to make with your GEAR and you only have a very limited time, seconds at best as a countdown timer initiates, to make a choice which really adds to the tension of the battles. Do you block, evade, fire weapons or go in for a melee attack...it's all very well executed into the story quite nicely with animations during the battles. In summary, this additional dynamic really had me even more intrigued with the narrative in ACE Academy as I found myself eagerly looking forward to the next engagements with the GEARs.
Visually, this novel is really stunning with it's top notch illustration and professional presentation. The manga inspired artwork is some of the best I've seen in any V.N. and is filled with bright cheerful colors and terrific shading. Even the menu screens are beautifully done which shows the commitment that this development team really put into this title. One very eye-catching feature is the animation of the characters in this story. They certainly aren't the static 2D figures that you see in most visual novels no. The people in ACE Academy are wonderfully animated. Their mouths move when they speak, their eyes blink, they even show different emotions with their facial features like blushing and getting upset or angry. Sometimes even cute little speech bubbles with different animations in them like a heart or a tear pop up over the characters heads depending on what they just said or what they're feeling it's all very manga-like and fun to observe as you read the engrossing narrative. They also change clothing on a regular basis, whenever you meet someone outside of the Academy for a social engagement they are always wearing something different. I found this to be a wonderful little detail and something that you don't often see in most visual novels. On another note, the sound is of the upmost quality. It's truly immersive as the development team has managed to include ambient noises such as doors opening/closing, phones ringing, birds chirping, vehicles etc., basically all the sounds you would hear as the characters interact with each other and their environments as the story progresses. I really love it when these sounds are incorporated into the V.N. because it truly immmerses me within the story. ACE Academy has voiced dialogue and typically I like my V.N.'s without it but I must admit that the voice actors in this title have done an impressive job with the script. I find them all endearing and quite believable in what they say and how they say it. Also, your little sister Nikki has the cutest voice ever. In conclusion, with all the effort put forth in just the visuals and sound quality of ACE Academy you would be hard pressed to find another visual novel with as outstanding a presentation as this.
To date, ACE Academy has been without a doubt the best and one of the longest visual novel experiences that I've had on Steam. The story is extremely well written and quite entertaining and some of the more emotional scenes will even bring a tear or two to your eyes. There are many unique characters to interact with and an abundance of choices to make throughout the branching narrative and let's not forget the fun GEAR combat. There is also a ton of "pop culture" references thrown at you in this V.N. so that was an added bonus as well. As far as options go, there are the basics for audio, video and text speed. Also included is an unlockable CG gallery and a very memorable original soundtrack with a few homage bonus tracks thrown in for good measure. Sadly there are no Steam Achievements or Steam Trading Cards to collect which is a shame because those would go over nicely with this title. As most of the V.N.'s that I've tried on Steam have been fantasy based or occuring in present day, it was very refreshing to finally get a quality title that was purely science fiction. In conclusion, featuring a truly intriguing story in which you actually get to pilot a mech, amazing artwork, a rich cast of memorable characters and a terrific O.S.T., ACE Academy is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED to visual novel fans, anyone wanting to experience a great sci-fi story and definitely to anyone wanting to try a visual novel for the very first time.

The problem stems from a handful of things. The first of course is the play to win aspect. It's pretty rampant. I understand that they need to make money somehow, but it's pretty over the top in this game. Secondly if you don't create a character that has flying as it's mode of transport (You can choose super speed, flying, jumping extreme distances, etc.) then you're pretty much walking at a snails pace. Last but not least is just how amazingly repetitive this game is. Every mission, every quest, every objective is essentially exactly the same. Kill x amount of this badguy. Defend objective x until the timer runs out, kill henchmen until the badguy arrives to take a package.
Now don't get me wrong there is a lot that is good about this game. It's pretty, the character creation is really fun, and the costumes you can unlock are pretty cool. But overall I have to admit that as much as I wanted to like this game it just falls flat. It gets right to the finish line and just sits down and refuses to go any furthere........Unless you have $14.99+$14.99+$9.99+$5.99.....

This game looks interesting, and games that "look interesting" often don't deliver — but Moon Hunters is not one of them. It  delivers on all fronts, and very well. Both single player and multiplayer are worthwhile and offer immersive, drawing experiences that I'd highly recommend.
The first thing that stands out about this game is how spiritual it feels; the atmospheric, story rich presentation is never pretentious or bloated. The storytelling is brisk, effective, and unerringly evocative.
The gameplay has been given a lot of love, and player choice is rewarded narratively and mechanically no matter how the player approaches the game. The game brings to the table something that "choice-based" games have been lacking for a long time, despite widespoken desire: different choices instead of objective good/bad choices. Every choice you make with every NPC you encounter, every power you upgrade, the amount of enemies you do or don't defeat, and which of your traits you increase all formitively shape the legacy your playthrough leaves in tangible ways. Add, then, a short-but-substantial playtime for each playthrough and extremely high replayability with a colorful, diverse cast of playable characters (which expands as you play) to the mix on top of the constellation system that chronicles your prior playthroughs, highlighting your past exploits, and you have a delightfully easy game to sink your teeth into (bonus points — a gauntlet arena mode for your past playthrough characters, if you want to revisit old builds). It's a perfect intersection of several genres and playstyle approaches. You can hop on for twenty minutes or three hours and get something rewarding out of it.
The only downsides to this game are a few bugs and glitches here and there, but an easy-access bug report feature has been placed carefully in the pause menu, and I personally haven't found any of the glitches to be gamebreaking or detractors from my having fun with the game. They're minor nuisances at their absolute worst, and negligible otherwise.
The game's major strength lies in its intense respect of player agency and willingness to add the player's interaction with the world to the world itself — it sells itself as a "Personality Test RPG" for good reason. For that reason, I've nominated it for the "Choices Matter" award, and I really can't see any other candidate more fitting for the title.

I used to love tower defense games a few years back. However, they all became very similar - almost cookie-cutter in their design and gameply - making most of them completely undesirable to purchase, or even to play for free. Space Run goes back to doing tower defense the right way. The main feature/attribute that the other tower defense games were missing was that you always had more $$ than you needed. This means there was no strategy needed. None of your decisions mattered. You were going to get to the next level regardless. So, with Space Run, you are back to the [strategic] reality of finite resources. Choose wisely, otehrwise you may not defeat the enemies or the elements.
Just recently I vowed to never purchase another tower defense game. However, Sanctum (1 and 2) made me rethink that decision. And now Im glad Ive purchased Space Run. You can tell if a twoer defense game is good almost immediately and while Ive only played through 5 or 6 missions, I knew right after the intro/tutorial (which isnt even painful) that the game was going to be fun, challenging, worth my time, and more importantly, worth my money. The full price of 14.99 USD seems a little high but the sale price puts the game right into the Goldilocks zone.
Would I recommend the game. Sure thing. And I havent played enough to give it a rating out of a possible ten points. Will add that rating later.

I really tried to like this game. I appreciate the work of the developer, and I think the subject of the game is important. However there are just too many shortcomings in the game to recommend it, even for an indie game.
First, the graphics: Most of the scenes are very dark, and you either look for dark gray objects on a darker gray ground, or try to find your way using a absurdly small cone of light coming from your mobile or a flashlight. And even if there is a little more light, graphic is simple and static.
The story: As I said earlier, the subject is important, but why must the story be so shallow-brained? Poor kid is left by his mom, despised by his dad, bullied by his classmates, whatever could happen to a kid, he got it. Locked in the barn, thrown in the water and his mother even bothers to write a letter how much she hates him before she leaves. Oh, come on.

Short review - Worth the price for sure. Good art. Solid sountrack. And I enjoyed the premise of the story. The dialogue was well-written and I laughed more than a few times. However there is one pretty large caveat and there will be spoilers in the the full review. However, I would reccomend the game, especially if you pick it up on sale. It's a yes from me.
***********************************
Full review
The game is made in the Ren'py engine. From personal experience, VNs made in Ren'py tend to crash from time to time and have a few minor bugs. I found none of that in ACE Academy (known as AA from here on out) so that counts as major points in PixelFade's favor. Kudos on simply a *well-made* game. Can tell a lot of effort went into crafting this game.
The game also has English V/Os. Voice Acting in VNs is always appreciated as long as it doesn't detract/distract from the writting. And that's not the case here. At worst, it's servicable. The only way it could detract would be if it was bad and that's not the case here at all. I would say there's a standout, but the primary characters all good a good job. Some of the dialogue is cheesy, but I'm not going to hold that against the V/As. They made it work.
The dialogue is well-written for the most part. Standard cliches aside, there's a very intriguiging story here and I found myself getting invested in the characters. I wanted them to suceed. I was rooting for them, Some of the dialogue is genuninely amusing and I found myself laughing more than a few times. AA is also HORRENDOUSLY cheesy at times and I find real-world references tend to "date" games. It's fine to fill your game up with time period references if you're making a game that's supposed to have a retro-atmosphere or there's a particular theme you're chasing (such as a movie intentionally paying homage to 80s action flicks or B-movie shlock). GEARs of Thrones? How I Met Your GEARs? That doesn't even make sense.
The only negative is that for as much as I enjoyed the writting and the story in general, the ending for AA is absolutely a bust. The game unmistakably feels incomplete. There's is NO getting around it. The game just ends JUST as it seems the story is starting to get REALLY interesting. I understand PixalFade is not CDProjektRed or Bethesda or another AAA developer and you can only do so much on a given budget. It almost feels unfair because PixelFade seems like an Indie developer you should all support. It's clear that there's more story capable of being fleshed out and for that reason I hope to encourage people to buy this game and support this company. Maybe the project might have been a little too ambitious but they should be praised for their vision and AA is nearly a great realization of it.
Instead it's merely good. But IS good. And occasionally great. But I won't hold their vision against them.
Support PixelFade, guys

Pros:
- The other girls' lives doesn't revolve around you. Unlike other VNs I read, their lives and interaction doesn't stop completely once you have picked out a route. I was surprised that other characters had found a relationship even without the MCs urging, especially since these other characters can be romanced as well. You could also hang out with them even after locking into another route which is a huge plus because in other VNs they fade into obscurity with the spotlight shining towards your route. (ehem Katawa Shoujo)
- Comedy and Fourth-wall breaks.
Cons
- MC's story was unsatisfying.
- The final match was unsatisfying.
- Some dialogues are different from what is said, to what is written in box below.
- No explanation on what key is skip, auto mode, etc.
- Backgrounds are recycled in some parts. When tutoring in the daycare you get the BG from the library at ACE, any lobby from other places gets you the Pilot's lounge, among others.
Routes:
Yuuna & Valerie>Kaori>Mayu
Yuuna and Valerie are my two favorite routes. Yuuna was just a sweet-heart and the comedy sprinkled during her route was just fantastic. Valerie, on the other hand was the best complement to the MC if you choose his flirtatious responses all the time.
Kaori and Mayu was meh. Kaori was just a tsundere and that was what she has going for her. Mayu would have been better had her father been introduced to the MC and an arc about how her father disapproves or something would be better, and the surprise Yandere Mayu was just too OOC IMO.
Recommendation: If you like a VN that isn't heavily-focused on drama or a thought-provoking story and instead focuses on comedy, buy this game.
Price: Buy it during sales. The story was really unsatisfying to justify buying the game full-priced.

Brothers is a beautiful and emotional game that tell us the journey of two brothers in search of a cure to their sick father. For me the strongest points are the story, that is well written to the point that you understand it, even if the characters speak a made up language, and also the graphics and art of the game. The gameplay resembles a bit to the PS2 game Ico, but you have to control, at the same time, both of the two main characters, making sometimes, and specially at the begining, a bit of a challange. The soundtrack is also very good. The weakness is the longevity, as the game is only 3 hours long. But exploring the scenario, getting all the achievements, and replaying the story can get you to extend the experience.

I can see why this has been on so many GOTY lists. The journey you take with the brothers is extraordinary. Closest thing I can liken it to is Ico, Shadow of the Colossus and Dark Souls, except if those had been made by Astrid Lindgren.
A couple scenes had janky animation, and at one time I felt frustration at not knowing what to do, but those issues don't matter on the whole. The world design and story more than make up for it. Critics like Adam Sessler & TotalBiscuit had hyped up the ending quite a bit, and probably as a result I didn't find it outstanding in any way. It ended like it should, but it wasn't the high point for me. The best scenes in the game were the ones which were completely optional. For example at one point you meet a man who has lost his family in a fire and is about to kill himself. Whether you help him or not is optional, and if you do there's a thing you can do for him which helps him deal with his loss. This entire area is off to the side and can easily be ignored if you choose to. But this, and many other areas like it provided the strongest moments in the game for me.
I'm glad I played it. I had seen clips from it and heard the hype from those who played it, but it didn't really prepare me from what the game is like. Don't miss it.

This is an odd one but a game I do not regret purchasing at all. Here is why:
(Note: the review is very long so if you don't want to read all of it, you can skip right to the conclution which sums everything up although I would reccomend reading all of it.)
Setting
You play as two brothers who recently lost their mother and are looking for a cure for their very ill father.
Presentation
The graphics in this game are not exactly what I would call cutting edge but the asthetics, the atmosphere and the sound are spot on. The game looks, feels and sounds beacutiful from begining to end and does a great job of conveying a story without any dialogue at all. The only problem is that occationally, you won't know where to go as it is not always clear but I felt that was kind of the point.
Gameplay
The gameplay is not that amazing and I feel that this is the weak point of the game. Although certainly not enjoyable or unplayable, the gameplay is not the best I have seen. The only noteworthy part of the gameplay is that you control both brotherts at the same time and that is why you need a controller as you need the two analoge sticks to control them both at the same time. The movement can be very hard to get used to and I often died because of confusion caused by the controls but it really helps you connect to the story and adds something to the puzzles that other puzzle games just cannot do. For example, there is a puzzle in which one brother has to hold something for the other brother for a long period of time while thge other one does something. During that time, your fingers may get sweaty and may even start to hurt which really helps you understand what the brothers are going through. Overall, the gameplay is very clever but not spectacular.
Story
This is by far the highlight of the game. I am not going to say too much about it so that the story isn't ruined for you but every character feels like they should be there, every hurdle adds to the experience and evcen though there is no dialogue at all, the writers did an amazing job in conveying the story to the player. It really feels like all of the other aspects of the game are there just for the story.
Conclutsion
Technically, this is not an amazing game but all of the game's aspects come together in a way that makes this a truely extraordinary game. Although short, you will feel the love and dedication that went into this game even if you don't really enjoy the gameplay which certainly is not for everyone.
I usually don't like puzzle games but I found this was an exception and I am very happy I picked this up.

Tower defence disguised as space exploration with strong puzzle elements.
You place different structures on preset ship layouts so that your defences adequately deal with the hazards for each level. As you proceed you get access to better structures, which allow you to complete new levels and replay earlier levels and finish them more completely. Different levels have different hazards, but also different handicaps on your ship.
The story is funny at times, but not really a big part of the game. The later levels are hard, and just surviving is often a challenge. There are some subtle (and not-so-subtle) references to various sci-fi series, and plenty of replayability. For a completionist there's easily 20 hours of fun. Just to complete each mission will give you at least 10 hours of enjoyment.

As you pour your earnings back into technology and upgrades for your ship, the jobs you successfully complete will increase your reputation, which will let you earn even more. Meanwhile, your android business partner will give you helpful advice and constantly let you know how badly you are doing at any given moment along your runs.
This game is a great little twist on tower defense that has you fitting out spaceships in order to hold cargo, passengers, engines, and of course, weapons. As you carry your cargo from one space dock to the next, your ship will be attacked by other ships, pirates, and asteroids. You can mine resources from the scraps of the stuff you destroy on the trip, and that lets you build and upgrade more weapons and engine power.
There are a lot of different components involved, and figuring out how to best layout your ship's "deck" with the stuff you need to take is definitely a challenge. To add to the challenge, you generally launch with very little equipment in play and you have to add the rest on the fly (literally).
My only complaint is that weapons have a limited wedge of fire and rotating the turrets manually can be a bit tedious in the midst of a pitched battle.
Overall, Space Run is a lot of fun. I mean, really who hasn't dreamed of being a rogueish space pirate? And have fun spotting all the sci-fi references in this one because they're all over this game.
