Spore's known by many as one of the most ambitious as well as one of the most disappointing games ever to be made. This is one of the few points of which it does not disappoint, actually, because nearly everything else falls flat.
Spore's gameplay consists of 5 stages: The cell stage, the creature stage, the tribal stage, the civilization stage, and the space stage. Starting from the first stage, cell, you can already see things going wrong. It'd be hard to ignore, as the cell stage is pretty much the same as any other game that makes you eat things to grow. It adds a few other gimmicks, namely the ability to customize your cell. I'm sure this is a big factor as to why people bought this game, but in the cell stage it starts off fairly limited. You can also choose whether you want to be a herbivore, carnivore, or an omnivore, though you have to unlock the mouth part to become an omnivore. If you choose carnivore, you have to hit moving things, other cells, until they die. Sometimes you'll get hit in return. Getting hit by other cells is a threat whatever you choose, but the carnivore and in extension the omnivore are the only ones that will have you provoke other cells. If you choose the herbivore, you will hit stationary things and eat them. Larger cells might chase after you sometimes. The game will say they're cells, but they're really only fish. That's about all there is to this stage.

The creature stage is next, oftentimes said to be the most enjoyable stage with its only competition being the space stage. However, it is not enjoyable. The gameplay boils down to three things: killing other creatures, dancing with other creatures, and digging up skeletons that can be found at random. To achieve this, you place parts on your creature that assign various abilities with skill levels. Speaking of this, the reason this is said to be one of the most enjoyable stages is the customization, which is much more expanded than in the cell stage. It will remain that way throughout the rest of the game with little bits and bobs being added in the tribal and space stages. When killing off a nest of creatures, thus driving them to extinction, you essentially do the same thing as in the cell stage, hitting them until they die, but now you have abilities that are assigned to hotkeys. They all do nearly the same thing with varying damage and time to recharge except for one ability where you can shoot poison at a distance and do damage over time. When dancing with your fellow creatures, though it isn't just dancing, you will eventually befriend them and can add them to your pack. However, as your creature is most likely better than them in one or both ways, it may be more worthwhile to simply recruit members of your own species to follow you around. The worst part of the creature stage, I'd say, is looking around for bones. When you scrounge them up, you get a part to add to your creature. As you will most likely finish everything else before you find all the bones, a lot of your time in the creature stage may be spent going on a scavenger hunt for these things if you want all of the parts for your creature.
The next stage, tribal stage, can be nearly entirely skipped over. It is very similar to the creature and civilization stage, and can be described as a merging between the two. You won't spend much time here. You start with three other villages aside from your own. Deal with them and you're done. You control more units now, which you can increase by making your villagers reproduce. Combat's similar to the creature stage, except now you give your villagers roles instead of hotkeys. Befriending others is also the same, and your new friends will give you gifts afterwards. You also need to get food, and for some reason you can domesticate animals but I don't see much point in doing that with how easy it is to do all of this.
The civilization stage is just Spore's attempt to be a grand strategy game, but without any of the depth or management that it takes to be a good gran strategy game. Same formula as before, conquer or befriend, and now you can capture resources that you can trade. This sounds very similar to something else with the same name. You get to customize your cities and create new settlements. There are land and air forces. This is boring and goes very quickly as absolutely nothing is polished enough to warrant any consideration.
The final and arguably best stage is the space stage. You get to do the most here, and this is where Spore comes closest to being its own game. You can colonize new planets, terraform them, and make them suitable for life. That was what kept my attention for most of it, but terraforming planets gets to be boring quickly. You can trade with other sentient beings, establishing trade routes to accomplish this. Said sapient beings can also form alliances and go to war with each other without your intervention. They'll sometimes give you quests, though I know this is expanded upon in the DLC. There are many, many star systems to explore. You will not get to all of them. This is where it ends, though. You get nothing else, and so this, with all the content it adds and improves upon from the previous stages, is probably not going to last more than 30 minutes to an hour.
The graphics look bad, and the soundtrack is nearly nonexistent. I would only say to get this if you like what I described in the space stage or if you like superficial customization, which is probably the best feature. New things were introduced that had the potential to be cool, but they simply couldn't fulfill what they were made to do. Not a good game overall, I'd say.

Red Faction Guerrilla plays a lot like GTA and is a part of the Red Faction frachise, for this reason many mainsteam review sites approached it with very high and unrealistic expectations. When it comes to open world games such as this Rockstar set the bar rather high, thus making it very difficult for other studios to release similar games without unfair comparisons. Volition did, however, strike gold with Saints Row a few years earlier with Saints Row.
Red Faction Guerrilla is set many years after the worker uprising. Military forces from Earth were first greated as liberators, they even terraformed the surface of the planet making it habitable, but over time the EDF became yet another oppressive regime and Red Faction rose up again to fight them. Much like GTA, you can roam and explore the entire environment on foot or in any number of vehicles. You can pick and choose your missions, taking on side challenges, or missions that advance the story along. Its totally up to you how you do them and in what order. As a game that follows the GTA formula it suffers from what I like to call Police Swarm Syndrome. PSS is where you get a wanted status and suddenly cops, or EDF troops in this case, start coming out of the woodwork as if by magic. Their vehicles swarm you from all sides, and if you're on foot you can almost forget about surviving. Then, when you finally get to a safehouse they stop chasing you. Its the same formula that GTA follows, and while its a formula with obvious flaws I've yet to see anyone else come up with something better.
Being a Red Faction game, many expected to be able to destroy everything in the game environment, but you're limited to just the buildings. This is a limitation of what was possible with game engines are the time. Games like Minecraft has demonstrated how to do voxel-based game worlds, and I'm certain we'll soon see game environments with the graphics of GTA V or even Crysis 3 that are fully destroyable without requiring huge amounts of memory or CPU power. Just look at what SOE is doing with Everquest Next. Some were disappointed by the inability to destroy everything, but knocking down buildings on top of EDF soldiers or blowing buildings up is still delicious fun.
Red Faction Guerrilla is one of the top 10 most underrated games of all time. Much of that is because it shares gameplay mechanics with GTA, and its from the Red Faction franchise so its obvious why expectations were high. Still, warts and all, the game is very good, the story well crafted, and its simply just fun to play which in the end is the most imporatant thing.
I recommend this game for fan of the Red Faction series and anywho who likes the GTA open world formula.

This game had promise, but later levels become a function of tedium with constant need to adjust turrets. I enjoy the premise and I enjoy Tower Defense style games, but I don't find micromanaging turrets any fun. If they add in a tactical pause option I may find myself going back to those levels and changing my review accordingly. If you happen to enjoy that sort of gameplay mechanic you will probably enjoy the games later levels, but if not I really couldn't recommend the game. There is also the problem of gamebreaking bugs, see below for details here. That is the short summary of why I can't recommend the game personally. For further details keep reading.
Pros
+Great premise which freshens the stale Tower Defense genre.
+Voice acting is generally humerous.
+Variety of turrets/upgrades is relatively small, but generally each feel unique.
Cons
-Micromanaging turrets, which may be a plus for some people but not for me. Also, here a tactical pause would alleviate this con.
-Gamebreaking bugs, after my 6 or so hours playing the game the game froze and or exited to windows a dozen times. This usually happened when a new unit was introduced and then it would freeze/exit and I would then have to start all over on that level.
-Turrets/Upgrades while unique feeling would benefit from more upgrades or options. Also, the idea that all the later turrets take up more space on the ship and thus generally undoing what benefits the stronger turret gave.
That is the overview of the game, in my opinion. I will update my review, if/when they update patch fixes for the tactical pause and gamebreaking bugs.

This is the games weakest aspect. While running around Mars with a sledgehammer and some bombs is fun and all, the whole "smash building" thing gets VERY repetitive.
The destructible terrain would shine greatly if the devs used it properly. I had a blast when EDF soldiers were closing in on me and I was holding out in a mansion that was slowly crumbling, in which I used my hammer to make the second floor collapse on my enemies while I made my hasty escape. It was a fun scenario, but it happened by complete random.
The developers seemed to realize the whole "hold out in building against enemy waves" thing was fun, and tried to add it in the form of defence missions. The problem is that your allies, the Guerrillas, need to be ♥♥♥♥ing babysat as they're extremely incompetent and will die at the drop of a hat.
Oh, and did I mention the babysitting? You're apparently the only useful guy on Mars, as everyone else is too busy sitting around with their thumb up their♥♥♥♥♥♥ If a civilian or ally dies, the Guerrilla morale meter goes down. This means that any of those braindead idiots walk into a collapsing building, or directly into enemy fire, you're punished.
The game tries to give you things to do by generating missions. Seems fun and all, but there's only 2   types of missions, and they're both f*cking AWFUL.
The first is the defence mission, which I've mentioned before. Braindead AI ahoy!
The second is a timed car-delivery mission. This means that even if you're a millimeter away from the checkpoint, the game marks it as failed. It's annoying and not fun. At all.
The main missions comprise of "go here, explode that." Sounds fun, right? Now do it 100 more times.
Also, it's """"""open world"""""", except not really. Buildings don't respawn, so once you're done the main campaign there's nothing else to destroy. I had to install a mod just to have actual freeroam.
Overall, I'd rate it 3/10. Good game mechanics and graphics, awful everything else. The only people who could enjoy this game for more than a few hours are the ones with ADHD.

I've been looking at this game for a while with some doubt because the screens and most videos didn't really give me a feel for how it was played or much of any information.
I'll try to provide some help for others in the same situation:
# The game is essentially a tower defense game, mixed up in that the 'tower' you are defending is a moving spacecraft carrying a quantity of cargo which you must physically protect from attacks and safely deliver to the destination. Your spacecraft is made up of a collection of hexagonal tiles, the layout of which differs from mission to mission.
# You will come up against asteroids and pirates in a variety of forms, sizes and quantities including 'boss' type enemies.
# Each mission you begin by placing the single engine and power slots and your assigned quantity of cargo slots across the layout of your ship. You must then start the mission and make use of 'construction points' of which you will be provided some at the beginning and which will slowly regenerate as the missioin progresses.
# You collect more construction points by destroying asteroids, pirates and other cargo ships that you come across, spending these points on slots and special  slots-specific abilities which you unlock as you progress.
# There is strategy in the construction of you ship, using the layout of hexagonal tiles, creating the right mix of offensive, defensive, supportive and engine slots so that you can adequately protect your cargo, survive attacks and go for the speed bonuses on each level - The added constraints of the free space some slots require around the ship and in that some slots require multiple hexes and/or a minimum distance from extra power nodes.
# As you progress, each mission gives you quantities of 'Fame' and 'credits' dependant on your performance. The Fame works like a level cap, with higher levels unlocking new ship slots for you to buy with your credits. You also use credits to upgrade these new slots to add new abilities which you can temporarily switch on during a mission (For example rapid 40 second rapid fire boost for laser turrets). Each slot has three upgrades, the third of which is usually a passive, permanent enhancement of the slot (for example, 30% boost to engine output).
In many ways, this game feels like Space Pirates And Zombies (SPAZ) in art style, combat, upgrades/levelling and to some extent story and humour. There is a smattering of story, but it is essentially pointless.
The tower defense elements are very reminiscent to me of Sanctum in how you are supposed to place, manage and pair them to create the most desireable effect.
There are some complaints that the game ends up requiring too much micro-management, but this feels more me to be a misunderstanding of what the game is: This is not a tower defense game, its more like a strategy defense game. The micro-management is intentional and provides challenge through both the creation of your ship and your use of slots and abilities.
Some of the most fun I've had with the game is micro-managing my turrets so that they create interlocking fields of fire to track a passing ship and gradually shifting the orientation of each turret as the passing ship moves out of the fire arc, slamming the enemy ship with continuous broadsides.
Equally, some of the most tense moments were monitoring areas that were taking a pounding and timing the use of the shield recharge bonus and the Laser turret rapid fire to keep my slots and cargo alive.
I would highly recommend this game.

I've never reviewed a thing on Steam and there are stome truly great games out there. This game definitely deserves a review. If you're trying to find that game that is just the right combination of RPG, strategy, and warfare, this is the game for you. This one hit the spot and I hope that there will be more games just like it.
If I had to say anything negative about the game, and I'm loathe to do so, then I'd mention that its graphics are not quite on par with other titles. To be clear, this doesn't mean that they are bad, exactly but that they are just not as good as other titles.
I'd also mention that, while the game does all three of the aforementioned genres (RPG, Strategy, and Warfare) very well, it is not perfect in any of them. It has elements from all of them, but if you want to play an excellent strategy game, you will have to go else- where (Any Paradox title, Civilization, or Total War). If you want an excellent RPG then you will want to buy such titles as Dark Souls, The Elder Scrolls, Dragon Age... etc (the list is long), and if you want something that is more focused on the warfare elements that appear in this game, I'd recommend the Dynasty warriors series. In short, the game has elements of all of these genres, but isn't the best representative of any of them.
I hope they keep improving and release another one.

This is quite possibly the worst game I've ever had the misfortune to waste my time on. Just downloading and installing the game took literally 12 hours. The character creation customization is impressive, although, the majority of the powers are already behind a paywall. The inventory you begin with is quite small. In fact, it appears to be smaller then it was previously since I watched a free-to-play review of this game and in that video the guy commented on his large inventory, which was visibly twice the size of the one I had.
The opening dungeon features a custscene with superman. Ok, he sounds vaguely like superman, looks like superman but apparently he lost the power to lip sync because while his lips move occassionally, their movement and what he is saying don't relate AT ALL. Considering that is the first cut scene you ever see, you think they could at least get that right, but NOPE. Bruce Lee movies from the 1970's had better dubbing. I'm not even kidding.
Visually, the game otherwise looks good. That is, however, where anything positive I have to say about this game ends.
The combat system however, is *INCREDIBLY* clunky, at least with a mouse. The UI cannot be customized *AT ALL*, the controls cant be customised *AT ALL*. The in game help leaves MUCH to be desired. Thats just dps. For healing, this game has to the most horrible implementation *ever*. You cannot actually target someone, the game simply heals whatever it thinks the priority target is. So, if you can see someone is about to take damage, well, that doesn't matter someone on low health but taking zero incoming damage will be prioritized regardless of what you think. Yup, ingenius.
The efficient heals have a rather LONG and IMPOSSIBLE TO MISS animation and are interruptible. As a PVP-oriented player I immediately recognized that casting one of these heals would immediately lead to the entire world spamming the lvl 1 zero cool down hard stun on you for having the temerity to consider joining a game as a healer.
This would be bad enough, but at least I could perhaps enjoy a few instances of pve first? LOL NOPE! The people I had the misfortune to group with used the games abilities that allow you to fly, walk over walls etc. to take themselves to every level, corner and as far away as humanly possible from each other in both terms of distance and elevation, aggro everything and mindlessly drag this uncontrolled mass around with them as they ran like chickens with their heads chopped off from the ravening hordes of mobs. Fortunately, if you cast a heal then the instance population would then b-line for you and end your misery in short order, before returning to annilating your moronic companions.

This game is very short and sweet. For what it is, though, I liked it a fair bit. The characters all have different combat styles, and the RP aspect is really fun. I played this with my partner, and we had a lot of fun. I'd recommend this to anyone who likes pixel art, pretty landscapes, the stars, and fighting in games. The combat system is not difficult to master. Your choices in the games  (usually made by exploring as many regions on the map as you can), will determine what you're known as. Once you've beaten it on one character, you still have not beaten the game. Seriously. You wont get to the end of the game just through one playthrough.
Good luck!

Even though the core game is pretty short, the characters are all distinct enough that multiple playthroughs feel pretty warranted, especially since the game gets mixed up each time so you'll get some fresh levels to go through. On top of that, having your stories from past characters be carried over and referenced gives a nice tied-together feeling to the whole thing.
The multiplayer is fun and pretty easy to get started with. The character mechanics can work well together and it's fun arguing over which choices to take.

A single run of this game is all it takes to see how deep it is.
Extremely repetitive, huge areas with boring combat mechanics, unimpactful dialog choices that do not affect the way you apprehend the game.
The next runs will be about getting the game achievements (ie: getting all the constellations, unlocking animals/spirits dialogs, solving the only puzzle of the game ...). If you want more details go checkout other negative reviews.

While Space Run is a novel idea, there's still room for significant work to be done to make this a real stand out product.  It's worth a look, but I'll wager that once players finish the game, it won't have the replay appeal that it deserves.
The Good:  A catchy story that engages the player in the sci-fi genre.  IMHO, I feel engaged in the story to want my character to make the fast, safe deliveries.  I've even played the same job a few times over to get the highest rating and to see what the next job offers entail.  This is also necessary as ship options and upgrades aren't cheap.
The Bad:  The controls aren't smooth and there's no zoom feature so unless you have a good idea what things look like while they're all clustered together, you may find some frustration when you're placing pieces and even orienting them during the heat of battle.  Maybe it's just me, but sometimes the bad guys seem to have too much of an advantage...I'm also open to the idea that I'm not that good of a "tower defense" player, but this isn't about me.  Another aspect I disliked was the fact that destroying a pirate's boosters does not affect their speed.  They manage to keep up with you with their one booster while all seven of mine where giving me maximum thrust.
The Superficial:  There's some variety in this "tower defense" space battlefield even though it's simply flying from point A to point B (I would have liked to have seen a navigation screen so that I could at least choose the path my craft is going to take a la Starfox navigation screen on the SNES).  The story line adds humor, though your android's responses are repetitive.  Maybe the next iteration, we'll get to chose our crew and even chose a different android.  I for one would find a sassy female android better company than the annoying Addam-12.  I would have also liked the option of selecting the layout of the transport for my deliveries, but the "one man studio" developer made it work with the one you end up using.  Speaking of layouts, Star Wars fans will be happy to see a familiar shape on the BC mission "Asteroids on Steroids".  While I get that space is vast, I was hoping to see more engaging celestial objects in the background such as a comet, black hole, nebula or star.
Though I do recommend the game, I would hope to see a quantum leap in game controls and other improvements should there be another Space Run.  After all, they made a Cannonball Run 2....

Nice old-school game with plasticine-powered graphics that portray interesting and original locations. Humorous approach to design and sounds makes it funny.
There are three kinds of gameplay here. Scroll shooter and 2d platformer are done well, with different kinds of enemies and their behaviours. New ones keep getting introduced throughout the whole campaign in order to keep things interesting. Length of each level is timed very well - you will always advance to next location before you get bored with previous one. Each of them has different look and feel and is accompanied by well made music.
The "land your ship on the planet" part is overly difficult due to inertial controls and many traps thrown around. Thankfully, these sections can be skipped by falling down while you're invincible for few seconds after being hurt. Which brings us to the next merit of the game - accessibility.
Easy difficulty gives enough health and lives to complete the game, and you can start it from any level you previously finished.
It takes only about half an hour to complete the game, so you will have to play it few times in order to get the trading cards. There is a lot of room for becoming better at this game, which will make replays enjoyable.
If you like old-school experience of replaying the same game and getting better at it, you will enjoy this game. Otherwise it will still be fun to complete it thanks to accessible easy difficulty, though due to short playtime waiting for deal or promotion where the game can be taken for small price or for free is worth considering.

First of all, let me get this out of the way: I have never been much into Visual Novels. I've played Nekopara, which I enjoyed, but aside from that, I've never liked them. But ACE Academy is different. Much, much different. You see, I don't think any game could pull off the VN formula as well as ACE did, at least not for me. The story is emotional, beautiful, and brilliant, with lots of pop culture refs. Plus (and this is very important for me), the game wraps you up in the characters-- their flaws, their charms, their problems, the way they interact with the main character-- and then it's over, just as quickly as it started. Believe it or not, this is actually a key strength. People don't realize a lot of the time, but when a game is short and sweet, not only can it be better than a huge game, it is also much more RECOMMENDABLE, because it's something that someone can feasibly finish all the way through and still enjoy every part of it. I could go on about how it encourages you to save and take risks, and how each character deviates strongly from stereotypes, but I won't. ACE Academy gets my full recommendation. Go play it. And thank you so much, PixelFade.

Do you enjoy the screams of your knights as they sacrifice themselves to your will?

I've spent more than an hour playing this game, and not knowing what the hell I'm doing. Does pulling this lever make the train go? What about the other level? How do I get it to STOP?
...you know, it doesn't matter. Most games, if you go off course or something, they'd have a narrator, dialogue box, or an NPC yell at you that you're not doing the right thing. This game? You get maybe a squeak... and if it's really bad, the train might derail, that's it.  You can solve problems at your own pace. Eventually figure out what buttons cause what thing, and if that's really necessary. And moreover, even though you're playing a game and you have to pay attention... you can relax.
Play this if you are getting older and would like a game to play that will genuinely relax you. There are objectives, and you can try to meet them, and you will eventually figure out how to make the train move, but it doesn't matter. These maps are meant to simulate a 20-80 minutes crawl, and that is not contracted. You will spend an hour or more sitting in front of the map watching the train as you wait for curves to slow down at, changes in the speed limit, and just getting to the timetable of delivering passengers/cargo. It's a relaxing game.
Short story: great game for train enthusiasts, and older gamers who just want to play a slow-paced game that won't yell at us for going slow or thinking about what we're doing every five minutes.
If you're looking for Grand Theft Train and want to play mowing down people on the track, and jumping the rails to ride into the city, you will be very disappointed.

If you're a Tower Defense fan like me, you're going to love this game. It brings with it some of the basics you've come to love, while adding a ton of new features. While in a standard TD type game you are just defending a path, in this game you're a moving "platform" that asteroids and enemy ships come from unknown directions at all time, forcing you to fortify every position properly.
Add to it that you're transporting cargo for a specific company each time, and every piece of cargo takes up space on your ship, which further limits your building space. In addition to forementioned things each cargo type also have special abilities that will hinder you even further. Things like drawing power from your towers, Nuclear waste that can blow you up if hit or just snobby travellers that need to be positioned on the outside limiting your guns shooting angles.
Overall a great game, and definitely worth it for the price, even outside of sales! I sincerely hope they add more through DLC's or even a second, third, fourth etc game!

I'm tired of tower defense games but I enjoyed this one so much I've played it constantly.  I only have a few minor complaints, most of which could be easily fixed:
- There's sometimes a bit of trial-and-error required to get 5 stars on boss missions because you don't know what direction the boss will attack from.  You have around 5 seconds of warning at most, during which time you'll potentially need to recycle a bunch of towers and then set new ones constructing.  If players had more like 10 seconds it would seem more fair I think.
- [EDIT: The developer confirmed they're fixing this in a patch] The voice volume setting only affects menu voices, not the ones you hear while you're actually playing the game.  Since there are only a handful of different spoken lines, it can get annoying to hear your pilot say "Yahoo!  ...I can't believe I just said that" three times in a row on the same mission.
- [EDIT: The developer confirmed they're fixing this in a patch] Cutscenes are unskippable.  Every time you launch your ship there's a 10-second cutscene and you'll be seeing it a lot.  There's also a 20-30 second cutscene before every boss battle.  Since you often need to repeat boss battles several times, it'll start to get on your nerves.
- Tower balance could still use a little fine-tuning.  Rarely do you need the lighter versions of turrets once you have the stronger versions unlocked.  Some constructions and special abilities never seem to be useful or practical, while others seem much too powerful - for example, the heavy laser's Death Ray ability can one-shot pretty much any boss ship and only costs a tiny amount compared to how much you'll have saved by the end of a level.
Overall though these are minor annoyances.  It's an excellent game for a very good price.  You'll get easily 20+ hours out of it if you want to 5-star every mission.

After you run through the game once, your character becomes a myth, and the overall story isn't any particular conflict, but to maintain a cultural memory of the events and people who are important.
There's some great humor, lots of subtle interactions that you learn to optimize are you re-play the game, and the actual gameplay is easy to learn but with a bit more depth than appears on the surface. It's not grindy, which I appreciate. The music is generally great, although I suggest mixing up your locations a bit to change the soundtrack on occasion. The graphics aren't good, but they are pretty and thoroughly appropriate and I adore them.

Most visual novels I've been through was voiced in Japanese and I've heard not so good things about any of them being voiced in English but this one was wonderfully voiced in English.
Now for the characters. Most of time I'd see a romance option I'd be okay without. I didn't have one in this, I needed to be with them all. I know, I'm a ♥♥♥♥♥. Anyway, the romance options was a difficult phase, I was stuck between the French flirty blonde or the fiery aggresive red head in the end (I chose Kaori. She won my heart with that soft side and let's admit, anime. Girls enjoying anime is an instant 6/10 with only being able to score higher to me.)
The story was new to me. I'm not really into Mech or sci fi things, I enjoy the classic magic and steel sort of theme. But this thing got me wanting to play some Mech games, so big big plus. While the story is predictable in some things it doesn't make it any less enjoyable. Who wouldn't want to be in a family of wisecracks? And the numerous references makes the game memorable imo because you'll always remember the references you catch.
In the end, I would strongly recommend this game to anyone seeking to look into visual novels. Easily and I mean EASILY one of the best ones Steam has to offer. I apologize for the poor formatting, I don't understand a thing in it and I don't do reviews often.

Let's not beat around the bush. This game is flawed. Massively flawed, in fact. For a game that many waited almost a decade for, a game that promised to be the ultimate simulation of evolution and life itself, the final product is a bit of a mess. It's an entertaining mess, don't get me wrong, but some design choices seem questionable. Of course, I had just turned 10 when this game was released almost a decade ago, and had no idea about any of this. I was just a kid who saw a game where I could play god and lead some microbes on the path towards becoming an interstellar empire, and I was instantly sold. This game can be really fun, and it holds a lot of memories for me, but it comes off more as an interesting experiment than it does a fantastic gaming experience. It's definitely worth a look though. Perhaps you won't find the same enjoyment that I got out of this game in my childhood, but I don't think it should be overlooked. Perhaps I'm being a bit sentimental, but I can't really bring myself to hate or even dislike this game in any capacity.

The game has it's share of bugs, that's for sure. But honestly, what game doesn't! A lot of people who dislike this game dislike it for the grind, and to them I say I agree with you. The game highly focusses on the grinding aspect. If you want a new gun you're going to have to grind for it. Myself, I have hundreds of hours in this game, and I can tell you that the grind isn't something you have to do, it is skipable. You can do this in 2 ways. 1. Buy gold and boost (The game isn't pay to win, but I'll get back to that) 2. You can use the starter rifles! (They're seriously good!) If you don't want to do either of these things, then you'll have to grind but that's fine. Now, a lot of people say that the game is pay-to-win, and I can say that it definitly isn't. You can buy gold, and you can use it to boost for better weapons, but you'll only be putting yourself at a disadvantage. You see, the devs added a feature that makes certain guns put you into a certain type of match making grouop (Bronze, silver or gold). If a player were to boost for a gun and got themselves into gold match making, they would be playing against experianced players that would be beating them over and over. The same goes for tanks and planes. With that said, it's not even worth buying gold to boost, since it's very expensive. There is plenty of better things to do with gold. Now, I personally love the game play. Given, there is a lack of content and the devs need to add more guns, tanks, planes ect. But when it comes down to the game, it's very fun. The maps are vast and interesting, and the gameplay is enjoyable. There is good reason to play all the classes. One thing though, this game is way more fun with friends. The devs have been tweeking the squad system to make it rather enjoyable and way better than the old system. All in all, I definitely recommend this game. But again, it is a WIP, and it is a free-to-play indie developped game, so don't take it as the final product and do expect updates and changes!

Huniepop is a fun game though probably not one you want your family to walk in on you playing. Despite it looking like a mere joke of a game, let me tell you how fun and addicting it really is.
Story: The story is about what you'd expect from a game like this. Your a socially awkward loser (male or female) who can't pick up da hoes. One night your in a bar, once more trying to swoon women when one approaches you. After botching an attempt to flirt her you head home. She meets you at your apartment where she reveals herself to be a love fairy who is going to help you get laid. She hands you a device to track (stalk) all the hot women in town and its your job to meet up with them, flirt with them, feed them, take them on dates, and then have sex with them. That's it, that's the whole game, and it couldn't be any better.
Overall Score for Story: 9/10
Gameplay: So you probably already know that this is a match 3 game. However its able to stand out from other titles in its genre. Some differences include the various power ups, items, and anime girls that accompany you on your journey to become a pro playa. Its pretty addictive and it gets pretty difficult as well. You'll start off by visiting a girl, feeding her food, and then taking her on a date which is where the match 3 part of the game comes in. You'll begin with 20 turns and all your equipment in your inventory. Matching three or more of the Talent, Sexuality, Flirtation, and Romance will award you with the points you need to complete the level. Matching the Passion tokens will increase your score multiplier while matching the Broken heart tokens will decrease your overall score. The joy tokens will give you additional turns based on how many are on the board and the sentiment tokens will give you the points to activate your abilities. While it sounds a bit overwhelming now, its introduced very slowly and is easy to learn.
Overall Score for Gameplay: 9/10
Graphics: This game is very aesthetically pleasing and memorable. All the characters are very well drawn and they fit in nicely with the environments in which they inhabit. The visuals are very colorful and the design for the characters ensures that no one is too much like another, and the various hair designs and costumes make them stand apart even more. On top of all this, there are some beautiful particle effects that appear whenever you match the tokens in game.
Overall Score for Graphics: 9/10
Characters: The characters are pretty cool with a few exceptions but that's more of a personal preference. There's characters for everyone and you'll more than likely find several that resonate with you. Not only that, but a few of them are just downright funny and will give you a few good laughs.
Overall Score for Characters: 9/10
Soundtrack: The soundtrack is surprisingly good. Every area of the world has its own unique and memorable track that plays while your there. It's seriously something you could listen to by itself which is likely why the OST is sold by itself. To be completely honest, there really isn't a bad track in this game.
Overall Score for Soundtrack: 9/10
Sound: The sounds in this game, while minimal, make it a much more satisfying affair. Whenever you match some tokens, they make a sort of gush-crush sound which sounds amazing when you go on huge combos. Other from that every time you access something in the menu or inventory there's a simple, yet fulfilling sound that accompanies.
Overall Score for Sound: 10/10
In the end, what appears to be a joke game that you will play for 5 minutes and then stop actually happens to be one of the best match 3 games on Steam. If your not into match 3, you may just consider this game for the waifus and the laughs you will get. This game is definitely worth the $9.99 but goes on sale every once in a while for $2.50. Either way though, this game is rock solid and will definitely be a memorable experience.
Overall Score for Game: 9.1/10

You control two brothers, and the method of control is quite genius (and the reason a 2-stick controller is HIGHLY recommended, although it is possible with two hands on a keyboard).  The left stick and trigger control the older brother, the right stick and trigger controll the younger brother.  Using this method, you must employ teamwork to overcome obstacles whilst searching for a cure for your father's illness.
Nothing about the game is particularly difficult to beat, but it's one of those rarities where it's more about the journey.  The story takes the brothers through some fantastical areas, meeting an assortment of characters - some kind, some not so.
A smattering of boss encounters require some simple but effective teamplay from the brothers.
Whilst the two-sided controls can be confusing at times (I found it helped to keep the older brother on the left, as he controlled with the left stick), this only adds to the impact at a late point in the game, where older brother must guide younger brother from afar in one of the most touching moments of videogame in a while.
It was a terrible shame when the game came to an end so soon after beginning, but I will certainly have no reservations about buying a sequel should one come about.

Wow.. I cannot find the best way to explain my experience from this game, but I have been moved and feel unable to truly express what a gem of a game this has been for me. The steam winter sales of 2013 had Brothers on sale and not having heard of it, I decided to watch the trailor.. Already I felt "This looks like it'll be good", and I instantly snagged myself a copy. I installed and played Brothers in one sitting, unable to stop myself from progressing through the game.
I felt such intrigue and splendor as I navigated the beautiful levels and explored some of the secrets and easter eggs hidden in each world. The main characters themselves, Nyaa and Naiee are loveable but disticntly different. The older Naiee is mature and respectful whilst the juvenile Naiee is cheeky but adoreably curious all the same. And despite the fact that all the dialogue in the game is in tongue, the body language and emotions portrayed by the characters alone is more than enough to understand.
My only qualm with this game is that it felt that it cut short too quickly.. And the hope I had towards the end of the narative didn't come true, yet I can accept it. I just wish I wasn't feeling so.. robbed of my happiness.. Regardless of this though, the loss any player might feel as the tale of two sons concludes, the grief felt is shouldered by the in game characters and it's hard to not feel like you the player aren't there with them mourning.
What ever the case, the journey and excitement of Brothers makes it truly a game experience I won't forget, and one I hope everyone can share and be a part of. I've been moved to the point where I already purchased a second copy for a friend's wishlist. Have fun playing "Brothers"!

If you're into Tower Defence games (TD) then this is the game for you. Whereas normally creep travels through your tower maze and gets obliterated by your defences, Space Run takes this concept and reverses it. You pilot a cargo spaceship equipped with weapons and defence systems and have to deliver urgent cargo.
By destroying foes you get money and can upgrade your ships weapons and stuff. This is often necessary in order to beat the levels. The game is quite stressful since there are some RTS elements included (e.g. changing the alignment of your gun). Sometimes there are some nasty difficulty spikes, especially if there is a pirate to combat.
The story may be forgettable but the replay value is quite high, since you'll want to get all the possible stars, right. Graphics are okay, nothing to write home about, though. To sum things up: this is a nice, fun and easy accessible game, that is hard to beat if you're a completionist, but rather easy if you don't mind third places.

Space Run is a nice revamp on standard tower defense games. Instead of having a static playing field, you build your modules on a ship where the danger can elevate in an instant. Because there are few breaks in-between waves and no pause feature, things can get hectic pretty fast, but I think that adds to the overall fun of the game! The game is a little glitchy, but it's nothing too bad that will mess you up in a fight. If you're into tower defense games, you will like this!
Very fun game. It's like a tower defence game but in space and on a moving ship that changes size on each level :)

Overall, a really fun game with decent difficulty. All the weapons and what-not are well balanced, so you'll often find yourself using a different tactic on each level instead of finding one overpowered combo and yawning your way through the game. Definitely a must have if you're a tower-defense junkie like myself.

Ater all negative reviews I've seen, "Nux" comes off as a pleasant surprise. Presentation is pretty unique with all plasticine stuff and quirky humour. The game itself is very old-school in a good way. Each planet (which represents a level) has 3 stages: typical vertical scroller shootem'up,  landing on a planet, and a basic platformer mission on the surface, when you have to retrieve 3 diamonds and get them to your spaceship. Difficulty level is just right, and mouse control actually works well. It's not punishing, but chasing high scores is actually fun. I wouldn't go as far as saying "Nux" is a hidden game, but it can be fun for a while, and certainly worth it if you can get it on sale.

Salutations fellow Steam community members! This was my first time ever playing or buying a visual novel and I was thoroughly impressed at the amount of content ACE Academy offers. I haven't quite played all the routes quite yet (only finished one so far), but I couldn't resist leaving a review before I went back and do the others.
~ The game does reuse scenery quite a bit
~ So far I have done one playthrough of many to come and I am currently sitting at about 7 hours of gameplay for time estimate
~ I bought this game when it was on sale
~ The voice acting is pretty decent, but it is as most of the other reviews say "It's just there to help with atmosphere." I certainly agree it does!
~ I did notice a few grammer issues like past-tense and pretense errors during my gameplay, but should not annoy you too much if you aren't strict about grammer
~ The art style is modern/contemporary and is easy to adapt to
~ The music really kicks in at the appropriate times working with the other elements of the gameplay to create that comedic, serious, or warm moment in time

I like VN but I love combat. If you want combat with a lot of depth this is not for you. If you want a VN with combat here and there then this is a good option. I bought the game because it's on sale and I was curious to how little combat this has. And the combat is basically Quick Time Events where you choose the right choice in the standard middle of the screen dialouge options with a timer on the side. To be honest, it works really well to simulate fast paced combat. The only down side is that you can't customize Eagle, your mech. But I guess it would be a lot of work to implement an actual combat system with stats and inventory. If ACE Academy have that I would give it 5 stars.
However since it is a VN you can't just review it based on a side activity. The meat of the game is the VN elements and that I would give it 5 stars for. The English voice acting is excellent, although 2 of the characters sound a bit similar. The character CGI is beautiful, the writing is great, and the cute emotion-speech-bubble to highlight what the character is feeling is a nice addition. The writing though is what sets it apart from other VN games I have tried. The game doesn't take itself too seriously, so you have jokes and memes aplenty which not many VNs implement which is a shame. Here are a few of those memes, various alternate movies and tv shows, a certain ultimate from an edgelord from a very popular team-based first person shooter, and a globally famous meme from Dragon Ball. You can also name 1 of your own special attack and I legit named mine Falcon Punch :D
So this is a solid VN game with pseudo QTE combat which is great, but with a customizable mech, it could have been perfect. 9/10 would play again.

A charming story well told. Steers clear of saccharine in the main, and has some truly poignant moments. Pace is gentle and the puzzles not hugely challenging, but as long as you are prepared to immerse yourself in the story and enjoy the scenery, you will have an enjoyable ride. The 'single player co-op' generally works well. I was slightly sceptical of how well controlling one brother with each stick would work, but had few problems. Generous checkpointing means even clumsy play is not very harshly penalised. I would have enjoyed a true two player co-op experience (with harder puzzles), but was pleasantly surprised at how well the mechanics worked. The game is fairly short, perhaps 3-5 hours, but I did not feel short changed. Overall if you are in the mood for a switch in pace after some frantic RTS or FPS, you could do worse than give this a try.

This game is short, very short, I finished it in just over 3 hours and I was taking my time in places to look at the scenery and enjoy the music, so if you're looking for a lenghty game this isn't it.
However that being said it probably has one of the most well executed storylines I've seen in a game thus far and the way the conrols are designed made me feel connected to everything that was happening on the screen.
For the price it's currently at £3.59 I can't recommend it more, just to experience the story and to be happy that you did is worth more than that price In my opinion.

I should be noted I played this game well before I got steam, so the gameplay hours is a bit misleading.
Spore is one of those games that was just too hyped up for what it was. For many the game was a dissapointment because of overblown promises and lost features in it's early days. What was promised as being one of the most ambitious universe sims at the time ended up being more like five seperate minigames with some online connectivity. If you are looking for some deep and complex strategy game with deep meaning and infinite replayability you aren't going to enjoy what Spore has to offer.
That out of the way, I still reccomend this game for everyone else.
Given the price it is at now in 2017 (the year I reviewed this game) It's a pretty fair deal for what you get. Maybe when this game came out it wasn't worth the price of a full game. But with the lowered price and tendency to go on sale pretty regurally it's a great game to pick up and have fun with for a couple dozen hours. For a creative mind the game provides hundreds of combinations in everything from the creature you make to the buildings and vehicles they will drive. And while the Online portion is dead (at this stage that's just a given) the game still offers increible potential.
So while it may not be the legend it was played out to be back nearly a decade ago Spore is still a pretty fun game. Perhaps if you want something to do on some rainy afternoon and need a pick up Spore is an excellent option. A lighthearted and simple game that will offer many hours of gameplay and some decent replayability.

Whenever I buy a new addon, I try my hand with it first, then go look at the manuals. If I still don't know how to do something, I will look at Railworks America, an amazing forum and great resource for enhancing Railworks. DTG/RSC addons are usually OK, but acuracy is often lacking and are occasionally overpriced. The TS Classics catagorization was a great addition and well needed fix for the prices of many DLCs. To decide if you should buy a DLC, look for reviews and videos. If you don't like the style of railroading captured on DLCs available on steam, look towards forums and other Railworks comunities and see if the type of railroading you crave is found there.

To begin, I have had DCUO on OS3 for roughly 4 years with 800 hours played and on PS4 with about 100 hours.  Recently, I started is on PC and it is no different from console versions, so this review will apply to any system.  That being said, DCUO is a toss up in terms of well crafted, F2P MMOs.
For quite a time, Sony owned and maintained this title to be excellent.  Recently, it was sold to Daybreak and has struggled to maintain it's life.  People will call this game "Pay to win" and in some aspects, it makes sense but truthfully it isn't.  End game content can have some "flavor of the month" powers but for most solo and story play, all powers and roles are perfectly viable.  There is no distint "best power" in the game.

That being said, 6 are free at the beginning with 7 more being available as DLC for $35 for them all.  I have purchased all the powers and find that, though each is unique and requires different play styles, none are remotely required for PvE or PvP.
The game is notoriously buggy as of late (last 6 months), which is mainly due to DayBreak not maintaining QA and failing to listen to consumers.  They are still producing monthly content that is pretty good as far as story goes, so that's a plus.

Speaking of story, the one in this game is fantastic as well.  It incorporates DC's best heroes and really make good use of many of them.  If you're looking for a F2P MMO, this is never a bad one to play, but content is slightly hindered with pricewalls, even if they don't stop completion of the main story.

I'm terribly split when it comes to Space Run, but in its current form, I have to lean towards not recommending this game.  In its addictive fun is frustration wrought by issues not dealing solely with the genre itself.
The good: Reverse tower defense!  I've always enjoyed a good TD, and despite its issues, this is still a very fun game; ever since playing old TD mods on Warcraft 3, I have immensely enjoyed the ever mounting challenge that they always seem to provide, and this game is no exception as the challenges come from outside as well as within.  That may come across as being hypocritical seeing as how I don't recommend it, but please, continue reading.
The bad: Unbalanced modules.  Save your space credits and don't invest in anything except laser cannon, heavy laser turret, force field, and all of the utility modules.  Why?  Use laser cannons until you can buy heavy laser turrets (despite their extra range, missile weapons cannot hit small targets), use force field because most everything will be dead from your heavy laser turrets by the time they fail (and if they do, just recharge them), and the utility modules allow for quite a bit of flexibility (e.g. fitting in power or engine modules in tight spots).  The rest of the modules either take up too much precious space on your ship or they lack the adaptability necessary to get you through missions.  Once you realize this, you'll quickly find that your reputation unlocks a plethora of items that you'll never use and/or upgrade, you'll be swimming in space credits after a few hours that you'll spend on modules only for the sake of spending them, and there's a disturbing lack of options for new tactics and module positioning when you restart missions.
The ugly: Well, I just said it: restarting.  What makes me say that?  Because you'll be restarting the same missions over.  And over.  And over.  And over.  It will get to the point where one module might get blown up because you were too slow or an asteroid will get too close to the ship and you may as well just restart right then and there.  Did you just invest eight minutes in that mission?  Start over from the beginning, however, because you lack a wide array of useful modules (try using an advanced defense complex against a huge asteroid or a heavy missile system against small pirate bombers) to change things up, you're inevitably stuck using the same setup again and again.  And that eight minutes?  No big deal?  Eight minutes here, three minutes there, five minutes from yonder... they add up faster than you would think.  Without any save option or checkpoint system or even a fast forward button, you have to plod along through the gauntlet from square one every time.  Don't misunderstand me; I've died thousands of times while playing Dark Souls, but every time you do, you can almost hear the game saying (maybe even taunting) "I know you can do better than that", but this game?  All I hear is "Well, sucks to be you".
Space Run has the makings of a great game.  Robert Clotworthy (the voice actor of Starcraft's Jim Raynor) is the voice of the main character, the graphics are simple yet aesthetically pleasing, and each company's cargo you carry brings its own unique set of challenges in order to shake things up a bit.  I'm two missions away from finishing the game, and while I've had my fun, I feel no compulsion to go back to get reputation stars I missed on earlier missions let alone replay the entire game.  If the game developers fix the shortcomings (maybe even throw in a "Survival: Endless" mode à la Plants vs Zombies where you can build your own ship sans cargo and just get wave after wave of pirates sent at you where you're forced to recycle modules in favor of ones that can handle particular enemies better), I'll come back to waste more of my life having fun with this game, but as it is now, save your money and hope that this gets the tender loving care it deserves.

It's tower defense with a different facade.
Position your weapons carefully; in addition to choosing the right weapon you have to take firing arcs into consideration.  Turrets cannot be upgraded directly, however they do have special abilities that can be activated at a cost.  Timing those abilities can be a huge difference maker.
Most tower defense games revolve around killing the enemy quickly.  Space Run takes a different approach, it's about arriving at your destination as fast as possible with all of your cargo.  Thus you'll have to balance adding engines and other defenses such as shields and anti-missle turrets in order to get the best possible score.
Your reward for success is reputation and money.  Reputation unlocks missions, weapons and upgrades.  Money is required to purchase those upgrades.  These unlocks include new turret types, faster engines, special abilities you can use in-game or flat passive bonuses that make a certain turret more effective.
One thing that keeps things interesting is varying types of cargo.  Some cargo simply needs to make it there in tact, other cargo introduces new difficulties such as draining nearby modules so they're harder to power, or modules that must be connected by the end of the map (costing you space and resources).   When carrying nuclear warheads you even have the option to use one of them on the enemy, though doing so will cost you as that warhead can't be delivered for obvious reasons.
Overall, it's fun.  My biggest complaint is it's too easy. I've gotten a perfect score the first try on most missions, the remaining ones have been a narrow miss.  There's also little to replay and unfortunately weapons just aren't varied enough.  In general building whatever the best weapon you have access to is the right decision.  Maps also have a tendency to favor sending enemies in from one direction, it makes planning your build up rather easy and predictable.  Additionally, while the game offers something like 30 maps they tend to feel very redundant.
Expect to get about 10 hours out of it, 20 if you're struggling and have to replay a lot.

Life Goes On is one of those games where a small, simple concept really carries the game through the whole experience. The idea that you need to die to use your own corpse to get through a puzzle is really cool. Most of the puzzles force you plan a few steps ahead to strategically die in one spot to use that corpse later. The puzzles hit a sweet spot where they're not so tough that they leave you crying in frustration, but are hard enough that you'll need a few tries to see the solution, giving you a solid sense of satisfaction when you do solve it.
The game has a lot of charm and great sense of humour. It's pretty self-aware of how morbid it's core concept is and takes more than a little delight in punishing the main characters over and over again. I laughed out loud a couple of times.
Most players will finish the game in a single night, which is fair value for the price. I like games in which you can have a full experience in a single sitting. In that sense it reminds me of Thomas was Alone and similar indies. Each level has extras challenges and a target number of deaths needed to get to the end. I found myself replaying levels to try different tactics to avoid piling up bodies as a brute force solution to a puzzle.
The only complaint I have is that jumping feels a little loose at times. There's a particular sequence with ice blocks that I felt held me up because I had trouble sticking my jumps, not because I hadn't solved the puzzle. Beyond that, it also feels like the game shows you most of its ideas around 75% of the way through. Even so, I suggest sticking it through to the end because the final level for each world is epic and a great example of using level design to tell a story.

"Life Goes On" is an inventive, charming, morbid, and challenging game. If you like having your ingrained habits turned upside down, this game is for you. I felt very similar to the way I felt when learning to play Braid. It forces you to think about your character's impact on the world in completely new ways. Am I a monster for throwing away the lives of loyal knights like used tissues? Yes. Am I having lots of fun doing it? Darn right. Get this game.

A nice and full of humor game where you transplant human (and alien) organs at surgery, in ambulance in motion, at space station (and on Mars, and who knows what they will add more in next updates) by controlling surgeon's hand. Despite "Simulator" in the game's title, no 100% realism is intended, but only fun.
It's also a game which teaches you how to use the mouse differently, i.e. after playing it constantly for 2-3 hours you have hard time switching back to the normal "point & click / double click" mode for some 5 minutes.
People either love it or hate it, and the most hate comments are about "impossible" to handle game controls, which your can actually get used to after a short time (keys can be redefined if that helps). You can always test whether you will like the controls on the Game Jam prototype / demo of the game, which is available for example at developer's site.

Moon Hunters is the first roguelike I’ve really enjoyed.
How will you be remembered?
The premise is simple: the moon disappears, and you have five days to find out what happened. Once those days are up, whether you succeed or not, the game “ends.” Much like The Legend of Zelda: Majora’s Mask, only you cannot reset the time limit. You will see a “bad” ending multiple times, but things play out a little differently each time; based on your actions and decisions, you unlock constellations (which are often new characters and world types), as you play, and no two playthroughs are the same. As you progress, you will eventually reveal more of the story as told by an old priestess, and even unlock a very challenging battle arena. Your story is reflected by your own personality, in many ways, through those you aid and how you respond to conversations. The developer has described this as a “personality test RPG.” The end result of your playthrough is reflected on this idea. Your ending, and the constellation’s history, are relayed to you by the old priestess, giving that character a personality of its own.
It is often compared to Zelda or Diablo, though, to be honest, other than a few similar gameplay elements, I don’t really see the resemblance. It is a dungeon crawler of sorts, with plenty of enemies, but no loot save for currency, no hookshot or bombs, etc, and your abilities are fairly limited to just three attacks/moves. You also do not level up or obtain new gear, but instead your stats increase based on how you play. Each character has different move sets, much like those of Diablo. This adds a level of challenge to gameplay, and depth to character progression. In a way, it’s based on how your character’s personality develops. For example, you can increase stats through dialogue options. Stats also increase through actions between stages, when your characters are camping for the night. You get one choice, as the usual; for example, you can add to your stamina by watching over your camp, or upgrade your strength by hunting. Sleeping also benefits you, as often you will encounter spirits and people who may come to aid you. It is even possible to gain animal allies as well, if you play your cards right. As you have only five days, your character progression is limited, and does not carry over to new games. However, I do believe this is intended as part of the challenge and gameplay, though it would be nice if some stats carried over. Again, this heavily influences the ending and history for that character, making each playthrough unique.
If you aid wild creatures, they may return later to aid you in your quest.
The fun part is discovering different events and people as you play each time. A playthrough takes about 30-45 minutes, so it’s great for quick gaming sessions. It does offer a lot of content, and while I’ve played a few hours, I’ve only unlocked around four or five characters and several world locations. The choices you choose when “creating” a character influence the setting of your quest, as well as lore, enemies, and people you encounter.
One of the selling points of Moon Hunters is that it offers online multiplayer. Getting into it is a bit of a challenge, as the system requires you to obtain a lobby code from a friend, or to share yours if you’re hosting a game. There is a Discord server dedicated to finding other players to join (check the Steam discussion boards). The multiplayer option seems a bit daunting at first, but I do think if you can get past that, it’s a rewarding experience.
All in all, it is quite a fun game. The graphics are beautiful, and the story is very well-written. Dialogue is quite descriptive, weaving an imaginative world and colorful characters. You’ll often meet new people with each playthrough, giving more back story to the world and its people.

Here’s a decently lengthy gameplay video I made:
Yes, I know, I’m not very good at this, but to be fair, this was my third time (I think) playing. Single-player can be difficult. I do think it depicts the game very well and it speaks for itself. It’s quite long, as it is a complete playthrough, so I recommend watching the first couple minutes at the very least to get an idea of what’s in store for you.
Pros:
A fun roguelike with straightforward, easy-to-pick-up gameplay
Good, challenging fun
Great for quick gaming sessions
Nice pixel graphics and music
A different experience every time with a wide variety of characters to unlock
A unique “personality test” feature which is based on your actions and choices each time you play, shaping your experience and character’s history
Cons:
Multiplayer games can be a bit difficult to start/join in
Previous character progression doesn’t apply to main game, except to the arena
Limited time to progress and improve character stats
I’d say the cons are far outweighed by the pros, as I’m really just nitpicking. The gameplay mechanics are growing on me. Long story short, I highly recommend Moon Hunters.

The pros of this game are many:

- The art, music and graphics all are wonderful.
- The universe, writing and themes are well crafted and left me thinking about stories, gaming and culture.
The cons are fewer:
- The "personality test" component is somewhat shallow and can sometimes feel arbitrary.  Whether or not you choose to pray at a statue or observe a statue can mean the difference between bravery and foolishness.
- The short-ish gameplay is convenient, but it does make me feel like I only got to play with a fully realized character on one or two missions.
- The game works best with more players; it is difficult to play casually alone.
If you have one or two friends who would play a 30ish minute game with cool art, themes and strategy, this is the game for you.

Space Run  features high speed spaceship combat that plays out much like a puzzler. You’ll spend your time lining up your weapons and powering your thrusters all to protect your cargo and make it to the end to collect your pay. It does this beautifully by fusing an unlock system both during delivery and between deliveries all while begging you to think ahead while the alarms are screaming that another set of enemies are on their way.
The unlock system is impressive. It features laser guns, rockets, point defense, shields, disabling cannons, warp drives, healing generators and each of these has a variety of special attacks and moves. You might for example enjoy a laser gun that can be reoriented over one that has an incredible rate of fire. It also pairs nicely with the games 30 deliveries. When you finish missions you’ll be given money depending on your score. You can use that to purchase or upgrade existing weapons. As you unlock new weapons you also unlock new deliveries with unusual and often times very hazardous cargo that could explode or shut off your shields. This means that the entire time you’ll play Space Run the game will be ramping up the complexity. By the end you’ll be able to appreciate going from just a ship with three or so lasers and some thrusters to fighting hundreds of enemies with dozens of ship defenses all while under the clock.
The clock and indeed the overall method and means by which you plan is worth giving Space Run a shot. It asks you to look at your ship, anticipate where attacks are coming from, put your cargo and defenses in way to defend them both from the immediate threat of incoming ships and the long term ability to fend off future attacks. But this isn’t just some planning game. As I mentioned before all your weapons have special abilities. You will have to get used to running your ship to defend yourself. You’re not merely watching a well planned defense, you’re executing it.
Which leads me to the sticking points. For example you might beautifully crush all your forward facing opponents but then found you’ve spent all your resources and are now unable to defend yourself from the rear. Or you might have proved an excellent defense but unable to make your delivery in time. This is of course is fine and certainly better than being too easy but the game has a tendency for deadly “gotcha” moments. Retrying with a different setup is often fun but eventually it loses it’s charm. You’re not given the opportunity to immediately try again. You’re given the opportunity in about 3:00. It’s short but it definitely could use some check points. I do have to say however knowing the level means knowing the route which does seem thematically appropriate.
If you like short puzzlers with a good dose of action and planning then you’ll have fun with this one. That being said it’s 30 levels are a bit too short for the current asking price of $14.99. You’ll probably get five stars on all levels in about 20 hours and that’s heavily replaying the levels. I recommend this game at $10.

This game is a fun little physics based puzzle game that has you valiantly send brave knights to their deaths so that they can help the next knights solve the puzzle!
Basic game premise is that you need to retrieve the golden chalice on the level while avoiding the various hazards. Thing is, the hazards typically require you to kill one of your knights in a creative way so that a future knight can take advantage and proceed further along on the puzzle.  Mix in a twist of some dark humor and it's a fun experience that is easy to play in brief or longer sessions.
It also provides additional challenge modes such as completing with fewest deaths in certain amount of time to add some replayability.
It's morbidly hilarious at times with some good puzzle progression to get you thinking about how to use mechanics culiminating in some interesting and well designed puzzles by the end!

The mechanics of this game force you to think of your character in a very expendable and hilarious way. Some of the solutions are diabolical in what you have to do to yourself so the next you can win. (That last sentence got away from me.)

If you don't like puzzle games at all, you're not likely to enjoy this game. If you do like puzzles (or at least open to the idea) then read on! The difficulty of the puzzles ramps up nicely so you'll likely find some challenges in later levels, but not overly frustrating ones. The game also provides achievements beyond just finishing the levels, for those wanting more brain teasing. And the game just oozes charm, with its cartoonish knights (taking some of sting out of what is actually a pretty macabre game... a dark sense of humor may help) and death traps. One of my favorite things is the roster of, often silly, names at the bottom that get steadily crossed out as you kill more of your knights.
It has an expansion coming too, which likely means I'll be revisitng the game myself soon. Thumbs up!

Ace Academy was definetly did well in sticking out among the other, "usual" visual novels out there, as it has full english voice acting and overall just feels a little more western inspired then most.
I have to admit that the story was really enjoyable, the charcters were entertaining enough, but sometimes came across a little cookie cutter, particularly Kaori and Valerie, oh and Mayu. The rest are passable. Yuuna best girl, yeah I said it, fight me in real life.
The voice acting was a big part of the enjoyment for me, it was a welcome new addition, seeing as all the voice acted VN's on steam are spoken in Japanese. No offence to sub watchers, I just prefer dubs. Anyways the overall quality of the VA I felt was kinda low, I know that the people who made this are an indie company and you gotta start somewhere, but there were times when I heard echo, some of the lines could have been delivered a little better, hopfully there next game will be a little more refined in the VA department.
Now I want to talk about all the choices and stuff. I was pretty let down by the abrupt ending, it felt like they where way behind and had to just push the game throught. They dident have to tie everything up in a little bow, I just would of liked a little more closure on everything, end the game on a more imperative note. Maybe i'm just salty because I dident "get" with any of the girls because I spread my time out with a bunch of different people.
The visuals are nice to look at, I don't think as nice as some of the other ones you can play on steam, but still ok for a indie company, I thought that the pictures of the mechs where pretty cool so I will give them props for that. This was clearly a passion project for the individuals involved in making it.
Overall, I think you should give this game a shot. It will keep you busy for about 4 hours give or take, depending on how fast you read, and as comes with all the things associated with VN, a nice escape from reality into a world of cute girls and giant mech suits, even though it does have its faults, I gaurentee you will find yourself chucking over some of the jokes and references, and having a fun time finding your waifu.

Match-3 games are addictive little time wasters and I love them. Though, I like the kind with a little more meat on their bones, that is to say – a story. On the Nintendo 3DS I simple loved the ‘Puzzle Quest’ series, which throws in some RPG elements into the mix and a great story. Sometimes, there are exceptions that don’t have to have a story for it to be good, something like ‘10,000,000’ is a great example of this, because it is very much action driven.
Hunie Pop is one that puts a dating sim into the mix. You win over the ladies by matching tiles, during gameplay you can give them presents, which are basically powerups that grant you certain benefits. If you reach your goal in a limit amount of moves, your approval rating with the girl goes up. Do this enough times and you can take her up to your room for some more match-3 gaming. This time, you have unlimited moves, but you have to keep up the pace of matching tiles to get her to climax and as a reward you get to keep her panties.
Yeah, so… the match-3 part is pretty solid and really well done. It’s a pain that your always have to go through the dating part. You cannot simply go to a girl and start a game, no you first have to talk to her and answer silly questions or ask even more stupid questions to her (you know, to get to know each other better). In This game I wished there was just a mode where I could play the actual match-3 game, but there isn’t.
The girls keep sending you pictures in rather suggestive, revealing postures or situations, there are also some dubious sound effects present in the game, this takes away some of the enjoyment as you almost feel guilty playing this game and wondering how you’re going to explain all this when somebody walks into the room.
It’s a shame, because the match-3 part is really good, the graphics are really well done (quality wise, I'm not commenting on the actual hentai) and the catchy music fits the game perfectly. Voice acting is equally well done, all the girls really have perfectly casted voice acting.
If you talk about a guilty pleasure, this game is it in the very literal sense of the word!
The game works well on SteamOS/Linux, it shouldn’t be very demanding so almost any setup should be able to run it. The controls are very smooth with the Steam Controller, another testament to how versatile this controller really is. I didn’t try this on the Steam Link, for obvious reasons - hentai in the living room, I think not.
