Obligatory header to the review: I focus on four primary areas whenever I review a game: gameplay, story, graphics, and sound/audio/general things that go into your earholes. Gameplay and Story get a rating scale from 1 to 10, and the AV stuff gets a rating from 1 to 5. My philosophy on this is that there are some instances in which a game may not necessarily have that much in the way of gameplay (take Amnesia for example), but the story/atmosphere/whatever it may be is reason enough to pick it up. Also, take the cumulative score with a grain of salt; it's just a numerical feeling about the game as a whole. That's part of why I do these subscores. Also, keep in mind that I'm not going off of school grade based rankings. A 5/10 denotes what I feel to be an average game. Likewise, 7/10 is a game that I think is pretty cool, and something that gets a 2/10 is near-abomination level. Pinning scores to an even further obfuscated rating scale is kinda senseless, but for the sake of my backloggery, I'll repeat again that 1.0-2.7 is a one-star game, 3.0-4.7 is a two-star game, 5.0-6.7, 7.0-8.7, and 9.0-10 are three, four, and five stars, respectively.
Gameplay: I really don't get the hate surrounding this game. Yeah, sure, it's not the same quality of game as the Itagaki-produced games, but it's still a load of fun. The gameplay is best described (in my opinion) as a cross between Devil May Cry and Rise of the Triad (actually, that's fair to say in more respects than just the gameplay). Rather than going with light attack/heavy attack/grab, the game has three different types of attack: shortsword for fast face fu- I mean wrecking; fists for punching things dead hard; and flails, which are essentially the Blades of Olympus. Along with that are some special weapons that you get from executing stronger enemies. These lead into the Element system of the game, which is really vital to grasp so that you don't launch your controller, chair, monitor, PC, and desk out the window. However, even more essential is learning how to counter.
Admittedly, countering is somewhat finicky, but I found it to be a godsend against the later bosses of the game. My biggest complaints, honestly, are the finicky countering and the camera, which can be a huge pain at times.  However, those didn't really ruin my day all that much. After beating the game, you unlock Ninja Gaiden Z mode, which is essentially a "Yaiba-lite" version that plays more like a beat-em-up game like Streets of Rage than an actual classic Ninja Gaiden game. This was disappointing, admittedly, but it's still a good bit of fun. Also, no, I haven't beaten it. I'm not good enough to do about an hours worth of gameplay on one continue. But hey, this review isn't about my gaming abilities; it's about the game, and this game is simply fun. While it's not as engaging as Ninja Gaiden Black, I still think this game is a load of fun and will definitely play through it again on higher difficulties in the future. 8/10.
Story: The Ninja Gaiden series has never been well known for being the most well-written, and I think it's about time that they embrace their incredibly camp nature. Spark Entertainment felt the same way, too. The writing most definitely got plenty of laughs out of the 12 year old inside me. The Engrish in the Arcade mode was pretty great, too, even if it is a bit of an easy joke. Unlike gameplay, there really isn't much here to talk about. If you've got an immature sense of humor, you'll probably enjoy the cutscenes and dialogue. Just don't go into it expecting Shakespeare. 7/10.
Graphics: Definitely the most striking aspect of this game. It's got that ultra-cel shaded style in the ilk of games like Madworld, Killer7, and No More Heroes, and it looks pretty dang good when you crank the settings to max. It ran near-perfectly on my GTX 760 at 1080p, max settings, and 60FPS, so if you've got a similar card, you should have pretty similar results. As for the actual art design of the game itself, some of the areas get a bit boring to look at again and again, but if you're spending that much time looking at the scenery, you're not playing the game right. Now, don't think I made those comparisons earlier in this section without intent. This game, much like the prior three mentioned, is pretty dang violent. Absurdly so. However, this helps feed into the campy nature of this game, so I don't mind it at all. Again, this is more proof that art style trumps ultra-high polygon counts most any day of the week. Your eyes will most definitely not get bored, presuming you're actually playing the game. 5/5.
Audio: This game has a pretty rad soundtrack, I must say.  The "hard encounter" theme is a bit meh, but there is some pretty good battle music throughout this game. They're songs you probably wouldn't mind working out to, if that helps give you an idea of the kinds of songs in the game. As for the voice acting, it doesn't get in the way. Nothing really that remarkable. Sound design, once again, doesn't really get in the way or make itself known all that much. For some pretty good songs, but not too remarkable anything else, the audio portion of this game gets a 3/5.
Overall: An absolutely gaudy adventure both in style and in substance that I overall had a pretty good time with. However, I'd hold off until this game becomes about $30 or so. Any higher is a bit too much in my opinion. 8/7/5/3; 7.7/10.

Ah yes, we've all heard of it, America's Army Video Game. The video game made by the US Army to encourage Americans like you and me to join the force. While I'm all for our nation's military power, this game is in fact, propaganda. But it's surprisingly fun.
The game lets you revive players. At first I thought I was about to play battlefield 3 and 4 all over again. But the devs really balanced everything. You can revive other players once, and use zip tags to secure enemies from reviving. The health system is interesting when you have to bandage your wounds or you will continue to lose health. Very small limited amount of guns, which means it's a very skill based game.
My favorite gamemode, search and destory, isn't implemented, but the modes are very similar. Both team spawn, must complete objectives, and dead players wait while spectating. Just how I like it.
It's interesting, but a lot of players actually use voice chat to communicate with other players. It looks like players that play this game are very patriotic for the American Army. Which leaves me to believe that many of these players are actually US veternans or want to be. There are even advertisements of the US Army telling you to join the military right before you enter a map. Everyone is trying to play tactically like a real soldier which is amazing. Players aren't acting dumb like it's a cod game.
But this is not a hardcore game. There are arcade features that make this game non-realistic. Recoil doesn't exist, shooting players makes you go down and then be able to revive them, and quickly patch yourself if you get shot like it's nothing. It leaves me to believe that the game acknowledges that people who are interested in joining the army are playing, so are making the game easy to make them comfortable of joining the force.
Overall: 8/10. It's a fun free game for everyone to play. But I might be worried of the chance of scouters looking for soldiers in this game to draft. They might actually draft you and me for being so good at this game. That was a joke. For the love of God, please don't actually draft me into the army.

I first played DCUO way back at launch on ps3 and while it wasn't the best mmo ever and definitely wasn't as good as city of heroes. I still thoroughly enjoyed it. Back then I would have recommended it. Now however I definitely will not recommend it. First of all I couldn't even get it to install properly. The launcher would just randomly shut down without any warning while installing. I basically had to keep opening it, it would complete about 5% of the install and shut again but I kept going out of sheer nostalgia for this game.
Eventually I got the game installed and created a character it was only then the real troubles started. The game makes all free to play users wait in a queue to join the server. The estimated wait time was 2 and a half minutes however it took 10 minutes to get it only to be instantly booted back to character select. Another 10 minute wait and I was back in the prologue only to find that the controls were absolutely atrocious. My character wouldnt turn properly, instead he'd just kind of run forward and gradually turn round while still playing the forward run animation. Sort of like the tank controls from the old resident evil games. I don't know if its a bug but I certainly don't remember movement being that clunky back on ps3.
To make matters worse if you didnt move the camera while moving the character it would just flail wildy in random directions. I tried searching online and found only one thread on steam of someone having this problem and absolutely zero solutions.
The flying controls seemed a lot more responsive so I tried to push forward only to have the camera completely disconnect from my character while i was flying. I made sure the auto follow setting was on but it didn't seem to help. It honestly felt like I was playing an alpha version of the game.
If you are a fan of DC then go ahead and try it. Maybe your experience will be a lot less buggy than mine but be smart and don't spend any money on this until you're sure it will work properly for you.

*Ughh* Where to begin....
(A list of PROs & CONs further down)
Back when this game came out I was very enthusiastic about this game, and that enthusiasm quickly turned to love. About 16-18 characters later, I must heavy-heartedly say this game was highly anticipated, flourished, and died. Maybe "was murdered" is more accurate though.
DC Universe is a perfect example of when developers make bad buisness decisions, combined with a lack of ambition to continue creating fresh, original content. This game started out strong, with one of the most detailed DC Comics-universe adaptation to date. After approx. 1 year SOE decided to dumb down the game enough to attract the broadest audience possible - the maximum character level became reachable in a matter of hours. Then, after the launch of 2 successful paid-DLCs SOE decided to make owning DLC mandatory for full end-game instances & storylines. You might be thinking "WTF" now, but it gets better.
For about 1 year, 1 paid DLC came out every 3-4 months (adding 2-3 instances, possibly a raid etc.) Not only would this DLC bring with it skill points, but also higher tiers of equipment. The last I heard the highest equipment level at the moment is 190-something (DLC required..). This essentially made the game Pay2Win.
....And as if that weren't enough of a kick in the face of every person who supported this game - they continuosly promised DLC, and commentlessly delayed (in some instances for more than 6 months), or cancelled it, and slowed down DLCs to 1-2 every 6 months. Essentially the game has been abandoned. The only reason the Servers are still running is in a futile attempt to get some money out of you.
Here are some listed PROs & CONs
PRO:
- ALOT of DC Comics Lore (very in-depth)
- great player community
- Heaps of end-game content
- Great Quests & Instances (Raids as well)
- Outstanding costume/armor system
- Great skill system (not explained well though. I recommend getting some youtube knowledge or clan)
- good PVP
CON:
- Level Progression is MUCH faster than it should be (Max level=30 -> reachable in ~5-10 hrs. depending on playstyle)
- Endgame content is extenstive, but requires either a payed monthly subscription, or MANY add-ons
- Free2Play-players have a purse cap, and inventory cap
- Linear Questlines
- Moderate replayability
- Shrinking (almost non-existant) Playerbase
- Events are constantly recycled
- Sheer number of required payed add-ons (required for "full" end-game experience)
- Devs have no interest in comics or players
Although DC Universe Online is a beautiful game with a keen eye for detail (very reminisent of the old Spider Man titles on PS1 etc.), it lost it's touch to the source material. Every add-on, every "new" feature, every event are just shallow rehashes of previous/existing content. If you are a comic fan, DC fan, or fan of any single DC superhero you should give it a go, but other than that I really can not recommend anyone start playing this game anymore. It is only a shell of what it once was.

It is amazing how this game can tell a simplistic (yet touching) story without saying a word, but story is not the only thing Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons has going for it, as this game also challenges your mind to multitask while controlling both brothers, which make the puzzles very interesting (allthough admittedly a little too easy). combine these two thing with great visuals, diverse levels and beautiful music and you have a match made in heaven.

(To all my friends that purchased this game: "You fvkin rock!")
When I am forty-years-old and I look back at the video games I have played, I will remember Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons among the greatest games of all-time.  When I think of timeless, classic video games, I immediately think of Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Super Mario 64, and Metal Gear Solid 3; video games that left a truly lasting impression on you that you won't soon forget.  Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons is a masterful piece of work that leaves you emotional, heavy-hearted, and awe-inspired.
Developers and Credits
Josef Fares is the creator and lead director of Starbreeze Studios on this project and it is worth mentioning that this is the man to follow for years to come.  There was a time when Starbreeze was one of the most talented developers out there, responsible for video games like The Darkness.  Even though not much of the original team is left, I am happy to see that they are returning to their roots.  This is a prime example of why Starbreeze creates games that defy the conventional standard that is demanded by big-house pubishers.  Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons is a love-letter to gamers and it does not miss a beat.
Storytelling
There are many games on the market that try too hard to get its point across but stumbles and fails.  Brothers is a game that says very little and it instead tells the story and narrative through visual imagery, action, and stunning sequences of events that connect with a purpose.  The characters in the video game speak "made-up" language but you can translate in your mind what they are trying to say because all words are committed with purposeful action and even inaction.  It does not "say" much but when the words do come out, they are powerful, metaphorical, and full of meaning.
If you are a thinker of life, its philosophies, and its many different viewpoints, you will appreciate this game to its core.  Brothers explores the lost of loved ones, rebirth, and transcendence.  It is a deep, thought-provoking piece of work that dares to convey ideas that most video games run away from.  When you are done playing Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons, it will steal away your heart and leave your soul very heavy.
Gameplay
The multi-faceted gameplay combines platforming, puzzles, and controls in a new and innovative way.  The platforming on the surface might not seem like anything new but due to the control scheme using twin-sticks, it changes the game completely.  You control one brother with the left stick and one brother with the right stick for movement.  This is the same for the left and right triggers, respectively.  You need to have pretty good hand-eye coordination but it is a very slight learning curve.  After a few minutes, you will ease right in without an issue.
I have not played a game with a control scheme like this, ever, and I have played hundreds of video games.  It lends itself intuitively to puzzles that are light to medium.  The puzzles require you think but they aren't headache-inducing because the point of the game is to let you enjoy a beautiful journey and memorable experience.  Puzzles are clever, smart, and they all involve the interaction and cooperation of the brothers.   This is not Uncharted or Super Mario but it combines some of those elements into the game.  Brothers consists of several different type of platforming techniques that you have not seen in any video game.  In the same light, the puzzles are unique as well.  It has never been done this way and it executes them extremely well.
The controls are very well-polished and intuitive to the point where you won't be frustrated or question it for a second.  Brothers avoids the plague of video games that are filled with hints and button tutorials that only get in the way.  It does not hold your hand.  There are no button prompts.  It asks you to understand the control scheme and play it to your problem-solving skills.  Basically, the designers does not assume that the player is stupid.  Hence why this game is a love-letter to the classic gamers.  You will appreciate this game to its fullest.  It requires you to figure things out on your own to solve well-crafted, clever puzzles that mesh successfully with the controls.
Warning:  This game is pretty much controlpad-required.  Also, vibration from the controller (I will say since a long time ago) is important for this game.  The ending will not be the same great experience without the vibration feature.  Please buy a controller.
Visuals
Have you ever read a fairy tale book that contained some of the most beautiful visual imagery ever?  A huge part of Brother's storytelling is through its visual imagery.  It is like a fairy tale told through a video game with the use of a controller.  It is absolutely stunning, beautifully intelligent, and mesmerizing.  Throughout the entire game, I thought I was under a spell cast by a Wizard standing behind me whiled I played.  At times, you will wonder why other games do not like as gorgeous as this one.
I am a very picky person when it comes to character, level, art design but I did not have one bone to pick with Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons.  Every aspect of the visual design complimented each other.  The choice of colors really plays into color psychology.  One moment, the colors are bright and hopeful, and then the game takes you through dark tones that scares you, creates tension, and tosses you into some crushing moments.  It is one of the greatest displays of color and visual imagery, along with well-polished graphics that I have ever seen in a video game.
Do the Achievements (Very Important)
Please look up the achievements online and do not worry about them being spoilers.  They are more like "sidequests" if anything but they are worth every second of your time.  I am not an achievement hunter AT ALL.  I am one of those gamers that love everything from hardcore, classic RPGs to light and fun action games, and of course indie games but I don't mind achievements as much as the next guy.  But you will want to grab all the achievements in this game and I'll tell you why in just a second.
The achievements in Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons are heartwarming, time-worthy awards that question a gamer's morality, generosity, and heart.  You could be a hero, a rascal, explorer, humanitarian, or trouble-maker.  The choice is yours.  Making the right choice will get you a cool achievement that is worth your time.  It opens up cutscenes that you won't soon forget even after finishing the game.  Do them and enjoy the memories they create.
This text box cannot contain all of my words so I will leave you with a few words of thought.  This will easily be one of the games where I look back and I will remember playing it in great detail.  From beginning to end, it captured my heart.  It is a piece of art, game, media that knows how to make use of all its forms and it executes them all very well.  The ending is extremely powerful and it will tug at your heart strings.  Not many video games let alone forms of art, media, can ask you to question life's meanings.

This game is so good and so cheap, every time it's on sale I buy gift copies for everyone I know. It's also the only game I've happily bought on or near release day at full price for two systems (PS3 and PC), and willingly suffered GFWL for. About 60% of my hours on this game are on PS3 and 39% on a non-steam retail PC copy, so this is probably my most played game ever.
If you're looking for story, stealth, or graphical fidelity, you'll probably be left unsatisfied, but this game absolutely nails gameplay, gameplay as metaphor, atmosphere and iconic imagery with a sledgehammer. The sledgehammer is absolutely the icon of this game, you really feel the crushing oppression in a ragged-edge backwater off-world colony in the quiet moments, and like an outgunned, outnumbered maniac at the end of his rope tearing apart a whole army at its foundations in the chaotic ones (even the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AI contributes to this feeling), and above all, between the bouncy vehicles, tactile destruction, responsive gunplay, hugely varied weapons and swarms of enemies, the gameplay is just flat-out FUN.
The multiplayer is endless fun when you can actually get a game, which is sadly very hard to do these days, but if you try on Wednesdays and Sundays and suffer GFWL, you can usually get a couple of rounds in.
Can't recommend enough.

This game is fun two ways:
Its a lot of fun just to put a bunch of modules on your ship and try and complete the runs. The management of your turret positions and power ups keeps you busy, but its not an insane click fest so folks with less coordination can enjoy it.
It is also not so easy to get five stars (or even four) on the levels beyond the basic ones. You really have to plan your strategy: which turrets will you use, how to position them (space on the ships is limited, and often taken up by bulky or inconvenient cargo), and managing your power ups so you have 'nuts' (money) when you need them.
It does seem that you can replay levels endlessly, which allows the player to max out every turret. It might be nice if this were limited, forcing players to choose a strategy (offense or defense) and run with it.
Worth every bit of the $10-ish it cost. I hope it makes its way to iPad. It would quickly become a favorite!

Despite the problems below, I absolutely love this game and would recommend it to anyone who likes beat-em ups, great stories and this kind of repetitive gameplay loop. Co-op is fantastic and the story is magnificent. It is a wonderfully written game with great art, level design and character design. The Voice acting is perfect, though the music is simple and after playing the game for a couple hours the snow area theme began to bother me making me avoid snow areas some times even if they had new events because the music there is awful and doesnt fit the game.
The game does have major problems though. I do still think it is a great game, but these issues need to be dealt with for it to stand the test of time.
1. BUGS. This game has all kinds of graphical, performance and gameplay bugs. Objects warping around, one of the bosses soft locked then crashed the game because his minions got stuck in some rocks, music stopping, and the swordsman's dialogue on the last day repeating every time Ive played as him. I just noticed the 'report a bug" option in the pause menu after 8 hours of play and willl use it frequently.
2. Combat: Fighting is this game is only fun with a few characters(Heduanna is the only character I can consistently feel comfortable with) and when Im enjoying the combat and I feel in control of my character its the easiest game Ive played since Pokemon. The character that feels the best feels perfect(Heduanna) but the gameplay is not balanced around her. Enemies just get stunlocked into oblivion and bosses can easily get cheesed out by her, while the rest of the cast feels awkward and deaths happen much more frequently with them because its harder to get out of dangerous situations with them.
3. Boss Battles: Going along with combat, boss battles are boring. Every boss Ive fought in the game(I believe Ive fought them all tonight) is a brick you have to hammer away at, and the difficulty is determined by your patience. Playing as range characters, no boss is a problem. Playing the melee characters however, every boss is either a pain or trivial depending on the upgrades you could afford along the way. One two subsequent playthroughs with the same character one final boss battle took 30 seconds of slamming the square button on my DS4 behind the boss, and the next took 20 minutes of dodging and quick, fearful slashes. Boss battles just arent fun.

I absolutely adore this game. It's so...arcane? Maybe that's the right word?
Mechanically it's a top-down action game with procedural map generation, character classes, upgrades, and both local and online multiplayer. Aesthetically, you play as an adventurer trying to find out what happened to the moon goddess. Along the way you go through swamps, forests, mountains, deserts, and more trying to track down clues and fighting everything from twisted, corrupted wildlife to cultists of the sun.
The game is loaded with all kinds of obscure choices. Tonight when I played, I encountered a man sitting next to a lake, gazing into a flower. I looked at the flower and saw a spider inside and I was presented with the choice to stomp or watch.
How do you respond to that? The choices shape your character's traits as well as their mechanical aspects like damage output or energy regeneration, but it's often impossible to know in advance what's going to happen and I love that. You have to respond to the situation; Would you watch the spider alongside this person you just met or would you interrupt their meditation and kill the spider? Maybe watching will bring you peace, but maybe failing to stomp the spider means the man gets bitten.
The game sends you on this quest time and time again, retelling the story in a different way each time. Through play you unlock constellations that let you start from different home towns, play as different characters, and use different costumes. I am certain there are also tons of endings that I haven't seen yet, too.
I play a lot of procedural, play-this-again-and-again games and this is one of them that I keep coming back to and keep trying to get new friends into.
Get this game and take a friend along for the ride. You'll be glad you did.

It's not DMC, it's not MGR, it's not even slasher, to be honest. This is tribute for players like me, who lost all of his money in smoke-covered bars with coin-up NEO-GEO machines. This is more like a Double Dragon or any straight-walking fighting arcade games of SNES/SEGA age. Combat system is fun, variety of combos and moves are impressive and the graphic style is nice. It's not Crysis of course, but nice, stylish look inspired by games like Killer is Dead. Main story is pretty short (you can rush the game in 4 hours), but you have many reasons to repeat all missions. There is a lot of hidden objects to find, lot of difficulties to complete, ranks and medals to earn and so on. There is even an Arcade Mode in it, when you have NES inspired HUD, and funny, static cut scenes with 8-bit graphic.
The biggest problem at the moment is price. 60 EU is absolutely too high for that kind of game. After all, this is only short spin-off of bigger franchise, aimed for a very specific kind of players. I don't regret buying this, but if you're expecting DMC clone, or even something like previous Ninja Gaiden games, just don't buy it. Buuuut, if you like arcade beat'em'ups like Streets of Rage, but with more modern design and improvments, then you can think about shopping. But IMO, wait for discount anyway.
Oh, and one more thing. I'm mad at people who complain about this game, and by the look on their Steam profiles, they don't even have it. I'm sure that they didn't even bother to play pirate copy, just judging enitre game by it's price, wich is stupid as hell. And stop comparing it with previous Ninja Gaiden games. It is Ninja Gaiden as much, as Metal Gear Rising is Metal Gear. It's spin-off, not NG4.

If you can accept the new direction of ninja gaiden, there is a really fun hack n slash with a great b-movie vibe with a colorful new look and feel to a hack n slash.
The story is about a foul mouthed ninja named Yaiba kamikaze who gets killed by series protagonist,Ryu Hayabusa. several weeks later, Yaiba is rebuilt by a corporation so that he can "stop" the zombie outbreak(yes you fight zombies, but I'll get to that later) and Get his Revenge on Ryu Hayabusa. The story is pretty basic and predictable, it ends up being really abrupt near the end.
The writing is something you ethier are gonna love or hate, personally I see the majority of the dialogue to be so bad it's good, and the humor comes from how vulgur the characters are with lines like "He's got some hot woman helping him. I'm sooo jealous. Maybe I'll kill her when I see her. Or maybe we can make out. Maybe we'll have a threesome! I'll do whatever Yaiba tells me to do. I'm so horny...". There are some geniunely funny moments like the introductions of the zombies, which is just slap stick humor at best.
The gameplay of yaiba isn't ninja gaiden, it's more like Devil may cry,rygar, or Lords of shadows. The actual combat consists of 3 weapons which are a flail(basically a chain),Cyborg arm, and your ninja sword. It takes some time for the combat to become really entertaining, when you know how the system works. You can also do executions which will you give you more health(especially usefull when upgrading to do up to 10 executions) and a counter system which when you pull it off is incredibly satisfying though it isn't that well implented as lords of shadows. You can also pick up weapons from enemies by executing them(or a mashing qte) ranging from numbchucks to electro whips to a rocket launcher, which make the combat more interesting because each enemy has their own weakness to certain elements . there is also platforming, which is on rails and quite fun for the most part.

Now the one thing that most reviewers criticize the game is the difficulty, which the game really isn't that hard if you get all the collectibles. Which there are 2 types, the first one being health shards(which combing 4 of them will increase your health),story parts and elemental resistent shards(which makes the game a hell of a lot easier to get through). I HIGHLY Reccomend you get all of them since they will make the game a lot more easier than the reviews are saying are saying it is.
Here is a video of where you can find them.

Now there are 2 flaws with this game, the first is that the game is rather short it took me around 6 hours to finish the main campaign and honestly it could have included a few more levels to make it around 8-10 hours long which would have been the perfect length for this game. The next one is the camera, which is fixed and you can't control it, however it is a improvement over the console version, which apparently is worse.
Overall the gameplay is fast paced,franic, and just good mindless fun.
The visuals are pretty solid, they are done in a cel shaded look which gives the game a comic book look to it, and I ike the designs of the zombies(and yaiba As well), since all of them are Unique, and all look drastically different. Animations are very fluent and fun to look at. The PC version also runs at 60 fps, which helps with your reaction time in the game.
Sound is pretty good, the soundtrack fits the mood of the game and has some killer tracks in there . sound effects are great especially the attack sounds when you hear the crunching sounds of zombies being ripped to shreads. Voice acting is alright, nothing really stand out and half the time I barely noticed it, but what is there is just fine.
In short, Yaiba: Ninja Gaiden Z is an enjoyable hack n slash, with a nice look and feel that you don't get from the typical hack n slash. I would reccomend the game when it's on sale, since asking for full price is too much for what is there.

UPD: After going back to this game, I am now ashamed of my past attempts to justify the game's existence. It's a bad game, even worse, it's a♥♥♥♥♥♥Ninja Gaiden game.
Of course I was excited when I found out a Ninja Gaiden game was coming to PC. Of course this excitement didn't last as I pretty much instantly found out this was not going to be a true Ninja Gaiden title. So here are my first impressions after playing first two missions:
- The game is fast, but not as fast as classic Ninja Gaiden games.
- I'm playing on Normal, and the game manages to pose a challenge sometimes. Basic enemies which attack in hordes are very easy. This is one of the things that make this Ninja Gaiden look more like a God of War title.
- No free jumping this time around. The jump button is used for dashing. Blocking and countering are still there.
- A lot of finishing/execution cut-scenes. Again, this is where the game is obviously treading into God of War territory.
- Different weapons are there, but you have to pick them from enemies, and they don't last long. A strange change but I guess it works.
- The story is cheesy in a good kind of way. Had a few smirks and grins out of it so far.
- The game looks beautiful, feels like you're watching a cartoon.
Overall, I'm enjoying the game so far. I'd be happy to play classic NG games instead, or Bayonetta, or DMC. But I'd pick Yaiba over God of War any day of the week.
I would urge you to buy the game so we can get more Team Ninja games on PC, but I have little hope for that. This game is made in UE3, which makes it easy to port unlike other Team Ninja titles. Not to mention the insane launch price and the fact that the game is absent from the top selling titles on Steam.
So, only buy this game if you are certain you'll be able to get some enjoyment out of it. If in doubt, wait for a discount. It's not that bad, it's actually pretty good. Too bad it's not really Ninja Gaiden.

Not sure why so many reviewers (IGN, Gamespot, ...and all the others except Famitsu) are giving this game such bad reviews. IMHO i think the people that played the game did not take the time to learn all the various combos and most importantly the elements system. In other words all those reviewers just plain suck at games and shouldn't call themselves gamers. They look at the few bad things and blow it out of proportion. And yes I said they are not "Gamers."
I do agree that there are some aspects of the game that can be mind-wracking, but its not as bad as you may believe. Such as the camera...Yes the camera can become an issue at some times, but all you need to do is dash out of the fray and get back to slaughtering zombies. Other reviewers complain about how some zombies are impossible to kill with out "Zombie Weapons," but that a bunch of bull...default weapons are just as viable.
With that said about default weapons, counterattacking the zombies is easy with the convenient circle indicators above their heads; just need to time your button presses right - you'll see what I mean if you buy the game.
You cannot play this game thinking it will be a true to heart/spirit/whatever...Ninja Gaiden game. It is a hack-n-slash to its core - with some SMALL RPG elements via the leveling up system and perks. Jumping around is by simple three-button quicktime events that have checkpoints in between - so don't worry about dieing during the event and having to restart the entire level. And for those combo junkies that do their best to rack up huge combos...well this is your game IMHO - just avoid getting hit. As mentioned earlier about the camera, if you get surrounded by zombies, just dash out - it works rather niceley.
Now for the animation, I love it! Not too many games these days have orginal art and animation - especially since everything these days is a got dang FPS. The whole comic book style - though not original - but what is original these days - it is still nice to see and in this case its done rather well IMHO. Animations overall are fluid - havn't experienced any stuttering or issues so far.
If gratuitous use of adult language and sexual themes offends you...then this is not your bowl of pudding....go get something a little sweeter. Yaiba and his motley crew have a bunch of sailor mouths, but I'm fine with that.
On my last note - the zombie comedy and easter eggs are pretty neat and original.
Overall, this is a recommend - Highly recommend if I could. Like any hack-n-slash, take time to learn the combos and other systems implemented. Learn your enemies' movement and patterns to know when to strike, defend, and counter. If you take time to learn, I promise the gaming experience will be much better than trying to bash your way mindlessly to death and eventuall victory.
....And for those that didn't buy the game cause the price was "too high" you're missing out on the FUN!

This is a very interesting game with a lot of fun concepts. I was actually taken completely off guard by this little game.
Story: It's about two brothers trying to find a cure for their sick father. The characters speak gibberish but that doesn't mean you dont understand them. The story line moves along at a great pace, and at 2 1/2 hours, this is what you would call short but sweet. It's an emotional rollercoaster that will play with your emotions making to chuckle at one part of the and feeling depressed in another. I suggest playing it all in one sitting or the some of the impact could be lost.
Gameplay: This is unlike any game i've played, the closest thing I can think to compare it with would probably be Ico. The left half of your controller controls the big brother and the right half, the little brother. It's essentially a 1-player co-op game, which very well could have gotten stale, but every chapter the game introduces new concepts to keep things fresh. The only negative gameplay wise I can think of, is that it can be confusing to control, you almost have to split your brain in half to control the brothers simultaneously.
Graphics: The game has rather stunning art direction. Even though technically the graphics aren't amazing, artistically, they are. There's underground jails, dark forests, arctic wastelands, among some others. Your eyes are in for a treat.
While I didn't cry or choke up during the game, I can see why others would, there's some heavy stuff in this game. The biggest negative is that, there is virtually no replayability other than tracking down the 12 achievements, but that's not what this game is about. It's less a game and more of an experience, that I think everyone should give a chance. All in all, if you're in the mood for something different and unique, I'd say give this game a go.

Mixes the tower-defence theme up a bit by putting you in control of a moving ship. Your task for every mission is to get yourself across the map as fast as possible. The faster you can do it and the more cargo you manage to bring intact, the bigger the reward. Opposing you are waves of hostile ships that can fly in from all directions and do their best to destroy you. As a player you can place turrets, engines and other modules on your ship, which all alter your craft in different ways.
The gameplay is dynamic and, unlike with similar "defence-oriented games", I never found myself waiting for the next wave or for something to do. There's always something incoming and the game is paced well enough to always keep you buys, without turning into a micromanaging click-fest. At first the game seemed fairly straightforward and simple, but som of the missions during the later half of the game actually got quite challenging.
The Positive:
- Well paced, both in terms of the actual battles as well as how you unlock and learn new things throughout the game.
- Polished, Didn't encounter a single bug during my playthrough. Graphics and sound effects are also well done.
The Negative/My Nitpicks:
- The story(to the degree there actually is one) mostly bored me. I had patience for the dialogue and banter between the characters at first, but during the 2nd half of my playthrough I found myself just skipping it all.
- There's not much to do once you've gone through all the missions, beyond maxing your score. Some sort of Survival-mode or other challenge would have been welcome.
All in all I'd highly recommend this to anyone who'd like a quick bit of fun with a strategy game. It doesn't last all that long, but it's well done and I've had good fun playing it.

Having played the first 3 hours, i really can't understand the horrible reviews this game got. I really enjoyed my time so far. It looks like a very nice spectacle fighter.
I like the art style and the cinematics. The controls are pretty good so far. You combo your attacks with 3 buttons (which is just complex enough for me). Doing big combos while being surrounded by dozens of zombies is really satisfiing, i have to say. In addition to these buttons you have a dash to quickly move (no jump btw), a block and some other actions like grabbing a zombie in order to use him as a weapon or throw him. Overall the combat feels really good. I can't complain at all.
The difficulty seems to be pretty high, but I don't mind dying a few times now and then. They could have added a few more savepoints. But that's only a minor complaint.
The camera is fixed, you cannot adjust it yourself. This will♥♥♥♥♥♥off some people. And yes, sometimes you end up in a situation where the enemies are behind the camera, where you can't see them. This can be annoying sometimes. On the other hand, you can use your right thumb purely for attacking, blocking etc. and don't have to interrupt only to move the camera. I think both systems have pros and cons. I am fine with how Yaiba handles it most of the time.
So yeah, i think it's a good game. The most important thing is that the combat feels really good, and that's what these games are all about, right? ;)

This is a very interesting game with a lot of fun concepts. I was actually taken completely off guard by this little game.
Story: It's about two brothers trying to find a cure for their sick father. The characters speak gibberish but that doesn't mean you dont understand them. The story line moves along at a great pace, and at 2 1/2 hours, this is what you would call short but sweet. It's an emotional rollercoaster that will play with your emotions making to chuckle at one part of the and feeling depressed in another. I suggest playing it all in one sitting or the some of the impact could be lost.
Gameplay: This is unlike any game i've played, the closest thing I can think to compare it with would probably be Ico. The left half of your controller controls the big brother and the right half, the little brother. It's essentially a 1-player co-op game, which very well could have gotten stale, but every chapter the game introduces new concepts to keep things fresh. The only negative gameplay wise I can think of, is that it can be confusing to control, you almost have to split your brain in half to control the brothers simultaneously.
Graphics: The game has rather stunning art direction. Even though technically the graphics aren't amazing, artistically, they are. There's underground jails, dark forests, arctic wastelands, among some others. Your eyes are in for a treat.
While I didn't cry or choke up during the game, I can see why others would, there's some heavy stuff in this game. The biggest negative is that, there is virtually no replayability other than tracking down the 12 achievements, but that's not what this game is about. It's less a game and more of an experience, that I think everyone should give a chance. All in all, if you're in the mood for something different and unique, I'd say give this game a go.

I, at one time, might have discounted or otherwise insulted this game for being gimmicky and ironic, in private, to as many people as I could rant to.  Do not vote for this game, I said, for it is just monkey cheese nonsense being sold to dumb internet people.  But somewhere between not enjoying the demo and receiving the full version, this game grabbed me between it's shaky noodly fingers.  Between the awkward controls and the wonky physics is a game that actually works under it's own weird set of rules.  Sure you might drop a fresh organ or two on the floor, or lose a couple out of the back of a moving ambulance, and oftentimes it won't be your fault, but at the same time you'll likely just nod your head and realize that it's just another facet of the game and reload, ready and eager to take another crack at Bob's insides (was that one entire sentence?)
Point being, this game is a celebration of the human condition, and a real testament to courage and the power to overcome obstacles that seem impossible.  You'll laugh, you'll cry, you'll make your janitorial staff quit out of protest, but most importantly you'll learn to love and live.  And harvest organs.

Ive played an hour long game, the combinations of towers, turrets and modular ships are endless. Its really a game changer for TD.
Notable:
- Two games in one, in the hanger, make strategic decisions on where to place cargo, where to place THRUSTERS! and choosing upgrades. Then once the ship is flying, place towers, re-orientate lasers.
- Constantly juggling whether to go faster* by placing more thrusters or preparing for attacks from asteroids, pirates, and other container ships flying past.
*There is a 5 star rating, the faster you get to the end, the more you are paid.
- Intelligent towers. Eg. lasers cant be placed behind others. And thrusters can't be pointed at other towers or in the same direction as a laser/missile launcher.
- Each hex has its own "hit points" when it runs out, the hex blows off the ship, taking the turret with it.
- Asteroids, and other ships ram into the ship destroying turrets and the ship itself. Which kills off area's to place turrets, this is not scripted.
- No bugs, no resolution problems except "high resolution fonts" setting in windows 7.

It's not as simple as tower defence, you have modules to protect, asteroids to avoid (well... blow up!)
The game does not get boring easily -which is one of the reasons I hated PvZ- Each mission is different from the last, and there is no "standard build" as the placement area for your spaceship changes each time, forcing you to adapt.
I have not had this all that long but so far it is my 2nd favourite Tower defence game, right after bloons!

Great game … a good mix between tower defense and runner ...

Basics-
The game is mostly about hex placement- not far off the tower defence model, but with an emphasis on trying to be just capable enough everywhere and in everything (So you can spend more on better engines to win the race), rather than the tower defence model of dealing with waves in organised stages (Slow them down, wipe out the cannon fodder, heavy hitters for the toughest, etc). Expect some micromanagement, but nothing too heavy.
Good bits-
Nice graphics and good humour, with a fun premise, and it the game doesn't need a long time spent on it to get into.
Downsides-
The main downside is a mix of repetitive missions and a certain level of grinding- to advance you need to upgrade, to upgrade you need cash and to max out the performance on a mission, and the missions don't change when you repeat them, which you'll have to do quite a bit.
Overall-
Good game, fun premise, but it's a tasty snack, not a four course meal- still, fun.

ACE Academy takes place in a hypothetical alternate timeline where the Allies lost World War II, leading to the terrifying future dystopia that Hitler envisioned: Every person on the planet is white and really good at everything.
Yes, exceptionalism is the norm in the ACE Academy universe.  Everyone is physically, mentally, and emotionally fit.  Name any hobby or activity, you and all of your friends are good at it.  You might wonder how well this dynamic works when the plot ostensibly revolves around a fighting competition.  Well I'll tell you.  It works by keeping the stakes low and having the characters overcome any minor obstacle that appears in their way within five minutes of its introduction to the plot.
"But you can't have EVERYONE be exceptional," you may say.  "Story quality aside, having everyone be 'exceptional' literally defeats the meaning of the word itself."  Well you see, ACE Academy is the perfect demonstration of why you are wrong.  Even though all the people in this story, including your rivals, are talented and super-cool nice people, you are still the BEST at being talented and super-nice.  But that's the thing.  The winner is YOU.  You are ALWAYS the winner, "you" meaning "every single person who plays this game".  You are all white guys, and you are all winners.  It works.  The system works.
By the way.  I've heard it said that there is a basic premise behind every harem anime, and that is that the harem is always focused on a particular fetish, and all the girls within the harem are just variations of that fetish.  I believe that is at least true for this game, and in this case the central fetish is "being normal".  Of course, all the girls are exceptional at everything, but that IS normal in this universe as I already stated.  Their personalities are otherwise consistently plain and reasonable.  And within that central fetish of exceptional normalcy, you have your standard variations:
- Shy normal
- Loud normal
- Sexy normal
- Normal normal
- Siscon lolicon
Anyway, I hope this review has helped you determine whether you are a member of the intended demographic for this game.  If you are uncertain, perhaps this will help: Statistically speaking, you probably are.

Moon hunters is a Pixel art, roguelike/lite game with RPG elements (skill leveling etc.) and a story that unwinds with every playthrough. This game is great for short bursts where you just want a break or for long playthroughs where you explore every corner looking for more story.
This game won't be everyones thing but if you like fantasy, mystery and exploration you'll have a good time! The art style is good looking as well without being too generic. The unique point of the game is it's personality trait system and what it unlocks. Depending on what actions you do, your characters personality will change and will define what he/she does. They can be any compination of brave, impatient, wise, cunning, intelligent the list goes on! Moon Hunters has high replayability with (now 6 i believe) unique characters and content that changes and unlocks with every playthrough
In short, avoid this if you're sick of rogue(insert whatever it is here) games and pixel art indies. Definitely get this if you want story, exploration and a bit of good fun! Also the soundtrack is amazing!

I'm trying to figure out what made me redownload this game, but for the life of me I cannot comprehend what was going through my head.
I'll try to be fair and start off this review with things I like about the game.
1.Voice acting.
The game is almost fully voice acted, and it is done rather well.
Some classic voice actors are in this cast, such as mark hamill as the joker,
The cutscenes are really nice too, animatic comic shorts with fun dialog.
2.Combat
The combat, whilst simplistic at it's core with a rock papper scissors theme with blocking ranged and melee, is rather fun.
There are many abilities many weapons and a good ammount of combo's making this feel like a nice action beat uhm up.
3.Visually appealing scenery
The graphics look nice, not 100% modern anymore, but still polished with a few different areas with unique feels between gotham and metropolis.
4.Let's you be a hero OR villian.
A lot of games now a days have this "nothing is black and white" mentality when it comes to factions.
There are usually multiple factions and no one is set in a better light than the other.
But in this game you can be outright evil if you want to. (though sadly there is no middle ground or multiple choices, you're either a criminal or a hero)
Now onto the reasons why this game is a failure, has failed, and will hopefully shut down.
1.Free to play, expensive to enjoy.
This game will attempt to squeeze every penny out of you if you let it.
Not only are almost half of the power types behind a paywall, there are even basic in game features most mmo games don't even consider making you pay real life money for caged off behind pay walls.
One of the worst offenders of this is money in game.
That's right, the money you pick up off the ground in game has a limit.
1,500$ of in game currency is all you can pick up.
If you pick up any more of that without spending it...well, that money is gone now.
You can't use it, you can't get to it, but you can look at it taunting you all day just begging you to spend real life cash to get to it.
Not a problem you think to yourself, I'll just pay the price of unlocking infinite money an- NO! WRONG!
It is a monthly cost to increase your money limit.
And it comes in levels.
First level?
2.5k currency
Second,
Infinite.
So there are two layers of paywalls just to get infinite cash, to use the money you earned to buy things.
It's either that or buy tokens to unlock some of the money just once.
There are also entire episodes (raids/areas) hidden behind 5 dollar pay walls as well.
Just scroll up from this and go look at how much it costs to unlock all of the DLC of this game.
Now add up that along with a 15 dollar per month charge just to 'fully' enjoy the game.
Fun right?
2.Monthly charge option in a F2P game.
This is probably the dumbest thing any of these games can do.
There is a reason your game couldn't keep using a monthly fee model and survive.
It's an outdated archiac payment model.
I would almost gladly pay 30 bucks for this game if they removed the money cap and monthly pay option, and just made the things you can buy vanity items.
That's how almost 100% of the successful F2P games do it.
This game is doomed to shut down just from that, at least till some of the die hard fans start losing their nerve as well.
3. Limited to two character slots in F2P.
I don't know about you, but a game all about making a unique character should allow you to toy around with more than 2 options.
I usually use my second slot for test characters, but everytime I made it to level 10 on one of them, I ended up deleting them because I knew it would be permanent and I couldn't try out any other combinations.
So be absolutely sure what you have it what you want, because if you have two characters you don't like, one has to be deleted to make another.
4.Huge gear gap.
This game has a severe gear gap between new and old school players, and the only way to really fix the gap is to buy some of the newer raids to keep up with the new gear sets.
Even tokens in game for buying gear have a currency cap as well, so you will constantly need to go back and forth buying single pieces of gear, going back out and grinding more money, just constantly refreshing your money.
I took to buying expensive vendor items and reselling them as currency, which is an painful way to work around the issue of the money cap.
I spent a long time trying to grind pvp and money to finally buy a full set of epics in the game.
I thought I was pretty well geared, everything I had was a massive upgrade from the blues I had.
But along came a plasma glowing shield wielding man, covered head to toe in cash shop effects and a money blocked weapon set.
I spent 15 minutes blocking all of his heavy attacks, smashing his ranged attacks, and breaking through his blocks.
After all that time I still did no damage to him, and frustrated that he couldn't kill me, he finally just slowly flew away anticlimactically after giving up.
There are no words for how depressing that is, to totally outclass someone, but be unable to even hurt them, so eventually they just leave after getting bored.
5.RETURNING PLAYERS ARE PUNISHED WITH DELETED CHARACTERS TRAPPED BEHIND A PAYWALL.
This is the thing that stung the most for me, when I redownloaded this game and booted it up, I was told to make a new character.
That's fine, I don't expect them to keep the data of a guy who hasn't played in who knows how long.
Slight problem though....THEY DID HAVE MY DATA, but they wanted me to pay FIFTEEN DOLLARS to recover it.
Wow, the most underhanded slimey thing I can think of for a F2P title to do, hold your characters hostage.
To massive fans of this game who don't want it to change and who are happy to see it stay exactly how it is, know this.
This is a video game, and a business, it will shut down if it keeps this up.
The console release of this game could be make or break, so please, let some of the criticism come through.
Mark my words, if this game doesn't change it's ways soon, it will go down in under a year.
Unless the small number of you who pay to play seriously can keep it afloat, in which case bravo, you're successfully made a game into a buy in club for just you and a select group.
These types of games, even this one, tend to only survive based on their non paying, or frequent but not monthly pay players.
They keep the community diverse and add to the population, giving you monthly paying customers more people to group and play with, and if the market place wasn't so unaccessible due to the money cap, more people to buy your items in game or sell you something you need.
I've slammed down anywhere between 50 and 200 bucks on other games with F2P models, and I don't regret it at all.
But this game is making me regret playing it for free.
That's a serious problem when you can't even keep cheapskates interested in a "free" product.
Bottom line, don't waste your time with this game.
The download is rather large if you don't have great internet, and while leveling can be a fun experience once you max out and start thinking about getting sets, working on your character, decorating your hideout, you'll find more roadblocks and annoyances than you would care to stomach.
It becomes a pain just trying to manage what little funds you have with what you want, and the game just becomes really unrewarding and punishes you for trying harder with it's money caps and huge gear gaps for late comers.
The game pretty much punishes you for getting invested in it, or punishes your wallet if you cave in.
There are bad greedy business practices afoot here, and a gaggle of fanboys ready to defend those practices as well.
You don't need these problems.

It's very sad and disappointing how this game wasn't really given a chance due to mediocre reviews from popular media sites.  OK, this game has flaws;  The AI isn't bad but also nothing special, the behavior coding is pretty poorly done with followers walking in front of you while you are aiming and firing as well as running in front of your vehicles while you try to make getaways, and the game can get slightly repetitive.  HOWEVER, as Craig put it, Red Faction Guerilla is truly masterful at destruction.  The first true "Next Generation" feeling of awe I felt was from this game when I destroyed my first structure.  After I finished with it, I watched as it groaned while trying to support itself under its own weight then eventually crumbled beautifully into a glorious pile of scrap.  I don't think I have ever felt as truly satisfied than when I "stuck it to the man" in teh form of a giant mining truck plowing through military controlled compounds, watching architecture collapse all arounds me as I literally drove into then out of large structures.  If you have the capacity to be moderately creative, and teh rig to handle that "creativity" (I would recommend 512+ VRAM, though you can run this game at 256 on lowest, at least I had to for a while) then, as someone who has actually logged a respectable amount of playtime, I cannot describe this game in any other way than a "work of art."  I would say it's easily worth 20$, a steal if you get it under, like I did...

RF: Guerrilla is an open world action game set in Mars, which is controlled by the Earth Defense Force. The main character joins the Red Faction resistance after the introduction/tutorial level and the goal of the game is to free Mars from the tyranny of EDF.
Gameplay is pretty standard 3rd-person shooter, but the twist is the destructible environment. The ground isn't destructible but all buildings etc. can be destroyed. There are also vehicles to drive around, but most of them are quite slow and not that fun to drive around in. The story progresses through missions, which aren't very long or even that innovative. There are also several side missions available, but they repeat the same pattern and get tedious very quickly. The story isn't very good either.
Difficulty-wise the game is kinda hard, because you die quite quickly even on normal and it takes some time for the health to regen. However, you could just go to a vehicle for a few seconds, which regens your health quite quickly. You also run out of ammo for the weapons very quickly and then you have to pick up one of the enemies' weapons or resort to the melee weapon. Alternatively you could go to an ammo crate, but those are sparsely scattered around the world and they don't even have that much ammo in them.
There is a small upgrade system in the game, which can be used to buy a few new weapons and then some upgrades to them. The "currency" in the game is salvage, which can be obtained by destroying EDF buildings, completing missions or by mining ore deposits.
I would imagine that people, who like to roam around the world and just do random stuff, would enjoy the game more, but I don't really enjoy doing that so I didn't have that much fun playing the game. The game is best played in short bursts, because there isn't much to do in the game unless you really like destroying virtual buildings.
I finished the game in about 13 hours and I did about 45 of the 104 side missions the game has. The main story doesn't take that long to beat, but you must do some side missions for each area before the final story mission for the area unlocks.
It's just an average open world action game that isn't much fun to play.

This is one of the most tactical shooters I have ever played, ranking just below Operation Flashpoint: Dragon Rising. All of AA: Proving Ground's maps are well-designed and well-balanced, and the gunplay rivals AAA genre leaders like Call of Duty and Battlefield. The slow-paced, team-driven combat is nerve-racking; you'll be sweating as you carefully defend the upstairs of a bombed-out building, waiting through the uneasy silence for what you know will be an enemy squad. You'll hear your teammate call out in the live chat (nearly every player you'll come across actively uses a mic) that you're position has been flanked. Smoke grenades will conceal your every side as you try to dash away, knowing full-well that the position, and possibly the match, have been lost.
AA: Proving Ground features intense, immersive battles in every round, featuring 6v6 and 12v12 matches of its equivalent to Call of Duty's Search and Destroy and Domination game types. In both game types you only have one life, but can be revived by a teammate the first time around. Also, like Operation Flashpoint, you must bandage yourself when hit or you'll eventually bleed out.
This game's strategic play style and slow pacing provide the team-based shooter you've been waiting for. People claim that Battlefield is the tactical leader of the fps genre. Tactical? It's nothing in comparison to AA: Proving Ground. The best part about Proving Ground is that the game is completely free and has -no- microtransactions. You don't have to pay a cent to get the full experience.
Get this game. Now.

ACE Academy managed to get my attention by featuring two of my favourite anime genres: High school romance, and giant robots. But what started as an impulse buy to pass the time quickly became a solid favourite of my steam library the more hours I sunk into it.
For starters, the game has a solid story to it. In a Gundam Build Fighters-esque setting where the world has become obsessed with giant robots called GEARs, you are a nameless protagonist (named by you) recently transferred from America to Japan to the pilot program of titular ACE Academy following the death of your parents.  It hit the right points throughout and kept me engaged through multiple playthroughs . And while it does flit more with the tropes of the high school romance side than the mecha side (Beach episode, hot springs episode, etc), there was enough science fiction here to keep it fresh. There are moments when it gets a too meta though (Less leaning on the fourth wall, more smashing it and then crushing the pieces into a fine dust), which while they made me laugh, also pulled me out of the story a bit.
The characters are also a decent bunch, filling the usual tropes sure (Mayu is shy, Yuuna is kind, Kaori is Tsundere, etc), but giving each character their own strengths and flaws. I was also surprised to find the characters were all fully voiced too, and while some of the lines were strangely silent (It was still in Early Access as of writing), the cast is diverse enough that each and every character had their own unique voice, including the one-shot background ones.  It was all well recorded and well-acted too, which is always a bonus. The protagonist too is just enough of a blank slate to be relatable, but still has enough of a personality (some of which is dictated by you) to make it easy to relate to.
The event CGs and music are also well done, with a good variety of pieces that for the most part fit in well with their respective events.
There are some problems however. While the game is still in Early Access as of writing, I’m not sure how many have been, could be, will be or can be addressed, but I would at least mention them to give my honest opinion.
The biggest flaw is the mecha combat. While I wasn’t expecting Titanfall for a VN, I was sort of expecting some kind of turn based system based on the screenshots, as opposed to the quick time sequence in the build I played. While this isn’t a game breaker for me, I can’t shake the feeling that mecha combat had a larger role to play in earlier ideas. There is, for example, a loadout screen filled with empty squares that is seen exactly once, and you go through several lessons that feel important to the mecha piloting process, but ultimately just serve as world building information. While the mecha aspect is a focus of the storyline, it feels a little under loved by the end of it as a result.
There are also a few odd choices for who of the secondary cast gets to be shown, and who doesn’t. The VN goes the RWBY Volume One route of having most of them silhouetted, and while that makes sense for one scene unnamed characters, there are a few, such as the professors and your sister’s friends, who appear multiple times and whose appearances aren’t revealed.   On the flip side, there are characters that appear exactly once that are fully revealed, only to be never seen or heard from again. There was one character that was even shown using CG pieces instead, when having a silhouette with Yuuna giving facial reactions instead would have looked just as good, perhaps better.
Speaking of CGs, while as I said before they are well done, there doesn’t feel like there’s enough of them. This might just be a personal issue of mine really, but I felt several times certain scenes needed more than just the text. This partly manifested as black screens with text describing interesting goings on, but also scenes that I’ve seen to be important in other non-eroge romance VNs (e.g. kissing) that are just described here. And while they're described well, it falls slightly flat when all you’re seeing is your girl smiling at you. A few more backgrounds might not go amiss either (An alternate library/study background, especially in Kaori’s route, was the most glaring one.)
In the end though, these issues don’t really take away from the game as a whole.  These are just things that I think would make a great game greater. ACE Academy is still worth the asking price. If you’re looking for a good story and strong characters to while away some hours with, this game will definitely be worth your time.

Having finally completed episode four, I can say with absolute certainty that this is a fantastic and wonderfully-made visual novel.  With giant robots!
There are a number of technical glitches, of course, the most notable being that there are several lines of audio in episodes 3 and 4 that either don't play to the wording or simply don't play at all.  However, looking beyond those, this is definitely a game worth playing.  All combat and decisions (including some VERY emotional ones) are based on choices, including quick-time events!  And all characters, both human and giant robot, bring a life and energy to the game.  And just when you think it can't get any better?  It does.
All in all, I highly recommend this game to anyone who's a fan of visual novels, anime and manga, and especially of mech battles.  Every moment of this game is electric, hilarious, moving, or any combination of the three.  I wouldn't change a thing about it, and in fact, I think I'll play it again!

[Disclaimer: I won this game from an indie dev giveaway on twitter, so I paid no money for it]
I really wanted to like this game, seeing as it is a first attempt by a new indie company. Had it been made by one or two people, I’d say bravo, however a team of 13 came together to create this and well, I’d like to hear whether or not they all actually enjoy playing the game, because to my experience, it is not a fun game to play.
The premise is relatively intriguing, in spite of it being yet another zombie game. However the controls are not nearly responsive or precise enough for this type of platforming. Couple that with not enough checkpoints and inconsistencies with the game logic, it just leads to frustration and constant death/repeat cycles.
Example: in the first encounter with a zombie you are told to be quiet or they’ll hear you. That’s fine, it just means you have to walk past them instead of run. Cue: excruciating walking sections. Fair enough, that’s a rule I can put up with. Oh wait, several sections later and there is an identical zombie that will straight up instakill you as soon as you go near it, regardless of the speed you are going. *sigh*
The jumping is infuriating: from a standing start, you jump upwards three feet and about an inch forwards, so you may struggle to jump onto a box you are standing right beside. From a walking start, you jump upwards three feet, and six inches forwards, again you might still struggle to climb the box. From a running start you jump upwards about three feet, and forwards about fifteen feet. That seems like a reasonable progression. *facepalm*
Level two “This Rat Ain’t Chef” (I guess something got lost in translation there): there’s a section where there is a corpse in a box with a rat eating it. Above, some platforms suspended by rope. With no prompting, you are supposed to realise on your own that if you push this corpsebox into the right position, the rat will chew through the rope and lower the platforms. I guess my mind just couldn’t make that logic leap, I applaud those who did manage it. I found a Spanish Let’sPlay of the game on youtube that let me pass this section. [Post-Release of Steam Edition Review]
Heyyo,
Wow! Thankfully Nordic Games saved this game from the broken mess it was. I knew underneeth the messed up framerates and poor game optimizations that there resided a fun game. Surely enough? There is. :)
Now I can truly enjoy Red Faction: Guerrilla the way it was meant to be. The addition of DirectX 11 is VERY welcomed and provides decent multi-threaded optimizations to the game (uses about four out of the eight threads on my Intel i7-3770k @ 4.2GHz OC) and an updated NVIDIA SLI profile keeps the temperatures nice and low as both cards share the Graphical load very well.
I wish more games took more serious adventures into Physics like this game does. This is truly the best example of Havok Physics.  The way the buildings collapse is just mindblowing. This game was truly ahead of its time with destruction much like Red Faction 1 was at the time that game released.
For Red Faction: Guerrila? I remember a game developer interview video where they talked about how the team had to take some engineering courses to teach them about structural integirty and other portions of building layouts to make the physics in this game the best yet and they were and they still are. Sometimes? It does get a little silly with one wall or a few posts holding up the roof of the building, but such was the limitations at the time of the game's original release.
The single-player campaign is where I've spent all of my time (sorry no MP review heh) due to how much exploration there was and just how much fun it is to cause wreak havok against the EDF (Earth Defense Force). Wrecking buildings, smashing up bridges and doing side-missions is just dang fun! :)
The storyline is one about how history repeats itself. After the Red Faction fought off Ultor Corporation (yes, the same Ultor from Saints Row series.. same game developers btw, Volition is why) and they mistreated the miners so they revolted and with the held of the EDF? They overthrew Ultor Corporation. Sadly? The Earth was desperate for the precious resources of Mars and they abused the miners to try and get as much resources as fast as possible which is where the new Red Faction of this game comes into play.
The setting is VERY different from previous Red Faction games. This one takes place on the surface of mars in big open environments on an open world map. Previous games were usually subterrain or underwater due to the atmosphere being dangerous to humans at that time. Another major change? The shift from first person to third person view. This game also favors melee attacks a lot compared to the older Red Faction games which guns reigned supreme.
The only downside to this game? The driving. It's ridiculously sensitive on a keyboard and the terrain is extemely lumpy... so combine the two and you get a vehicles that start turning extremely sharply very quickly and you have to tap your A and D keys to try and attempt only minor steering corrections, otherwise you'll find yourself ramping off a lump and launching into a wall or worse.. a pit that is an instant-death... so yeah... careful when you drive. It can really mess you up.
Otherwise? This game is now VERY solid. I look forward to seeing what Nordic Games does in the future. I backed them on Kickstarter for a project they just partnered with called "Shadowrun Online" which is now called "Shadowrun Chronicles" and can be found on Steam btw. I highly suggest you all check it out if you're a fan of turn based RPG's.

The 32.6 hours of my life playing this (at the time of writing this, aka August 13th, 2017) was worth the $5 I spent for it in the Summer Sale. To be honest, I would've spent the whole $20 and more for this game, if I had to.
The game is simple, at first: you're a new cell that came from a meteor and you have to survive. After you eat a few things and get a little bigger. That's when the game lets you evolve your cell. There's not too much to customise with this first time, just a spike (that you just got), flagella to help you go faster, maybe a new mouth, and eyes. But, as your progress through the game and kill/watch other cells be killed, you'll get more part to customise with. In the cell stage, this includes a poison & electricity thing to help defend yourself, cilla & jets to help you go faster,and an omnivore mouth, if you want to be an omnivore. Becoming an omnivore is a bit harder to do than being a herbivore and carnivore. You have to keep the amount of plants and meat you eat about even. Yes, that's right, you'll probably need an omnivore mouth to do this, and you have to find that yourself, unlike the other mouths... God, I could go on about all day. I'll just go on to the creature stage.
Now, the creature stage... once you get big enough in the cell stage, this unlocks. Basically, you grow legs and go onto land. I honestly can't decide whether this or the cell stage is my favorite, so far. In the creature stage, you can actually get a 360 degree view of your creature, and you can put parts on all of it, not just the sides and/or top of it. And you also get more parts. So many more parts than compared to the cell stage! Every item has four "tiers", as I like to call them. Once you get the first tier, you can get the second tier, then once you have that, you can get the third tier, so on so on. The first tier of just hands if more parts then you had in the cell stage alone! Now, you'll also need arms. Arms can help you pick things up, and I think they're mostly for the next stage. There's also strategy involved in making a creature, you can't just throw a bunch of random things on it. I mean, I guess you could, but it won't be very good. You see, mostly every part has benefits. You need eyes to see clearly,  parts kinda like armor (maybe a certain foot, hand, or mouth) for more health, "weapons" for fighting skills, and other parts to help you get allies. To be honest, you'll probably never end this stage with the "social" things, kind of like herbivore, carnivore, and omnivore in the cell stage... I usually go around killing everything weaker than me, but that's just me. You can also get pack mates, though I usually find myself grabbing a few of my own species in a pack. Once your brain is nice and big, you can go on to the Tribal Stage.
Now, this is where I find myself quitting a world and starting a new one most of the time. The tribal stage is an RTS. That's it. You no longer control one certain creature, you control all of them. You can no longer edit your creature, just put outfits that look kind of horrible in my opinion on it. Of course, these outfits benefit your species, but are you really going to play this? I mean, if you're a big fan or RTS's, go ahead. I can't imagine anybody who is, though. Well, basically, you can make friends with tribes or literally kill them and their houses. Killing their main hut is the main goal if you're trying to destroy them. And you can't just go around killing everybody or making friends with everybody like you did before, oh no no no. You have to get certain houses by using your food that you have to collect and your species has to eat to stay alive. Yes, you have to buy the weapons and instruments that you use to please other tribes. I haven't been able to please  a single tribe yet, and that's mostly because they attacked me first. I skipped this stage, made a new world, and started it at the civillization stage.
Okay, the civillization stage. I only played 10 minutes of this and it was boring, but at least it wasn't as bad as the tribal stage. You get these things called spice geysers for money, or "spice", and, like the tribal stage,  you can be friendly towards other species or  kill them. I don't really have much else to say about this.
