Lego Marvel Super Heroes 2
by TT Games/Warner Bros.
Genre: Lego/action/sandbox
Released: November 14, 2017
-----
The evil (but impossibly silly, as voiced by Peter Serafinowicz) Kang the Conqueror has ripped 1 1/2 dozen slices of Marvel history and lore and placed it all into his battle arena of a city called Chronopolis. And it's up to the many heroes, anti-heroes and villains of the Marvel universe to help put it back the way it needs to go!
Lego Marvel Super Heroes 2 is the sequel to, naturally, Lego Marvel Super Heroes and also Lego Avengers which came out in the past couple years. As with those games, this one tasks you with a large open world and many objectives to accomplish, many puzzles to solve and more than 20 story-based levels to clear. However, the difference with this hub world is that it's all in one; a massive, wide-open sandbox of a conglomerated city combining the architecture of more than 15 areas based on Marvel Comics' history as well as inspired by several entries from the Marvel cinematic universe.
You have Manhattan, in several forms (present day, in eternal winter; Noir, from back during the 30s and in black and white; and 2099), being the main hub of activity of all of Marvel Comics. You have the old West, medieval England, Asgard in a more apocalyptic form, the Nova Corps home world of Xandar, the underwater city of Lemuria, ancient Egypt, the Colosseum world of Sakaar from Thor: Ragnarok which I have not seen, K'un L'un, Man-Thing's swamp containing the Nexus of All Realities, the floating Inhuman city of Atillan, the Kree city of Hala, the giant Celestial head of Knowhere (which is not present in the beginning of the game) and finally, Kang's Citadel wherein lies the seat of his power. That's 16, all off the top of my head; that leaves two that I forgot, so suffice to say, the game is pretty massive.
Being the first game in which TT Games took advantage of next-generation consoles, the game looks pretty spectacular, with reflections pretty much anywhere you can think of, as well as lens flares, directional lighting, ambient occlusion, antialiasing, and many things that did not show up in previous titles in the Lego series. Also, when selecting from the more than 250 characters (whether assigned to you as you go through the story, or those that you can unlock through purchasing using the ever-present Lego studs), you can view their trading card at any time, showing you their powers and a brief writeup of their history.
So if you want a little more Lego in your video gaming experience, and who doesn't, then check this out! I don't think you'll regret it.

LEGO Marvel Super Heroes 2 is a must have for fans of Marvel Comics, without a doubt. Excluding the X-Men and the other mutants, nearly every hero and villain are here. From the well known Captain America and Black Panther to the greatly unknown Squirrel Girl and Ms. America, you can find any fan favorite fully fleshed out with their own levels, minigames, races, and puzzles. As the story combines nearly every alternate universe and timeline, the stories flow together seemlessly, going from the Old West to the Great Depression to 2099 in a matter of a few levels. The main characters of the story also differ from previous games, favoring those such as Ms. Marvel and She-Hulk as recurring characters over the likes of Iron Man and the Incredible Hulk. As imaginative as it is fun, this is one of my favorite LEGO games, and is the only one I have felt compelled to 100% since LEGO Star Wars. However, there are several issues I have with the game as well. The game was clearly geared towards console play, as the keyboard and mouse controls are extremely difficult to use comparred to a controller. Use of a controller in this isn't only recommended, it's practically required. While the levels are all different in the sense of location and characters, they all begin to follow the same structure, which isn't all too bad. If you don't mind solving a few puzzles that lead up to a boss fight with more puzzles inside, then this shouldn't be a problem. While this is more of a personal complaint, I feel that some of my favorite characters didn't recieve much screen time, such as Luke Cage and Miles Morales, however this may not bother others. With the negatives aside, however, my favorite addition to the game is the addition of the character cards, which include a brief description of every character and the year and issue of their first appearance. Overall, though, this is a very strong Marvel game and a very fun LEGO game, and it's definitely worth the money.

I am currently playing through LEGO Marvel Super Heroes 2 and although I am enjoying it, there are one or two things that I'm not overly keen on.
1) Some of the levels are short. Really short. They are basically just 'boss areas' with little to explore.
2) There are a lot of boss battles in this game, sometimes two or three per level and they can get a bit tedious after a while. The developers have made defeating enemies a bit more difficult in this game and although I appreciate why they've done it, certain methods you have to go through in these fights can leave you a bit frustrated and even bored.
3) Not sure if it's just myself that's having this issue but the attack mechanics aren't very effective. I tap the hell out of the X button but my controlled character just spins and leaps around the person I'm trying to attack, rather than hit them.  I manage to get them eventually but this is a bit annoying, especially when you have a number of enemies on you. Didn't have this problem in other LEGO games where the attacks were far more effective first time, every time.
That said, this is an enjoyable game so far with all the usual LEGO video game antics plus there is a huge roster of Marvel super heroes to unlock and play as. I like how they have minituarized certain lands and areas from the movies into one conjoined map; it makes the areas varied and fun to explore. I would recommend this game to any LEGO fan. 7/10.

This sad tale is beautifully rendered with lush graphics and attention to detail.  Brothers is a unique puzzle game because you control two characters on the screen at the same time.  The puzzles aren't extremely difficult but they are fun as you are constantly maneuvering the brothers around the screen to complete tasks.  All of the achievements come from finding extras that were put into the game that don't have to be accomplished to complete the game. Amazing game, no dialog(something similar to sim speak) but it really gets to you the further you play through.  The characters grow as you progress, the plot thickens(based solely on what you think is going on) and the controls are there not only to complete the game but to slowly coerce you into caring what happens to the brothers.

To me, this game was a different experience than what I have typically played. First off, the controls are different where half the controller controls the big brother and the other half the little brother. It takes some time to get used to this control scheme, but provides a unique control experience for playing the game and solving pullzes. The story was engaging with a mix of funny and sad moments. To me the story is delivered through the visual experience as I could not get the spoken words in English. I am not sure if that is how the game was setup or if I missed a setting. The environments are stunning with the Unreal engine. Your travels take you through fields, forest, caves, snow covered mountains, and villages. Each environment is visually appealing and detailed.
Overall, I enjoyed the game and recommend it. The game is short, but the puzzles and exploration are engaging and provide a break from the "typical" games released by larger developers.

The draw of this game over JC2 is that there are some fun physics involved. Let's talk 3rd person sandbox destruction on the biggest literal sandbox of all: Mars. You play Alec Mason, hammer-wielding badass and walking instrument of devastation and vengance with an apparent grudge against every sign of human habitation on mars. On its own, it's a great, cathartic panalopy of destruction.

TL;DR: A decent remake weighed down by Activisions greed. 2/5
A remake of COD4 sounds like it came straight from one of my wet dreams. It's done really well too, the visuals are done well enough to make it look like it belongs on the current gen, From intense firefights in the desert streets in the middle east, to the eerie atmosphere of Ukraines abandoned city it all looks top notch. The sound effects have also been bumped up conciderably while still holding true to the original. Guns still sound as iconic as they first did in 2007, It all sounds crisper and clearer and you can tell there has been a-lot of love put into this title.
The overall gameplay plays the same as Cod4 did back in 2007 and it all feels really smooth, responsive and what you would expect from a modern shooter title. The multi-player also adds new challanges, finally prestige for the PC version of Cod4, a bunch of new camo's and all the classic stuff you got from the original multi-player. Unfortunately this is where the negatives start to pile up and cracks really show.. We are now greeted with the "depot" which is basically the same pay to win bulls**t from the last few COD titles. IMO this does not belong in a $70-90 game period but it is a huge kick in the face here to all the old COD4 veterans. This is the kind of crap thats seen in free to play games and its increasing presence in full priced titles is concerning. There are a few arguments that can be made in favor of this mechanic, but honestly it's just a half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥money grab thrown in a classic title that has no place to be there. The other negatives that effect multi-player is the lack of dedicated servers on PC, matchmaking works fine for consoles and games with a high playerbase but the fact this game is shoved in with COD infinite something (never going to install it) and the fact that they are pushing new titles every year to thin out their playerbase as much as possible. Finding a server with a low latency is basically impossible without any form of dedicated server system and jumping into multi-player you are guarenteed to lag your♥♥♥♥♥off.
My last and biggest gripe with this game is, as stated above that this game is shoved in with another COD game that no-one wanted. If you purchased the special edition of infinite warefare chances are you only did it for the remastered version of COD. It's such a shame because this remaster is really well done, it looks beautiful, sounds amazing and is a huge nostolgia trip for me personally. But the unashamed cash grabs by activision make me loathe actually playing it, you're better off just playing the original if you want a Cod 4 experience on PC.

Short version:
Pros: Main Storyline is good. Bonus missions added to coincide with and supplement the now cancelled counter-part TV show are also fun. The gun play is very satisfying and arguably the best redeeming feature of the game.
Cons: No real meaningful storyline content has been added since the second season of the TV ended...the TV show had 3 seasons. Unless you buy the season pass and a copy of the game on Amazon or another 3rd party site, you will be getting a watered down experience. Server crashes, critical errors, character load errors, and overall lag/latency issues are a daily if not weekly occurence.
Ugly: Developers ignore game breaking / severe bugs present on Public Test Server and release major patches with said bugs present anyway. Attempts to monetize / reward patron players as of Summer 2016 has polarized the community. See official Defiance game forums.
Longer explanation below:
Since the game has adopted a Free to Play model, Trion-Worlds has made some poor choices. As with most games that are F2P, cosmetics are generally the way a company can make a nice profit. Unfortunately, in addition to the game being not that great looking, there is there is not much in the way of said cosmetics. You can purchase a small variety of outfits for a single character on your account, not all. You may also purchase vehicle skins for the variety of dodge vehicles, ATV, or buggy you'll be roaming the newly teraformed frontier with. As these are very limited options, the developers implemented a cash store option that includes includes other such as exclusive weapons with exlusive bonuses. Some of these weapons can be meh, while others are rather overpower and may be seen as pay to win. Sometimes events that coincide with real world holidays (halloween, christmast, valentines day, etc.) drop weapons that are simliar and help balance out this problem. TLDR, cash store weapons in PvE is fun, but taking these into PvP can create a severe and ugly inbalance.

A remarkable experience, one that I really thought achieved that much sought-after balance between compelling gameplay and compelling story, and like many great stories it's all about the journey. You control two brothers on a quest to find a cure for their ailing father, each brother controlled simultaneously with the left and right analog sticks on your controller (if ever there was an ad for getting a 360 / PS4 controller for your PC, this is it). It doesn't take long for your brain to adjust to this, although I found I had to keep the brothers on the same side as their analog stick to keep up! This isn't just a gimmick either, it really works, even to the extent of serving the story. There were times that I felt this was the best Tomb Raider game I'd played since the first one, that sense of edging around precarious drops and leaping between hand-holds, and the game exploits the co-op nature of your two characters well. It's also really spectacularly beautiful in places, and I kept wishing my Steam screen save button was working, but alas no. The game clocks in at just over three hours, but it feels right, almost like experiencing a great movie. The less said in any review about the actual story, though, the better. Just play it.

BUGGY, POORLY-ACTED AND A STEP BACKWARD
PROS: Plenty of characters; hours of game play (for 100% completion); usual Lego humor
CONS: Very buggy; poor voice acting; missing mechanics
This game broke my heart, and I don't mean how many Marvel characters aren't included because Fox won't let Marvel have the rights to the X-Men and Deadpool back. I'm okay with anything that Marvel does to rescue their properties from people who turn out garbage like the last Fantastic Four movie.
Considering that the first Lego Marvel Super Heroes is my favorite Lego game of all time, I was really looking forward to this game.
Had I known the recent voice actor's strike included this game and that TT hired scabs to fill in the missing spots, I would have waited for a huge discount during a summer sale or simply boycotted the game completely.
The acting is BAD.
So bad.
"Teachers reading picture books to kindergartners during story time" bad.
If you hate dubbed anime, play this with the sound off.
This game is a case study in why professional voiceover talent is so important to a good gaming experience.
With that out of the way, the positives:
It's more of the same Lego puzzles and humor. If you enjoyed every other Lego game to date, this one has no surprises. Poor acting aside, the writing is as fun as ever.
You will also have many hours of play to get that all important 100% completion.
They also changed the Red Brick method. Instead of having to work through much of the game looking for the 2x multiplier, all five are already included at the beginning. You merely have to earn enough studs to unlock them.
Now for the negatives (apart from the terrible, horrible voice acting):
Bugs.
Lots and lots and lots of bugs.
It's a good thing the opening video of Star-Lord flying his ship in front of a gorgeous panoramic view of space while "Come and Get Your Love" plays in the background is so appealing because you will see that over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over again as you will constantly be booted to the desktop.
If you're LUCKY.
If you're unlucky, enjoy repeatedly restarting broken quests to get NPCs out of trapped areas or to hopefully get them to trigger events to allow you to complete them.
And once again, the Red Brick mini-kit detector often fails to point out all of them on several levels, forcing you to search online for the elusive missing pieces. Worse, when they do work, the arrows sometimes only appear if you are literally right on top of them.
Many of the puzzles are TERRIBLE, particularly those annoying slide puzzles (the kind where a picture is cut into eight pieces and one empty slot and you have to rearrange them back to the original orientation). If you're bad at those (like me) expect a lot of frustration as you randomly move plates hoping for a solution.
As a Lego enthusiast, one of the nice things about Lego games is watching them evolve, particularly how every subsequent game seems to recognize a poor mechanic or irritation from the previous game and corrects it in the new one.
Not this time. Just the opposite, in fact.
One of the best things previous games featured was being able to enter a Free Play level at any of the checkpoints, thus saving you the hassle of playing through the entire level if you only need a gold brick after the third checkpoint. Well, guess what? You have to start at the beginning of the level every time in Free Play. So prepare yourself for constant repeats as you grind toward 100%.
Bottom line, this game should be avoided until they patch it at the very least, although I'd wait for a huge summer sale discount.

This game is quite ambitious with how far it dives deep into comic book alternate realities.  In other words, it's weird as hell.  A lot of the mechanics are good and what works is quite fun.  However, the game lacks some serious polish.  Playing coop in the open world is audio-visual nightmare with characters talking on both sides, constant achievement popups, tutorial pointers, and random times when the entire screen is needed for a cut scene, interrupting the other player.  This all happens  about every 30 seconds and really starts to get on the nerves of both players.  Even worse, however, is the buggy state of the openworld quests.  About twice in 30 minutes, I spent a substantial amount of time trying to complete a quest when at the very end the NPC decided to have a stroke or something and made it impossible to finish it.  One time I was stuck and couldn't move while the NPC just kept yelling stock "please complete my quest" lines.  Even more obnoxious was a broken boss fight.  If you do not precisely follow the code's rules on how to beat this boss, the boss will refuse to get out of his shield-state while constantly sending more and more little creatures to kill you.  It took about 15 minutes of this to realize that the game had bugged out.  We reloaded it and, yet again, the boss got stuck in his shield-state.  After a little trial and error, I found that it was because I was flying and shooting him.  That's it.  That's what was breaking the entire level.  These kinds of constant oversights make every part of the game untrustworthy.  I am constantly wondering "am I doing this wrong or is the game just broken again?"  And this is supposed to be a child's game.  In it's current state, I don't recommend it.  Maybe wait for some patches.

Bounty Train is a strategy type RPG, at first I didn’t think it was much like an RPG and placed it more in the rouge-like genre with games such as FTL, however after playing the game and learning more about it’s features it definitely fit more into the RPG category. Surrounding a very western theme of the 19th century using historically accurate events and trains to guide a story, you play as Walter Reed in a somewhat tycoon-esque game.
As with most games the first thing you come across is the sounds and visuals, when you start up the game you are introduced with the typical upbeat sounds of the wild west. Already setting you in the mood to stroll in to a saloon as you approach the bartender and with your best cowboy accent greet them with a “Howdy partner” And when you see the image of Walter Reed, with his red sash and hat, you fit the role even more. The actual graphics of the game are quite nicely done, however the cabins of each train segment don’t have animated doors, so when you traverse from one area to another, you walk through the door. This also happens when you attempt to stop a bandit from uncoupling your train, you will start to fight through the wooden walls with Walter Reed’s seemingly unfounded strength, who knew he could do that.
Once your battles have finished and you explorer the wider world you are accompanied by new music, it is no longer the intense cacophony of battle ready music, but the soothing winds and outdoor sounds as you look down on the ‘World Map’. Here you can select which cities you wish the travel too and once you have selected and entered into a town, a new form of music accompanied by immersive sound effects such as birds tweeting and people chattering to give you a sense of where you are. The changes from each area definitely help to create what kind of setting you are in currently.
As mentioned you play as one Walter Reed, a money orientated cowboy with his sights on leaving America as soon as possible. After receiving some news about his departed father, Walter doesn’t seem very moved by the deceased, instead his first thoughts are on what his father has left him after his death. It is here that Walter finds out that the shares his father had in a train company has been split amongst himself and his siblings, meaning Walter now owns 11% of the company, a train and $43,000. But there is a catch, he can only get the $43,000 on completion of a transcontinental railway, from the east coast of America to the west. Walter isn’t the brightest person on the planet, thinking that an operation like this would take a mere month and is confronted with the fact it could take up to a decade. The trouble doesn’t end there, if he wants that money sooner, he will have to get the line built in the shortest route possible, which is what his father would want, but there is an obstacle in his way by the name of Cornellius Tilberdnar (I have no idea how to say it either).

After getting to know this software and been using it for some time, i would have to say it have become a everyday utility to use the controller in both games and desktop use. There are other alternatives, but this software has its edges in functionality and ease of use. It is not without its limitations still and i am comparing this mostly to pinnacle profiler, antimicro and xpadder.
+Controller companion is the easiest to configure of them all
+Functional on-screen keyboard and
+Language support
+Good pricepoint and value
+Integrates 360ce controller emulator for non 360 controllers.
+Good automatic detection of the games that are configured.
+Community active developer
+Individual game profiles
+Workshop integration
-Intrusive steam in-game integration (disabling it does just not work, deleting the steam api dll. works half-ways unless you use the settings, which you need to use to make full use of the program)
-No default or manual game profile, each game needs to be configured for automation which can get tedius compared to having default profiles for both desktop and games.
-It doesnt reconfigure buttons on the pad, can only map them to keyboard and mouse inputs
Usually the only thing i need it to do is bind a controller button for screenshots and one for switching to desktop, thats it. And with controller companion, i have not found a way to do this without sacrificing the desktop profile and controls.
I like Controller companion for the easy navigation and desktop controls. Although Pinnacle Profiler have a lot more profile options and it is specifically geared towards games and advanced profile options, like autofire, forcefeedback and customized controls, but it is also more complicated to use.
Controller companion may be hold back with no default game profile. Which in turn forces the desktop profile to intrude in games a whole lot of the time... if you play many games these settings manages to get in the way every time you start a new game unless you use the desktop profile for everything or complement it with another controller software for a fixed profile so you can have those options for games and desktop combined.
7/10 for gaming + desktop, 11/10 for desktop use

The vast majority of the negative reviews here are just people complaining about the cost of a map pack. Thats one map pack. The best part of the game is by far the campaign, it has been remastered so all the graphics have been improved are are in line with what you would excpect from any modern game, this allows people to experience the original story and missions which were so popular in the original game, but with graphics sutiable for modern PC gaming. Krater is a top down Action RPG similar to games such as Torchlight and Diablo. The thing that seperates it from those games is that instead of controlling 1 character, you'll be controlling a squad of three of them. Oh, and it's set in Sweden.
You navigate the game via a HUGE overworld map similar to games like Final Fantasy VII. You can expect random encounters to spice up your journeys and this is actually a really cool feature of the game. One suprising thing is, despite the huge world, levels load in really quickly.
However, not all is good. Moving onto the combat - the combat was simply such a huge disappointment for me. It's so basic and the abilities cool down so fast, you'd think the game was set in Antarctica. Literally, every single battle just felt like I was playing guitar hero with the number keys in order to win.
Speaking of abilities, you'd think an action RPG on this scale has hundreds of them, right? Well I'll tell you now that there are 4 different classes in this game and how many abilities does each class have? Two. Yep, that's right: Two.
Being a game where about 80% of the time you'll be fighting, the combat system just makes it fall flat on it's face. There are plenty of other features like a confusing crafting system and permadeath party system, but they pretty much go unnoticed because of how terrible the rest of the game is.
I wanted to like this game, but all the potential it had has just gone at the window, leaving it with a 3 out of 10.

This game feels like someone took several successful games over the years and frankensteined them together, complete with a Swedish Mad Max voiceover.  The overall effect is initially disorienting, but smooths out as you embrace your new existence as a 3-person hive mind.
The combat mechanic is pretty straightforward hack-n-slash (think Torchlight or Diablo), with the twist that you need to try to manage the actions of three heroes instead of just one.  After just a couple encounters, I realized that remapping my squad members' special abilities and treating the whole group as one entity was pretty critical to coordinating their efforts.  Over time it became apparent that much of the game's value lies in this novel approach.
The navigation from town to town and much of the writing is very reminiscent of the first Fallout games. Random encounters occur when moving between known (and unknown) world map locations and the NPCs scattered around have hilarious problems that they need you to help with.
There is also a basic crafting system and everything devolves pretty quickly into a treadmill of quest grinding and gear looting/upgrading.
The world is mildly intriguing, if you are into post-apocalyptic mythos, and exploring it is the main reason why I continued playing after I wearied of inventory shuffling.

If you're looking for a neat idea done poorly, you've found your game.
In lieu of strategy and tactics, you've got a ton of random events. Even whether or not something functions seems to be completely random.
EG, you pull the train whistle during attempted robberies to scare the bad guys' horses - only there's no telling whether it will work or not, and I've literally never seen it scare all of the horses while it rarely scares more than one. So a major defensive choice you can make is utterly random. It might as well just randomly have horses shy instead of even giving you the illusion that you are participating in this aspect of the game.
A lot of UI elements break regularly. A lot of the UI is inconsistent. Space bar pauses in fights, no where else. You get a button to go immediately to the map screen from town, unless you're in the depot. The little "x" for closing the failed/completed missions is at the right most edge of the bubble, so it's constantly moving, meaning it takes about 4 times as long to close them all as it should (and why isn't there a button to close all failed/completed mission bubbles?).  If you fail a combat scene, you can retry - but you cannot retry until you fail; in other words, if someone dies early in the scene, you have to sit there trying to lose faster to retry instead of simply retrying.
The sheer number of random events is so high that the pretense of playing a game about trading and building your business should simply be removed. At times you will hit four or five random events between two nearby towns on a single stretch of rail track. It can be amazinlgy obnoxious, but it also can mean that you are in 2 or 3 combats in a row - forcing you to save-scum by saving every time you leave a town and then simply reloading if you get a bad string of luck.
I'm all for the train robbery mini game, I like it, but being forced into it over and over and never being able to heal up or save up money is obnoxious and defeats the supposed purpose of the game.
This game is simply not ready for release. It needs a lot of tweaking. It needs a lot of bug fixes. It needs the UI to be consistent and improved. The idea that they are selling DLC already is hilariously arrogant.
Until it is improved, do not buy it.

I don't usually review early access(2016-7-19), but for Bounty Train, I figured I may as well
Bounty Train is a game about running a train through the not-so-wild eastern coast of the USA right in during the civil war, trading in the cities and ferrying small amounts of passengers around. It has several ways to make money, and plenty more ways to lose it. But in the end every part of it works great on its own, but is still not really working together as a single whole game just yet.
You can trade, you can customise your train with carriages and historical locomotives, you can do combat when the bandits try to take your money, you can level up, and you can have a chase scene almost straight from a western. It is already entertaining and a pleasant experience, with the base gameplay being solid and simple enough to understand even for someone new to the game. At the same time it allows you enough control to remain interesting after you learn the basics.
The graphics and sound are pleasant, with the world map being a well made stylised view. That is where my first complaint lies. Specifically, with the transition between your train view to the world map. Every single time you do this you get a loading screen, which slows down the game by a lot as anyone who doesn't know US geography will need to go check the world map every time they see a place name to see where it is, and even those who do know will need to check it regularly to see if there is an indian camp or army position at the track they plan to take. This is quite harsh on the flow of the game, especially if you need to switch back and forth multiple time before actually moving your train.
Other negatives are balance issues. As it is early access, I'm not weighing them as much since they are mainly numbers that need tweaking, or things in need of more explaining. For example, the ability to escape from bandits is fun to have, with the chase being interesting and very good at engaging you as you have to control your train. But what it doesn't say is that you have only old trains, and you are not going to go fast enough to escape from anything at all unless you've left most of your wagons at the station. Any train that has enough cargo to make a profit is better off just stopping and shooting the bandits until they stop coming, simply because of the weight of your cargo slowing you down enough to make escape impossible.
At a similar note, often you do not get a chance to escape at all. When the army engages you(Which they will, both north and south will en up hating you for no particular reason other than you existing) you are only given the option to attack them, with no way to escape until time on their barricade runs out. The barricade they have lasts long enough for them to completely destroy your train before you can move on, which will feel like the game just said "Okay, you encounter this event. You lose", rather than it being your fault for your loss until the late game where you can defend against a small army group.
Another balance issue is the weaponry, some of them are just plain better than others, and when the bandits attacking you have these stronger guns and you don't, you do not have a good chance. What is worse is that you can not loot their weaponry; Loot is randomly generated after combat is already over.
While Bounty Train has a lot of potential, it is still unfinished as the Early Access tag says. Even then it is certainly worth keeping an eye on for when they tweak the gameplay and finish adding the rest of it. In the end I had fun playing this game so I would recommend it to others out there who probably clicked on this game for the prospect of trains. For an Early Access game a lot of mistakes can be forgivable at this stage. Character models don't match charcter portraits, dialogue choices don't matter, and combat early in the game seems dull while only slightly getting better later on.
For instance you can have these people waiting at the station for days on end (which seems like a silly system to begin with) and when you see a black character model you might expect them to have a smaller portrait of a black character when you speak to them, but I rarely remember that being the case. There's just not a lot of unique character models and I hope that what they're do now is just them using placeholders.
The game has a lot of characters that wait at stations that aren't looking to travel either. These people have white text above their heads and might send you on a quest to do some smuggling, deliveries, or other quests. Talking to someone can reveal their troubles and they give you a quest if you choose the correct dialogue responsive. However, if you choose incorrect responses and you don't get the quest you simply can try again as if you hadn't spoken to them already. I don't know if the game is trying to have a Mass Effect vibe as if you story choices matter, but if it is then it feels like a failure.
Combat seems a bit dull and it tries to be an autonomous real time strategy. The whole thing feels off when you can watch your characters constantly shoot someone just to see that person's health decrease little by little. Combat is all about firing guns most of the time, but it sure doesn't feel like they're shooting anything except for blanks. Combat only gets better once you have enough cash to outfit your hired help with better weapons, but even then combat isn't at a pace that feels enjoyable. It's a problem when you have characters using rifles, but they take as long as someone with a revolver to reload their gun while at the same time showing an animation above their head of a revolver being loaded. The battle experience gets ruined when you have bandits riding horses that glitch through trains. Moving characters and activating their special ability once in a while just isn't all that exciting. It lacks the call for interaction that I'm desperately craving. I want to be able to maneuver my characters and passangers in a cover system that feels familiar to XCOM. I want there to be more strategy. I want the way I drive my train to matter.
The story isn't that bad and is pretty interesting, but you have loads of time to complete the main objective and it feels like everyone is just a bit out of character. There's a clear lack of emotions in what your character, Walter Reed, has to say at any point in this game. It might have something to do with the fact that your choices don't really matter or it's just because the developers may not know how a no good bandit such as your self would speak in the 1800s. You don't even get to create your own personality for your character. You have forced dialogue options that either make him completely rude or sincere, but he doesn't grow as a character to become sympathetic. These scenarios can happen at different points during your travels making you question whether Walter Reed is getting up on the wrong side of the bed or just bipolar.
Don't expect this to be an outstanding game. It has its problems, Early Access or not. You can still have fun with managing your train and performing tasks in the game.

This is the most enjoyable and reliable medieval combat game out there. The gameplay is excellent, as it is easy to learn yet hard to master with its really cool blocking and attacking mechanics. As a disclaimer: When you first start playing multiplayer (The main mode) in this game, expect to die. A LOT. You may wish to quit and demand a refund but I STRONGLY ENCOURAGE you to continue to play. Practice and improve, and once you get the hang of the combat you will have a blast in up to 200 player medieval battles. The game offers a wide variety of weapons, from your typical swords, shields, and bows to more interesting ones such as mauls and lances. Multiplayer is the main mode here, and has plenty of content to offer. Despite being 6 years old, this game continues to have an acitve and loyal fanbase, with at least a few servers being almost full. Character customization isn't very much but can be used to create the funniest looking characters I have ever seen. There are several game modes in multiplayer, with your typical Team Deathmatch and CTF. The most fun gamemode out of them all however is battle, a massive fight between two teams of up to 100 players each where you have ONLY ONE LIFE. The adrenaline is real in this gamemode, which is what makes it so awesomely good. The game also offers a singleplayer mode, similar to its predecessor Mount and Blade. Just like the first game, you create a character in the land of Caladria, a brutal and unforgiving landscape ruled by various kingdoms. There are endless possibilities here, you can do whatever you want, whether it be a bandit/thug who ravages the countryside, or work your way into one of these kingdom's noble rankings to become king.
There is just so much content and stuff to do in this game that I really can't explain in this review. This game is amazing and I would definitely recommend it to anyone who enjoys third'first person action games and the medieval setting.
My Final Score:  9/10 (Amazing)

Spore was a very ambitious game. It was made by the developers of Civ city, and the game was about mimicking evolution.
There are a total of 5 stages, and each stage has it's own minigame tailored to it.
In the first stage you start from a cell, and the whole game basically plays like snake or pacman basically. You eat, you grow, you evolve. You have a choice to become a herbivore, carnivore or both. At this point, it actually sells itself as a good game, but it isn't like that. That's probably the most meaningfull choice you can ever make in this game.
In the second stage you evolve to a land animal basically. There is a cool editor where you can make your "creature". This stage basically plays like an MMO RPG (you have those keybindings and all). It's very mundane and the whole point is to either kill or befriend other creatures. The worst thing about this stage is how every other creature is random generated and looks very alien.
The third stage is the tribal stage and plays like an RTS. It's actually a cool concept, but was not given enough polish or depth just like everything else in the game. There are 3 weapons and 3 musical instruments in that stage. You get one of each depending on how aggresive you were last stage, and there are other tribes on the map that have other sets of weapons and music instruments. You either destroy or befriend other tribes, and for every one of those you get an weapon/instrument.
Like any RTS you have to gather resources here, and there is only one - food. You can gather or hunt. You also can tame animals, which then can be used for domestication. It sounds cool, but it lacks depth. There is a lot of missed opportunities here, and the stage lacks polish. Tribes will attack no matter what (they basically have intervals between each attack), so it's pretty much impossible to play non aggresively. But the biggest issue is that the unit pathing is just not very good. During battle you pretty much have to micro every unit, one at a time.
The forth stage is basically a combination of supreme commander/total annihilation. Basically, there are cities now, and you basically the whole planet is accessible. You can zoom in/out as far as you want. The cities are costumizable. All buildings can be made from ground up via an editor.
As for the combat, you can make land, air or water vehicles. There is an editor for that. Again, cool idea, but unfortunately mostly cosmetic. The components that you use to make your vehicle have certain stats (damage, health, speed of the vehicle). It would have been much cooler to have something similar to Kerbal Simulator where the design itself matters on how well something will operate. But the biggest issue with this is that you can only have one design for each land, air and water vehicles. This basically throws tactics right out of the windows and it all comes down to pure numbers.
The final stage is you going into space and visiting other planets, who are stuck at one of the stages. Basically it's god mode. They decided to make the final stage's minigame an "editor".
I liked the first, third and forth stages. But i still cannot recommend the game, and there are basicall 3 big reasons for that.
1) Like i said, these are "minigames". They lack depth.
2) This game could have been like Sid Meier's Civ. In that game, you play starting 4000 BC till the present age, making your own alternative history along the way. That history is very plausible by the way, which is why Civ is so loved. The difference between spore and civ is that spore simply doesn't have choices. Every playthrough is exactly the same. The playthroughs themselves are very short (since these are minigames). Games in Civ can take days.
3) Also the game is just very "alien". All the creatures are random generated and look ridiculous. They don't even look scary. I wish there would have been some option so that the game would mimic earth like creatures. The planet is pretty much the same, with no variation (except for color), and after stage one you can only roam on land. Again, missed opportunity.
4) The game is "childish", in a sense that it tries to appeal to kids. It is especially clear in the second stage. Here is the E3 demo showed in 2005.
As you see, it's much more mature.

Kentucky Fried Chicken, more commonly known by its initials KFC, is an American fast food restaurant chain that specializes in fried chicken. Headquartered in Louisville, Kentucky, it is the world's second-largest restaurant chain (as measured by sales) after McDonald's, with almost 20,000 locations globally in 123 countries and territories as of December 2015. The chain is a subsidiary of Yum! Brands, a restaurant company that also owns the Pizza Hut and Taco Bell chains.
KFC was founded by Colonel Harland Sanders, an entrepreneur who began selling fried chicken from his roadside restaurant in Corbin, Kentucky during the Great Depression. Sanders identified the potential of the restaurant franchising concept, and the first "Kentucky Fried Chicken" franchise opened in Utah in 1952. KFC popularized chicken in the fast food industry, diversifying the market by challenging the established dominance of the hamburger. By branding himself as "Colonel Sanders", Harland became a prominent figure of American cultural history, and his image remains widely used in KFC advertising. However, the company's rapid expansion overwhelmed the aging Sanders and he sold it to a group of investors led by John Y. Brown, Jr. and Jack C. Massey in 1964.
KFC was one of the first American fast food chains to expand internationally, opening outlets in Canada, the United Kingdom, Mexico, and Jamaica by the mid-1960s. Throughout the 1970s and 1980s, it experienced mixed fortunes domestically, as it went through a series of changes in corporate ownership with little or no experience in the restaurant business. In the early-1970s, KFC was sold to the spirits distributor Heublein, which was taken over by the R.J. Reynolds food and tobacco conglomerate; that company sold the chain to PepsiCo. The chain continued to expand overseas, however, and in 1987, it became the first Western restaurant chain to open in China. It has since expanded rapidly in China, which is now the company's single largest market. PepsiCo spun off its restaurants division as Tricon Global Restaurants, which later changed its name to Yum! Brands.
KFC's original product is pressure fried chicken pieces, seasoned with Sanders' recipe of 11 herbs and spices. The constituents of the recipe represent a notable trade secret. Larger portions of fried chicken are served in a cardboard "bucket", which has become a well known feature of the chain since it was first introduced by franchisee Pete Harman in 1957. Since the early 1990s, KFC has expanded its menu to offer other chicken products such as chicken fillet burgers and wraps, as well as salads and side dishes, such as French fries and coleslaw, desserts, and soft drinks, the latter often supplied by PepsiCo. KFC is known for its former and current slogan "Finger Lickin' Good", which was replaced by "Nobody does chicken like KFC" and "So good" in the interim.

Developed and released by the U.S. Army, AA:PG is a great looking game on the Unreal 3 engine. That being said, its gameplay is great, very realistic, and doesn't have the Battlefield, Medal of Honor, and Call of Duty health regen B.S. I do generally recommend this game, but it does have its downsides such as its small number of maps and high system requirements (not that anyone with a custom built machine from the last four or five years should have any trouble).
My main complaint really is that since AA:3, they have had fewer training missions. Sure, the training missions would be pointless at this juncture, but they were fun, and informative. For players of AA:3, you may remember the medic training, obstacle course, weapons familiarization course, and MOUT course. None of these courses, which were very useful in the game, and would still be in this one, are present, aside from MOUT.
Furthermore, if you have played AA:2, you would really miss the plethora of training missions, including: paratrooping, stealth training (the hardest one), sniper training, BRT, medic course (I'll concede that that was NOT fun), Hummvee driving, Hummvee CROWS system training, Javelin training, and many more fun training missons.
Lastly, and this applies to AA:3 as well, the maps are somewhat small. While some people will disagree, let me say that these maps are COD size compared to AA:2. AA:2 had vehicles, huge battlegrounds, and even fortified compounds. While this is still a beta, I usually tend to see the beta products are pretty close to the finished product.
The biggest reason this is an issue is that the maps have become smaller, the missions are fewer, the gameplay opportunities are fewer, and this is on Unreal 3, and the better of it runs Unreal 2. Things should be improved as technology increases, not removed.
Aside from the points in this review, I do have to say that I recommend this, but there really isn't too much to say in its favor. While the gameplay is solid, there is much room for improvement.

Mount and Blade: Warband and all of the its expansions and mods has brought me some of the most enjoying moments I have ever had in a videogame. From the brutal medieval battles of class Warband to the 19th century warfare that is Napoleonic Wars, the game never failed to keep me coming back to the battlegrounds for more. This is mostly due to its easy to learn, but hard to master combat system, and its various game modes, factions, classes, and maps. There are six different factions: Swadia, Nords, Sarranid Sultanate, Khergit Khanate, Rhodoks, and Vaegirs. Each faction specializes in their own respective areas. Swadia have very strong heavy cavalry, Nords specialize in having the strongest infantry with the best shields and massive two handed axes that cut through enemy shields and armor like butter. The Sarranid Sultanate is a nice blend of both cavalry and light archers, the Khergit Khanate are the only faction to be affective with horse archers which can be a nightmare to fight if they aren’t approached properly. Rhodoks are renowned for their sharp spearmen and crossbows and the Vaegirs are master archers with pinpoint accuracy even at the greatest distances. The three different classes offer many tactical options and deciding what you yourself want to specialize in along with the rest of your party can be quite thought provoking at times.
Single player is a pure joy to play through and being that it is an open world RPG sandbox that you can play around in, you will find that there is a ton of replay value here. Whether it’s the level up system that can be quite overwhelming at first, the pros and cons of the different factions, or the people you meet along the way and the relationships that you form with them, you will always find a reason to hit that “Start a new game” button and play again, but in a completely different way.
Multiplayer is also quite in depth and a very dedicated community has formed around it. You will be able to find both casual and competitive players who still play regularly. Multiplayer consists of eight different game modes: Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, Battle, Capture the Flag, Fight and Destroy, Conquest, Siege, and Duel.
-Deathmatch has you thrown into immediate chaotic action against other players in an all out brawl where it’s every man and woman for themselves. Actions happen very quickly, damage is high and health is quite low so at any moment anyone could die regardless of how skilled they are. It is a great game mode if you don’t have a lot of time to play, but just want to get in some quick instant action against players of varying skill levels.
-Team Deathmatch is very similar to Deathmatch in that you are thrown right into the thick of the action with no objective, but to kill the enemy at all costs. The difference here is that you have a team to work with and so does the enemy. Coordination is key here unless you are lucky enough to have a few players on your team that are experienced and can cleave through the enemy players.
-Battle is similar to Team Deathmatch except for the fact that in battle you only get one life per round which adds great tension to each round individually. At first having one life per round can be quite frustrating especially when you’re one of the first people to die before any of the main fighting begins, but overtime you will more than likely grow to like this one life based game mode as it makes you play more carefully and tactfully than you would in Deathmatch or Team Deathmatch.
-Capture the Flag is quite standard, it’s the same as any other Capture the Flag really. You and the enemy team each have your own flags and your goal is to retrieve their flag and bring it back to your base without letting them get yours. Short, sweet and to the point.
-Fight and Destroy has two teams put against each other, one faction will be tasked with defending valuable objectives while the other team attacks those objectives in an attempt to destroy them.
-Conquest is a real test of a team’s ability to work as a unit. In this game mode each team has to capture and hold key points on the map for a set amount of time while they fight it out with a limited number of lives.
-Siege is the ultimate test of a team’s tactical capabilities on the battlefield. This is easily the most difficult game mode when there are 60+ players on a siege server. One team plays as the defenders who attempt to hold a keep of massive proportions, while the other team plays as the attackers who raid the castle to try and capture it within a set period of time. It is easily the most brutal, bloody, nonsensical and downright gritty game mode that Mount and Blade Warband has to offer. Players of all skill levels participate in sieges and even if one team has veterans it will not guarantee them victory, because there is greater strength in numbers and coordination than one elite player going solo and killing as many people as he can. This game mode comes down to pure team work and pushing enemy fortifications in the right way as the attackers and defending those fortifications as the defenders. Often times classes play a major role in this game mode as every class has its own role to fulfill. For defense inept archers can generally mean instant spelled defeat if their infantry are not solid and. For offense having poor infantry who don’t do coordinated pushes as a group will also end up losing more than half the time. As attackers Siege has the many factors and rules that come into play with how you need to approach the enemy fortress to win and if you don’t follow said parameters then you’re going to die. . . A lot. Overall though it is still my 2nd favorite game mode and I have spent a great deal of time playing it with friends and flying solo from time to time.
-Duel is in my opinion the most personal and most in depth game mode that Mount and Blade Warband has to offer and I quite frankly find it to be the best. In duel you fight another player in a one on one fight with any weapon of your choice and any class of your choice, but typically it’s infantry with a one-handed weapon, two-handed weapon or a polearm with no shield. Whether you are dueling for honor, fun, or just to win, duel has something to offer for every player in the game. It is also the best game mode for learning about how melee combat works. At the time of this review the majority of my playtime in the game has been on duel and it still has yet to disappoint me to the point where I don’t want to play it. At a high level of play duel is the most fast paced and reaction based part of the game. The margin for error is minimal and one mistake often leads to death especially when using the two-handed Great Sword, which is the preferred weapon of choice in duel. Dueling is a progression through the game’s melee combat. You will first run around like an idiot as you try to figure out how somebody who is experienced at the game keeps killing you in a few seconds without you getting a chance to even swing, but overtime you will begin to understand exactly how the game’s mechanics work. First you will learn to recognize visual cues from your opponent and then you will learn to block. Once through that stage you will learn to feint and how to attack properly without leaving yourself completely open. Then you will learn about footwork, different feinting methods, chambering and several other aspects of the game’s melee combat and if you’re lucky you will find a mentor to help you learn it all.
At its core the game is brutal and unforgiving at the worst of times and at the best of times it can be the most rewarding game on the planet.

REVIEW
# indirect Pay-To-Win
The game uses the same PtW mechanic like WoT / WoW. You can easily level up but once you get the modifications for your gun the repair costs will kick in and you won´t make any more money to buy other guns, upgrades, modifications. All your money goes into repair / restock. The only thing that helps is a payed membership.
# False incentives
The game forces players to play tactical and go for the capture points / objectives instead of mindlessly killing the enemy. This is actually a good thing but it is badly executed. Quite often players who defend an objective on the outside perimeter do the actual work, helping teammates to capture the point. Especially players with a high K/D do the major effort to secure and hold areas, roads, paths, houses so that the team can progress. Unfortunalty these people fight and die outside the capture zone and do not get the sweet bonus which you really really need to pay for the repair costs.
This forces you to either play with an unmodded gun to save money or the buy a "veteran membership" which will grant you more bonuses (progression, money, etc...)
# Not a Strategy Game
Despite this game features a map of europe signaling players that this game is more than just fighting in staged arenas, the truth is, that so many random factors (army composition, loadout, weather, skills) which players can not control leads to a dominance of veteran players with their armies, deep pockets and the newest thing: Squad play which results in random guys fighting a pre-mate group with up to 5 (that´s what i saw, but i bet even more players are possbile) and just destroy them.
# Spawn Camping
Spawn points are more or less fix and enemy will use it to kill you the second after you spawned. Reto developed some system against it that you are invisible after start but that leads to rediclious situations where enemies spawn behind you or right in front of you.
# Cheaters
They do exist even though the people on the forum will tell you that they don´t and that it is all skill.
When people instandly turn 180° because you spawned behind them; when people shoot you half across the map, when the aim of people is switching rapidly, when the players aims at you though he can not see you, because he aimed at someone else and the field of view was so narrow, when they know you are coming through the door and have their crosshair trained on you.... after roughly 20 years of FPS gameplay i know when i see a cheater. This game makes it just harder to detect someone because of the OHK weapons.
# Camping
This is a valid tactic but gives you only kills and no objective = points. You might even help your team because you are defending or just killing enemies but the rewards for kills is too low in comparisment to capture points.
# Balance
While real war is not balanced and you might be outgunned against an enemy - in this game you can not even switch the loadout during battle so you are stuck with your rifle but you are fighting on a city map and a submaschine gun is what you need. Or you prepared for CQC but the enemy uses tanks. GG
# Shadows
A good idea poorly executed. Because of the shadows in this game you can stand 2 meters away from the enemy shooting his MG42 but you won´t the see body only the gun firing. People, cars, tanks, weapons, everything can become invisible in these shadows. It is broad daylight and you won´t see anything because of the difference between shadow and light.
I strongly do not recommend this game!!!
Like other people said in their reviews. Reto (developer / publisher) does so many unnecessary changes and tweaks to this game to make it feel like a rock hard game and then offering you a membership to ease a few of your problems.
Do not play or buy!

Bounty Train is still in early access, so bear in mind some of these things may change.
Basically this game is: you have a train, you go from stop to stop taking cargo and passengers around the United States during the Civil War while trying to complete a story quest, and in between stops you have encounters or get into fights with Indians or bandits or whatever. Your crew man different positions during the battles and each crew member has different skills and equipment that might help him.
This is *very* similar to FTL in many respects, in a good way. The view is top-down, you move the crew around, people board your train, different cars take damage and need to be repaired, etc.
So far my only gripe is that I feel like some of the time constraints on the quests need to be tweaked, since often I will accept a delivery for the next stop and the time limit runs out even if I go straight there, and also one of the bandit factions is the K K K, which is pretty stupid considering that the K K K didn't exist until after the Civil War, and this game starts in 1860. So I would like to see that changed but its not the end of the world I guess.
On top of that sometimes the game spikes in difficulty really suddenly and if you're not ready for it then you die really fast, and I feel like the money you pay to unlock each new city is maybe too high in some cases. But those are easy fixes.
Other than balancing and of course my hope for more and varied content, which any game can always use, I think this is a great game and I recommend it to anyone. Give it a try and I think you'll agree.

This game has an amazing amount of potential and I am updating this review which I originally wrote half a year ago to reflect the work the development team has put in since then. Random attacks that totally decimate the players cargo and train (which were my greatest initial complaint) have been significantly reduced. That is not to say they are gone altogether I still occasionally find myself against a bandit roadblock demanding a thousand dollars to pass and comprised of near ten bandits. It just isnt realistic to take on this many until very late in the game so expect to pay ransoms once in a while, it is infrequent enough now to be able to make up the losses. Some more variety seems to be have added in terms of items as well which is a big plus.
The combat seems to have been slightly improved after my last review, however I find the system is still often poor at matching the player with an appropriate challenge. Combat would be fine if the average attack group matched my crew of 2 or 3 men. Too often my men are outnumbered 2 or 3 to one and even when they arent finding a combatant to hire who is skilled enough to not die and consistently level up can be challenging. It does at least feel slightly easier to keep my crew alive in my recently started campaign than it did on the one I gave up on 6 months ago.
I am changing this review to positive however this development team still desperately needs to address the issues with text and culture I previously described. New text has been added since I last played which still has serious errors/flaws in it. For goodness sakes hire me I will write the dialogue from home and guarantee a far more engaging script than what is in the game currently. I understand this is early access but at some point broken english stops being acceptable. I noticed the word "slavery" misspelled multiple times  as "slavary" and that error is still there, things like that badly need fixing. Some of the offensive native caricatures have been removed it seems since I last played though I am sure I saw someone selling scalps in a town, did the designers do no historical research about the context of the content they are including?
The game also seems overpriced for how much is still missing. The designers are already selling a dlc despite not having the alpha released which seems problematic to me, i guess only time will tell if the team can follow through and deliver something truly worthwhile. Dont get me wrong, all the elements are there for this to be a truly unique and awesome game but currently the content leaves a lot to be desired and the designers badly need to hire a historical consultant/writer that is a native english speaker. I am leaving this last paragraph as is because it is in no way clear what the "titanium edition" is aside from some pre planned DLC so if there is no future content in store for having bought the special edition then I am not sure why I did. THe rest of my criticisms in this paragraph hold true, hire a bloody english speaking writer that knows a thing or two about American history and wont make such a minefield of the text. It is mysterious honestly because the subtext describing trains and such seems fine so someone totally different must be writing the problematic conversation dialogues.
I do have a few positive things to mention about the game. The methods to make money have been improved enough that it isnt just a dull "buy this good here, move it there" simulation. Events of the civil war heavily influence prices and special upgrades can be made to carriages to allow for illicit acitivties like smuggling. The missions in the city halls are actually well paying and realistic now, you can often make more money doing them than you would have buying and shipping the goods yourself. Easily addictive, I can sit for hours shooting from town to town helping ferry passangers and fuel the war effort while pursuing the main campagin goals. This is a much better game than when I first bought it though it still needs quite a bit of work before it can be called a finished game.
TL;DR if you love trains, the american civil war, or like games such as FTL or Sid Meiers : Pirates or even mount and blade there is probably something here for you. Whether you like the setting and beautiful environment or like the crew and train management system you can lose hours to this game. Keep up the hard work devs and thank you for all the improvements.

I'm writing this review becuase I feel many of the negative reviews for this game are from people who are not checking every part of the game before saying it is too hard.
First off I have near 12 hours of gameplay and other than the continue game option at the main menu maybe saving at a pretty bad point I have not seen any game breaking bugs. The game has not crashed, as long as you do not rage quit the continue option works fine for me.
Okay so if you like the idea of starting with a basic train and getting it off the ground to making big profits in many different ways then give this game a try. First off many of the reviews saying the game is too difficult to make money are just plain wrong. There are many lucrative trade routes in the starting cities if you look close enough. And if you really want to rake in lots of beginning cash take on passengers, contracts frim city hall, and bounties if you can find them. Yes you get attacked by bandits and indians a good many times but depending on what cargo you are carrying it seems to change the bandit numbers and skill level. For instance when I was carrying 20 stacks of jewelry across the map from New York to Chicago I was attacked twice by bandits that I could not outrun and thus hand to have shootouts with 22 bandits each time with decent weaponry. However this is to be expected if I am going to make upwards of $6,000 profits from this(this is a big profit margin in the game where the best train engine is around $15,000). Therefore I make sure my crew is geared with good weapons, equipment and make sure I have a healer before I do it.
Also another difficulty curve is the story mode because now you are on a time crunch which prevents you from making big runs like the one i described above. I beat it the first go around by making many more niche market runs using a much smaller engine and train. You are not able to carry tons of cargo but you can make 300-400 dollars off passengers also going to towns you are passing by and by looking for the city supply missions which pay handsomely and give you ample time so long as you can carry the cargo back in time. Also if you can get in on auctions for non production town buildings (hair cuts, hotels, etc.) you can make easy money each week that easily gives you the power to pay off bandits or you can find saloons to take jobs from the bandits, take on bandit passengers, or smuggle weapons to get on their good side and make money on the other side of the law.
The only real downside to this game I can find is that it is early access and some of the mission balances are not well done. The post office missions are completely useless and only good for if you happen to go to that town or just want to go somewhere new. The bandit and indians can be hard but making sure to arm your crew and give them the right skills means the difference between being able to take on 5 bandits or 15.
Summary: If you like trains or ground up money making games then this is a great game especially on sale for an early access. I really enjoyed the challenge of the story mode and completed it with only a few days to spare as I frantically hauled steel from the upper east coast all the way to Atlanta in my mediocre train. And the sand box mode gives you freedom to try out all the game options and train setups while fighting bandits with increasing difficulty.

Once you pop you just can't stop!
Imagine the scene, it's the week of your 27th Birthday and your friend suddenly messages you about a game thats come on Steam that you just have to try. You look it up and it's only a few Squiddly-diddlies (£1.99 to be precise) so, you proceed to purchase it along with Surgeon Simulator as an early birhtday present to yourself.
Little did I know just what to expect from Hunie Pop. Of course I had heard the rumours, the stories, the hushed voices detailing it as a sordid depraved slice of outright tittilation and general perviness. Lets get the elephant out of the room right away, this game does, indeed, contain adult imagery, that is a well-known and popular fact, but truth be told beneath the veneer of hentai lies a fun and addicting little puzzler. The story is thus: you, a guy or gal, are a total dweebo dorkmeister when it comes to women so the Goddess of Love dispatches unto thee a fairy named Kyu to coach you in becoming a desirible, eligable man/woman about town, or at the very least score with the eight lovely ladies you meet, presenting you with the objective of getting laid like a parquet floor.
Now how do we achieve that I hear you ask? Why a simple match-3 puzzle game of course! With just 20 moves you must fill your date's affection meter, but be careful, each girl has their preferred token types. For example a Girl may desire the Flirtation trait but dislike the Sexuality trait, so prioritising their favoured tokens is vital. Meanwhile  you can increase your score multiplier using the pink heart-shaped Passion tokens, earn more moves by matching the golden bell-shaped Joy tokens and gain vital Sentiment points (from blue teardrops) in order to use the Date Gifts, items which grant you aid in your date, from giving you more move to removing certain token types, but watch out for the purple Broken Hearts which basically screw up your score. With every succesful date the difficulty climbs but fret not! for success brings both money and Hunie!
Money is pretty self explanatory, this is used to purchase items for your prospective dates, from unique items which will increase the hunie gained from talking with them to little gifts which can either earn you more hunie or a date gift. This brings us to the dating sim side of the game. To progress with each girl you must talk to them, learn about them. This will not only fill in their profiles but, used in conjunction with the unique gifts, will bring in the all-important Hunie. Hunie is basically EXP, use it to increase the stats relating to the match-3 gameplay, for example one stat reduces affection lost by purple hearts whilst one increases your Passion multiplier. Whilst it's largely irrelevant which stats you prioritise out of the four main token types it's a good idea to reduce the damage of those purples but the difficulty curve is fairly easy so you should be able to handle your way through the first eight girls, complete four dates and you claim a trophy of your conquest and, once all eight are obtained you get the fun of the unlockable girls. I won't spoil them but the final boss (of sorts) is actually sort of underwhelming compared to characters you have already dated. Once you have successfully become the universe's greatest lover (no joke) you then unlock what is basically a survival mode with ever increasing difficulty that raises regardeless of success or failure on a date.
So what else can be said about Hunie Pop... well, as with the DoA Volleyball games theres a solid, workable match-3 game here that can prove quite addictive, the characters are your stock characters from most dating sims but a few do come across as quite charming and grounded in reality despite being somewhat cookie-cutter, also whilst it's only really mentioned in the manual, it would've been nice to have the voice actresses at least attempt the accents of the characters (Audrey, the stuck up ♥♥♥♥♥y valley girl soundlike is actually meant to be french... i mean i suppose I'm glad it's not 'Allo, Allo' levels of accent work but at least try!) but it doesn't marr the gameplay, more just my own personal niggliness. The artwork is nice (yes, even the smut... now kindly stop dribbling so we can get away from that please!) and it basically does what its reputation has established. If you want to play it for the smut then do so by all means but there is a fun little puzzler/dating game here, admittedly the strategy of using the Date Gifts does go out the window once you find the correct ones which almost guarantee success but the RGN gods aren't always kind so don't think you can't get screwed over in later Dates. Whilst it is possible to make dates easier with alcohol and food it is ultimately a waste of your money so save it for the gifts which can earn you the precious Date Gifts.
To summarise Hunie Pop definitely has a well-earned reputation for being hentai smut with a game stapled onto it, that is undeniable, but it's also a very enjoyable, nay addicting, puzzler. The characters, whilst fitting into your dating sim stereotypes, vary from eye-rollingly sledgehammer-subtle Trope fillers with the personality of a deck chair like the MILF and the ♥♥♥♥♥-queen to somewhat believable, albeit within this campy set-up, but believable nonetheless to the point I actually hated screwing up the Dates because of their dissapointment, i mean how many games actually try to make you feel bad for failing? In short it's a fun game, definitely a wee bit dodgy, i mean theres no way in hell you'd admit to your dear sweet old granny that you own it, but it honestly is worth a play, it is smut but theres more to it and I honestly think that, if you can get past the flagrant tittilation then you can enjoy it. It isn't for everyone but if you just want to se what the fuss is about I'd give it a go, just wait for it to be on sale, it's really not worht the full pricetag.
