Modern Warfare Remastered is a remastered edition of Call of Duty 4. It includes a stellar single-player campaign which makes you feel the struggles of modern war and witness the devastation that is possible nowadays. The single-player has had nothing changed apart from graphics and is completely worth playing.
The multiplayer on the other hand has been remastered like the single-player but with quite a number of additions, microtransactions being the big one. They aren't that bad apart from the fact that the guns that have been added to the game post-release are heavily locked behind the microtransactions. The guns are almost reskins of already existing ones in the game but tend to have very small stat differences. It is in no way pay to win. A huge majority of the items are simply cosmetic such as different characters, uniforms, player cards and weapon skins. You don't have to spend any money to obtain any of this due to the in-game currency earned by playing but it is very hard to obtain the guns specifically through this method.
Another huge complaint is that the only DLC from the original game (4 new maps released for around $10 back then) has been remastered and sold as DLC for the remaster for around $15. In my personal opinion and many, many other's, these maps should've been free with the remaster.
The developers have had 2 events occur in the game so far where some maps have been changed to fit the event and new cosmetic items and new modes have been added. I think this is a great way to keep players interested and add some variety to the game. The problem is due to having this remaster locked behind a purchase of the special edition of Infinite Warfare, the playerbase is really dwindling. The majority of gamemodes on PC are simply unplayable due to nobody queuing for them. The standalone version is going to be released soon but I doubt it will make much of a difference.
All in all the multiplayer is very fun and the cosmetics that have been added do add some variety to the game.
My recommendation is to buy this game if you played the original and wish to experience it if it came out recently as it is a fantastic remaster. Players new to the CoD series will probably struggle to get into the multiplayer as it is quiet on PC and the players are mostly hardcore fans of the series but it is definitely worth a try as the multiplayer is some of the best there is.

NOTE TO READER - I have spent more time playing the Single player rather than the multiplayer so i cannot account of all of online, especially in recent patches but I do have a general idea as to the feeling of the multiplayer.
Putting Aside Activision's controversial decision to only release this title up until recently only as part of a Deluxe edition of Infinite Warfare and it's subsequent DLC and microtransactions. (Which can be a pretty big ask)
Call of duty Modern Warfare Remastered is a mixed bag to say the least. While I can list only a number of Pros and cons, it depends on how much of a COD fan you really are and what level of dedication you are willing to put into this game to continue to play.
The Pros
The Graphics - The updated graphics engine definetly gives COD 4 a boost in the eye candy department as each level is given a breath of fresh air resulting in grizzled veterens of the older game reliving that sense of wonder and awe as they pass through new yet familar level sections. Guns and gadgets also get their own buff in the beauty department, even the weapons dropped on the ground or in the background look gorgous.
The Sound - More memory and better quality audio recording capabilites means that the whole sound effects for the game have been completely revamped. Most guns now have a more meaty sounds in firing, reloading or even when the player selects a different tool. Firefights sound more intense and the crack and whip of bullet impacts and shouting by both friend and enemy combatents gives a higher level of immersion to the experience of which i personally enjoyed a fair amount.
Gun and gadgets - Working in conjuction with the new sound effects, the animations breaths a new lease of life to familar weapons and gadgets. The guns have new and unique reload and firing animations and the gadgets also have new and unique animations however as a slight con, some reloads and activation of gadgets take slightly longer than their old game counterparts so the player is forced to learn when to time using certain abilites in order to not get himself killed by mistake.
Options - While there arent as many options That I would like, COD 4 Remastered does thankfully have enough options to allow a decent level of grapical customization so those who may not have the best of PCs can still run the game at their own pace.
The Cons
AI - The has not really been any sort of improvment made to the AI both ally and enemy. Friends will blindly run into certain death or live Nades about to explode. Enemies will either all focus you or completely ignore you just because you have a glass window in the way (Yes that happend) Even the Invicible AI characters will often show just how invicible they are by taking multiple shots and RPGs when they blunder out into the open after the player goes through a section in the level.
Multiplayer - This isnt really a con but in order to save on space and time reading I'll quickly sum up what I encountered in my limited time playing MP.  The Multiplayer while enjoyable and nostalgic at first, you are then quickly reminded of the issues and annoyances that plauged the original COD 4 MP. Perks like Juggernaut or Stopping power are just as overpowered and annoying to deal with as they used to be.
For a well known and historically dealt with issue, you'd think they would do the same balancing here as they had done on Modern Warfare 2. The Weapons have the same issue, Pin point accuracy M16A4s and Autoshotguns shred through most players before they even have a chance to react. Turning any potentially fun and enjoyable game in MP into a boring score counting game before the end credits.
To round off Multiplayer. I was playing MP during the period that COD 4 remaster was only available as part of a bundle with Infinte Warfare and as such, there werent many players on Roughly 4-5K. But those that were online, they mainly wanted to play just 3 game types, Team Deathmatch, Search and Destroy and maybe Free for all. While there were occasionally playing other game modes, either the teams were so few in numbers that they couldnt even get the match launched. Or they had empty maps with barely anyone about.
BS moments - BS or Bullsh$t moments are when the game clearly screws the player over or something odd which results in either your death or some funny incident occuring. For COD 4 remastered, 95% of the BS moments was the game doing everything in its power to screw me over. Enemy AI walking right past my comrades to shoot me from behind and point blank, or Sections of the map blocking my character's movement resulting in me either dying or taking unnecessary damage.
These a but a couple of BS moments that will hit you and hit you often while playing through the single player campaign. One incident that set me livid was during the escape from Chernobyl mission at the point where you defend the ferris wheel. Having set up multiple Claymores on the right in order to prevent the enemy from sneaking up to me while i was sniping, I found out to my instant being angered that not only did the claymores fail to kill their intended targets, but also served to hide the enemy long enough for them to fire a small burst which on hardened is enough to kill you.
This to me was the last straw as having tried numourous tactics and methods to improve my odds of survival let alone achieving my objective. From setting up claymores right at the enemy spawn, running around the area constantly, hiding in one of the ride stalls, etc. All of which failed not due to my own failings or lack of awareness but simply due to the AI and game just spamming everything at me and completely ignoring my one allied Sniper who was out and in the open the entire time.
This along with most of the campaign having these moments served only to get me to uninstall the game from my PC. While I am a fan of the older cod games and cod 4, my level of deication towards the series is no where near enough to calmly deal with the poor AI and downright cheating the game will do in order to artifically scale the difficulty in the campaign.
Summery - While COD 4 Remastered's faults as well as activision's DLC and Micro-transaction controversies are too much for me to enjoy the game anymore I cannot deny for any fan of the COD series who are willing ignore such things can easily find the old jem that brought Call of duty from a semi popular WW2 action game to the height of the mainstream first person shooters.
However like I said at the beginning of this review, The amount of enjoyment you will have of this game is dependant on the player. If you want a COD 4 with shiny graphics then you're good. If you want a COD 4 which can not only fill you with nostalgia but give you up to date balancing and quality to last hours and hours. Then you may want to give this a miss and just play the old COD 4 as that still has a strong player base and modding community.
Thank you for reading this fairly long review.

Recently, I subscribed to a month of WoW because my friend was playing and I thought - what the hell?  It's been awhile.  Also, I looked forward to playing a highly cooperative game with my friend. Even after all the challenger MMOs that have tried to one-up it.  Obviously, since I plan on deleting the game, my experience wasn't ideal.  Mainly, I was just bored.
I prefer to play DC Universe over WoW.  DCU is well-paced and immersive.  The combat is above average for MMOs and it seems to take skill to get good at your "power-type" (ice/fire etc).  The combat involves combo attacks which made fighting a lot more interesting to me.
You still get your typical "Kill X amount of X/Collect X amount of X" just like any other MMO but the game disguises it well in my experience and it doesn't get repetitive as fast as it does in other MMOs.  I have played one dungeon as of yet and it also seemed less repetitive then your typical MMO.  The dungeon still had a linear basis but unlike WoW you run (I fly) around a certain area and kill things rather then literally folow a linear path which I thought was a nice touch.
By far the one of the best things about DCU is the character creation.  The creators of this game did not hold back as far as aesthetic possibilities for your hero or villain go.  I consider myself a creative person and I had a blast making my hero.  (A gadget-wielding, flying zombie with a gas mask, tech wings, gangster hood and jacket, tech legs and boots with high socks who happens to answers to Batman.) I'll make this review easy and un-time consuming for you.
+The game definately has many connections not just to DC Comics but also to the Injustice series. In case the intro sequence didn't tip that one off.
+Combat is nice and easy to use and often satisfying if your not sticking to one class or weapon type.
+You can actually make a character out of inspiration from certain DC characters. Maybe not all of them but I guess that's to be expected for such a HUGE universe of characters.
+It's definately not as cheesy as Champions Online.
+They let you choose your means of travel right off the bat. You either get to have the Batmans acrobatics, Supermans fleight or Flash's super speed. These means of travels trump others in some way though so think before choosing.
-They don't give you much of an ability to customize your characters in-depth features. So your basically a clone.
-The more awesome powers are locked behind a paywall. I guess they do require money to keep the game going but this is a bit a low blow since I think I can speak for many when I say that the most interesting character you can think of may need power types like these to make sense. Some of the vanilla powers are kinda bland in some way so I can see what they're doing here.
-Honestly I'm not sure how choosing a mentor affects you. They don't exactly make it obvious.
Over all it's a pretty good game. Maybe a bit lacking in certain things and a little money hungry but hey. You can't build a decent experience with a stick and a few rocks.

I saw this months ago and I thought meh what's the point of using this if you have mouse and keyboard? Like honestly it doesn't make too much sense to me but now months later I thought hell why not give it a shot and guess what IT MAKES SO MUCH SENSE... straight up this is the best thing you can buy for your controller literally not even kidding!
Man so much features it blows my mind that a controller can even do all this, so first off like me I wanted to know this and I can confirm that you can turn off steamworks integration meaning it won't record your hours on the app... plus one for doing that, I hate absolutely hate apps recording hours... personally I think software needs its own section, its own tab on steam in the profile section! With that said let's move on everything is rebindable to whatever you want there's not only primary functions there's also secondary so e.g x button could be task switcher but back button + x can be start menu. YOU CAN FINALLY TURN OFF A WIRELESS CONTROLLER WITH THIS APP JESUS I'VE BEEN WAITING A MILLION YEARS FOR SOMETHING LIKE THAT! I hated pulling out the battery pack just for it to turn off. This app also turns off when playing a game so it doesn't interfere with whatever is going on but if you still wanna use it in game? Simple you can just turn it back on. Browsing with it on the desktop is sooooo smooth like I feel super lazy now its great and being able to turn up the sensitivity for the mouse pointer is good stuff. You can also set a bunch of profiles with custom rebinds for whatever you want!
I don't have much bad things to say like the typing is meh I rather just use a keyboard, to be fair though it works well for typing simple things though like cat or dog! The app also shows itself as recently played with 0.0 hours on startup which is fine but I'd rather it not show up at all considering the points I made earlier but that's it for the bad!
Seriously though if you thought about this like I did do yourself a favor and just buy the damn thing it's better than it seems and it's always I mean ALWAYS good to have another alternative just in case but for real this app transforms your mostly useless controller to something super handy... totally worth a buy at this price!
